issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the scheduled UI E2E failure in `Gateway connect denial > paces unavailable handshakes at a reachable Gateway`, where only two handshakes were observed instead of more than three.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. The shared mock Gateway now sends protocol-valid challenge timestamps when Playwright advances fractional-delay timers.

## Why This Change Was Made

Playwright can expose fractional `Date.now()` values inside virtual timer callbacks. The mock sent these directly as `connect.challenge.ts`, which the real protocol client correctly rejects because timestamps must be integers. Truncate the timestamp at the fixture producer and retain the existing pacing and recovery assertions.

## Evidence

- Scheduled failure: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42844215728/job/129927629436
- A minimal Playwright clock probe confirms fractional timestamps. Injecting that condition after the second handshake reproduces the exact `expected 2 to be greater than 3` failure on base and passes with this fix. Diagnostic injection is excluded from the patch.
- New fixture regression fails on base and passes with the fix; all 20 mock-Gateway tests pass.
- Both original Gateway connect-denial E2E cases pass unchanged using Chromium headless shell.
- UI E2E test typecheck (tsrs), focused lint, formatting, diff and test-line ratchet checks pass. The allocation accounts for 13 added regression/helper lines and 18 inherited base lines, leaving zero spare headroom.
- Independent full-context autoreview against `ecbad2efa1d7`: scoped-clean for P0–P3; no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper source runners are not built; the hosted ClawSweeper review has acknowledged the ready PR.

The patch changes no production code and adds one focused fixture regression (20-test file: 0.876 s total locally, 0.31 s test time; original browser file: 3.637 s test time). CI timing will be recorded when available. No sleeps, timeout increases, weakened assertions, or dependency changes.

## CI outcome and landing qualification

Exact-head CI [42860312499](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42860312499) passed the original E2E shard 4/7 and all UI unit shards. Shard 3/7 failed in the setup hook for `gateway-fresh-visit.http.e2e.test.ts` (`Fresh browser at the production Gateway HTTP boundary`): 180-second hook timeout, all three cases skipped; its other 622 cases passed. All three real-HTTP cases pass in focused local replay with the unchanged timeout (71.52 seconds total).

The classification table calls that failure new because the matching main job passed, without comparing scope. Source inspection qualifies it as unrelated: this suite starts the real HTTP Gateway and never installs the mock WebSocket changed here; its setup, HTTP harness and test-state sources are unchanged. The shared helper's production-build functions are unchanged. The exact slow setup stage remains unidentified, and this PR does not claim to fix that timeout or make CI green. Landing uses the authorized inherited-failure route with retained exact-merge, source and failed-job evidence.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Managed worktree provisioning combines worker delivery, authority assertions, and filesystem copy waits in one interval, preventing useful attribution of a slow preparation.

Related: #191873, #192548, #193056. Adjacent fs-safe work remains owned by openclaw/fs-safe#1055; this PR does not duplicate it or change the dependency.

## User Impact

Diagnostics only: file selection, copy strategy, concurrency, timeouts, authority checks, cancellation and errors retain their existing behavior. This is not a latency fix or a claim about the cause of a reported stall.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing private terminal worker receipt with fixed numeric aggregates, projected into the existing preparation log/event: host roundtrip, worker elapsed, root/eligibility preflight, authority wait, inclusive `Root.copyIn` await, an explicitly approximate roundtrip residual, attempted/accepted file counts and logical source sizes.

Copy awaits include Root admission, native queueing, filesystem work and nested authority assertions; they are not native copy time and overlap authority wait. Existing lstats supply logical sizes without extra IO. Failed receipts retain partial timings; cancellation or worker loss without a delivered receipt retains only host roundtrip. No paths, contents, per-file events, config, public API or new log family.

## Evidence

- Current head: `3a2f5a9f22ca9d05c4d491db6deaff93430dc349`. [Normal PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41963169836) completed **SUCCESS: 33 successful / 29 skipped / zero failed jobs**. Both reported required `openclaw/ci-gate` entries are **SUCCESS**; the full check list has no failures or pending items. No gate waiver or unchanged-check rerun.
- This CI run is bound to the exact head and tests GitHub merge preview `2ae3ab5b9f7dfcaaf1ded0ac2e4de42ddf2d415e`, whose parents are main `4a43644e7a7b455d6e257f1ab62fe00e74156a5f` and this head. Actual checkout/revision and parent identities are verified. No lane rebase/main merge was performed.
- Current PR test runtime selection is `bun-all`: named Bun results are copy **5/5**, copy-host **4/4**, preparation timing **3/3**, real service **16/16**; production/test types pass. [Earlier direct-head proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41948540409) at `7659c9d8c` covers those owner cases under Node and Bun plus build-artifacts. Production files are unchanged by the final test-only repair.
- The first normal PR run exposed an OWN closed-mock export defect in single-file Bun cleanup. The final commit preserves real singleton exports while retaining the existing fixture override; all four formerly failing host outcomes now pass. Fresh independent Codex P0–P2 autoreview is **scoped-clean**, no findings. Normal hooks passed without bypass/bootstrap. Net PR test LF growth is **0**, with no assertions or cases removed.
- **Base-red verified under Node and Bun:** [baseline job 127000792450](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41952674246/job/127000792450) checks out `c0d0d4d550d88f9cdf4b631b55e863293d984cb3`, exactly the merge base plus the same service regression test. `service.provisioned.test.ts:184` fails on absent `copy.workerMs`, `copy.authorityWaitMs`, and `copy.sourceBytes: 41`; returned outcome and existing preparation phases match. It is the sole failing case in each runtime invocation, with the other 15 service cases passing. The service test is unchanged by the final fixture repair. The throwaway remote branch was deleted and independently verified absent.
- Darwin-only filesystem-native siblings have 9 skips per runtime in the Linux proof, not native/APFS qualification. No live Gateway run, deployment, production latency root-cause or fix claim.
- Ready for **lead landing review** under explicit maintainer direction. No merge or auto-merge action was performed by this lane.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Managed worktrees with large `.worktreeinclude` dependency trees spend seconds repeatedly asking Git which selected files are ignored. The capacity-estimation pass also falls outside the preparation phases, obscuring that cost.

Related: #196768, #150532.

## User Impact

Included-file selection uses two Git processes regardless of selected file count. The existing preparation record now attributes pre-checkout discovery and sizing to `provisionEstimate`. No configuration, storage schema, or copy-policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Filter the manifest-selected NUL-delimited inventory with `git check-ignore --no-index --stdin -z`, replacing one `ls-files` invocation per 128 paths. Prefixing inputs with `./` preserves literal colon-leading filenames because `check-ignore` rejects pathspec magic and `--literal-pathspecs`. The initial inventory already contains only untracked paths, so `--no-index` prevents tracked wildcard lookalikes from suppressing literal ignored filenames. Selection stays bounded by the manifest, retaining #150532's protection against unrelated ignored trees.

Copy-time discovery remains fresh after source custody is reacquired. Capacity parent/file checks, copy-time descriptor validation, cancellation and live authority remain intact. Linux provisioning already requests reflinks with `cp --reflink=auto`; this change does not claim faster copying or remove a guard. Production LOC delta: **0** (inspection −3, timing +3).

## Evidence

Acceptance set before measurements: preserve exact paths/size estimates; remove per-batch Git processes; lower median/p95 owner wall time with no >20% CPU/allocation regression. Native owner/Git/filesystem fixture: **65,880 selected files, 2,195,978,040 bytes**, using the earlier dependency layout. Two A/A controls and five interleaved A/B pairs per mode, fresh process per sample, warm filesystem, natural GC. Linux Node 24.22.1, 4 vCPU/15 GiB runner, ext4. Kernel btrfs was unavailable; no btrfs or full-Gateway latency claim.

| Owner mode | Wall median / p95, before → after | CPU median, before → after | Sampled V8 allocation median, before → after | Git processes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Copy-time selection | 2.557 / 2.907 s → 0.437 / 0.517 s | 3.168 → 0.579 s | 264.9 → 100.1 MB | 516 → 2 |
| Capacity selection + sizing | 6.215 / 6.383 s → 4.136 / 4.349 s | 7.509 → 4.962 s | 1,616.5 → 1,447.9 MB | 516 → 2 |

A/A wall controls: selection 2.923/2.632 s; estimate 5.883/6.511 s. Five-sample p95 is the observed maximum, not a production tail estimate. CPU includes child processes; allocation is sampled including collected objects. Profiles from the initial candidate remove the repeated `spawn` hotspot; the table reruns the final `--no-index` implementation; estimate time still includes the unchanged `lstat` walk. Every run verifies all selected paths and the exact capacity total.

Reproduce with `scripts/perf/worktree-provisioning-inspection-measure.ts`: seed `--root <scratch> --seed`, then alternate baseline `--base-file <original-runtime.ts>` and candidate, with and without `--estimate`; `--profile <prefix>` writes CPU/allocation profiles. Baseline: `9b7dcdc7a66dc1bbcb0767b8109e798eb826954e`.

- Both updated regressions fail on base: missing `provisionEstimate` and 4 selection processes instead of 2 on the literal-path fixture.
- 24 focused tests pass on macOS: real service creation/removal/restore, bounded output, literal UTF-8/wildcard/magic/newline names, timing, cancellation and publication receipts.
- ClawSweeper’s tracked-wildcard finding is covered by a regression that fails on the first PR head and passes with `--no-index`; tracked lookalikes remain excluded.
- Fresh Codex autoreview of the corrected complete local diff, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no findings.
- The two changed real-service regressions also pass on Linux (18.39 s tests, 70.22 s including worker compilation); macOS focused test wall was 87.14 s including worker compilation and two shards.
- `pnpm check:changed` completed: formatting, lint, typechecks and all other selected guards pass; the dead-export scan reports unrelated baseline symbols (including newly exported knowledge helpers from #196767). Exact-parent reproduction matches byte-for-byte: 56 production and 30 full-tree dead exports, script scan clean. The 23 knowledge production findings were introduced by #196767; other inherited facade/helper findings are being handed back to their owners. The added script has no unused-file finding; the aggregate unused-file scan reproduces the same three main failures on the exact parent, introduced by #196685 and #196501. These are recorded main regressions, not passing aggregate checks.
- Production confirmation belongs to the next deployment's existing preparation record; no live service was changed.

First-head CI run `42912218220` exposed two main regressions introduced by #196206 (`97e91a16d636c`): stale non-managed GitHub spawn expectation and unauthenticated default-base fetching after an authenticated clone. Both reproduce through the canonical test wrapper on the exact original parent `9b7dcdc7a66dc`: spawn line 307 lacks the old failed status, clone-identity line 176 observes a request without the selected authorization. Existing repairs #196271 and #196889 own these failures; this PR does not duplicate them. Final-head CI is tracked separately.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory diagnostics repeatedly traverse the resident session-row graph on every memory heartbeat, allocating megabytes while measuring memory.

## User Impact

Projection byte and truncation estimates refresh immediately and then at most once every five minutes. Row counts still refresh on every memory heartbeat, and disposal removes all contributions immediately. The diagnostic documentation now explains that byte estimates retain their last sampled value between refreshes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resident-row inventory differs from the serialized view cache, so its existing byte accounting cannot replace this estimate. Throttle the existing owner-held estimate without adding a timer, configuration option, schema, or another cache. Production grows by five lines for the sampling deadline and conditional update.

## Evidence

Acceptance: through the real materialized projection and diagnostic dispatcher, preserve row counts, estimate refresh, and disposal; reduce aggregate heartbeat CPU and allocation by at least 80%, with no heartbeat tail regression. The fixture contains 5,000 synthetic resident sessions and 100 heartbeats spaced by a simulated monotonic 30 seconds. Setup, database hydration, forced GC, and disposal are outside the measured heartbeat totals. It does not model whole-Gateway throughput or a production database/workspace.

Five serial alternating baseline/candidate timing pairs, Node 26.12.1:

| Per 100 heartbeats | Baseline median | Candidate median | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU | 244.505 ms | 30.238 ms | −87.63% |
| Wall time | 246.293 ms | 31.708 ms | −87.13% |
| Sampled allocation, separate five-pair run | 581.868 MB | 61.323 MB | −89.46% |

Identical-source A/A CPU totals were 231.831 and 226.759 ms (2.19% difference). Allocation A/A totals were 580.515 and 585.381 MB (0.84%). Callback wall p95 fell from 2.830 to 2.497 ms, and worst observed callback from 4.054 to 3.876 ms. Separate CPU profiles recorded 161 → 17 estimator self samples. Five-pair CPU ranges were 242.358–258.012 → 29.839–30.473 ms, wall 244.044–259.762 → 31.166–31.919 ms, and allocation 581.369–584.135 → 58.910–62.131 MB. All 26 formal runs preserved the inventory and disposed to zero; instrumented timings are excluded.

Reproduce using `scripts/perf/session-row-projection-retention.ts --sessions 5000 --diagnostics --diagnostic-heartbeats 100 --output <result.json>` with Node `--expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs`. For comparison, use its existing baseline overlay loader, `--import ./scripts/perf/worker-retained-heap-preload.ts`, with `OPENCLAW_BENCH_BASELINE_DIR` containing the baseline retention owner; use an empty overlay for the candidate. Add `--allocation` or `--cpu-profile` separately.

The existing real-projection lifecycle regression fails on the unchanged parent at the new between-samples estimate assertion and passes with this change. The estimator's three tests also pass. The seven-line regression extension has a dedicated test-cost allocation record.

Codex autoreview of the complete local diff against `a2879ad0a140654acae1f807db4021fec6b5017d` is scoped-clean through P2. Changed-file checks completed. The one new benchmark lint finding was repaired; final targeted lint, formatting and script typecheck pass. The only outstanding local failure is the identical exact-parent dead-export signature (33 production / 9 full-tree / 0 scripts), with no changed file among the findings. Exact-head [CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42908882035) for `6d5d97f55cbb79ce5168a7c303543fea059a774f`. Hosted Codex review has no findings; [ClawSweeper final-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196881#issuecomment-6780585582) has zero findings and no before-merge requirements. No browser-runtime imports changed. Production allocation acceptance remains a later deployment/profile comparison.

<details>
<summary>Inherited dead-export attribution</summary>

The failed scan reproduces with resolved workspace dependencies on exact parent `a2879ad0a140654acae1f807db4021fec6b5017d`; normalized finding sets match exactly. Causal owner commits: #196207 (`c7152f3bda8e5`), #192552 (`625945b7ae01d`), #196252 (`80ba593b8b14b`), #191326 (`56617cd000864`), #190205 (`f63e5cd0f6d38`), #132716 (`964fa991c0aff`), #139911 (`071f606eae77a`), #129184 (`33d8f24c9926f`), `a7436c8b4a93bff59d099661d2b206bb0627ac2b`, #190544 (`cf1ae7bb6a729`), #196380 (`37a3b162a0c58`), and #196724 (`2c4e34a72f490`). The newest main regression is `projectLeaseDiagnosticFrames` from #196724: the exported helper has only a same-module production caller and external test callers. It is an outstanding main failure, not a passing check.

</details>

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

Sandbox reuse can spend minutes reconciling a managed workspace, while diagnostics expose only the total wait.

Related: #196835.

## User Impact

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: shared blobless project clones accumulate ordinary packs when publication hydrates content, checkout preparation fetches a pinned commit by URL, or an agent fetches from a secondary repository. These packs make later partial-clone maintenance unnecessarily expensive.

Related: #196784. The separate scripts/pr fix landed in #193670.

## User Impact

Managed partial clones retain promisor packs across these fetch paths. Agent fetches and pulls in shared blobless clones register Git's standard promisor/filter settings for configured and literal remotes, preserving later reads of peer-only blobs. An explicit `--no-filter` fetch is refused there; standalone repositories and projections retain their existing choices. No new OpenClaw configuration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Literal URLs do not automatically inherit `origin`'s filter. Publication content hydration also selected `--refetch --stdin` instead of retaining `--filter=blob:none`. Both owners now retain filtering. Pinned-commit acquisition reuses the existing project filter reader after its present-commit fast return.

The agent wrapper lets native Git select named remotes, groups and all/multiple fetches; Git rejects a top-level filter option for multi-remote fetches. Durable Git promisor registration is necessary for subsequent peer-only blob hydration. Relative fetch URLs are anchored using Git’s native transport cwd and URL-rewrite resolution, so other linked worktrees can use those promises; distinct additional URLs and push URLs are preserved. The existing config read supplies an invocation-local snapshot, so correctly configured remotes incur no config writes. One argument scan replaces the previous three scans.

## Evidence

Native regression tests fail on the original owners with an ordinary pack missing its `.promisor` marker. All 85 tests across the four affected files pass, including installed exec → native Git, remote groups, `--all`, `--multiple`, URL/path operands, upload-pack option values, pulls, subsequent peer-only content reads, and standalone behavior. Hosted review caught two additional regressions before landing: cross-worktree hydration through relative peers, and missing trees revealing previously unknown blobs. Both now have failing-before/passing-after native proof. Publication hydration needs at most two filtered batches when trees are absent; blob-only hydration retains identical Git argv and pack bytes.

On a synthetic fixture with 13,006 refs and 1,054 packs, pinned-commit acquisition falls from 9 objects / 3,147,341 bytes to 6 commits-and-trees / 623 bytes. Median wall time falls 358→254 ms and native CPU 310→170 ms. The additional config command raises JS CPU 11.27→15.33 ms and sampled allocation 1.08→1.52 MB; already-present commits still use one offline command and no config read or fetch.

Publication hydration transfers the identical requested blobs and pack bytes before/after, now with the promisor marker. Five paired trials and A/A controls show no demonstrated speedup: median wall 392→408 ms, JS allocation +0.9%, with host-tail contention.

The corrected small local explicit-fetch fixture measures 6→9 Git processes and 46.78→47.97 ms child CPU; wall medians 69.77→103.98 ms, with A/A 68.69 ms. This is added fetch-policy overhead on macOS, not a production Linux latency claim. Subsequent correctly configured fetches make zero config writes. A separate qualified Linux Git allocator interposer reports 2,374→3,586 allocation requests and 5,248,735→5,530,696 cumulative requested bytes per explicit fetch; all five A/B/A2 samples match exactly, with A2 identical to A. These counts exclude shell/Python, mmap and hidden libc allocations and do not measure retained memory. The already-present content path still returns before fetch policy and remains two Git processes with no network or pack changes; its earlier path-specific A/B/A2 control was within noise.

The exact base-root `git diff --quiet <a> <b> -- <path>` with two missing commits was separately verified through exec → Python bare `git`: 36 objects without the wrapper, 6 with it, all promisor; changed and unchanged paths retain native exit codes. The already-merged revision preparation needs no further diff change.

Production growth is 104 lines; tests grow 102 lines with an exact scoped allocation. The growth covers shared native fetch selection, usable promisor registration, and one reused project filter reader; there is no new cache or transport staging layer. The separate `scripts/pr` authoritative-fetch correction is merged in #193670.

Fresh independent Codex autoreview through P3 is scoped-clean after both hosted-review corrections. The corrected `pnpm check:changed` run completed: types, formatting and the other guards pass. It caught a test-only no-shadow error, which was corrected and passed targeted lint/format checks. The remaining repository-wide dead-export scan fails on 33 production / 9 full-tree entries. The canonical checker reproduces identical entries on exact parent `2a41138`, with no module-resolution errors; the causal attribution reuses prior lane evidence, with the new diagnostics export identified below. The test-line guard reproduces the same 128-line deficit on exact parent `2a41138ac9d467e12b33d8981cafe7d13ad6d019` (6,635,428 lines / 6,635,300 ceiling); this PR adds exactly 102 lines and 102 allocation. That deficit was introduced by #196346 (`b91520c`), not this change. The newly detected unused `projectLeaseDiagnosticFrames` export originates in `2c4e34a72f490c710bc155319fcabf872f482b3e` and is a main regression requiring separate repair. No live shared clone was modified for this proof, and the historical observed packs cannot be assigned to a particular caller from the available logs.

## What Problem This Solves

Sandbox preparation rewalks unchanged skill trees after more than 100 other destinations evict their usage records.

## User Impact

Docker and Podman sandboxes retain unchanged skill-copy reuse across large preparation bursts. Source revisions still reconcile the copies. No new configuration options are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing generated manifest now retains the source generation and identity-to-destination facts that previously disappeared with the bounded usage cache. The destination map also owns the identity set, removing duplicated persisted `entryKeys`. Non-local skills retain their identities with null destinations. Discovery still constructs every path; only an exact match to a discovered destination can authorize preservation.

Disk-based reuse is enabled only for Docker/Podman read-only skill mounts. Remote and unknown targets retain reconciliation after eviction because remote mirrors can return guest-written metadata. Their warm cache continues to use producer-owned facts. Legacy manifests reconcile normally; malformed selected mappings cannot authorize reuse. The warm-only defensive clone is removed because cold results already share the same entries and consumers read or remap them.

Production code grows by **17 net lines** across two files to retain and validate the existing manifest facts and preserve the backend trust boundary. There is no new cache, store, SQLite schema, engine queue, or shared writable tree.

## Evidence

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: shared blobless project clones accumulate ordinary packs when publication hydrates content, checkout preparation fetches a pinned commit by URL, or an agent fetches from a secondary repository. These packs make later partial-clone maintenance unnecessarily expensive.

Related: #196784. The separate scripts/pr fix landed in #193670.

## User Impact

Managed partial clones retain promisor packs across these fetch paths. Agent fetches and pulls in shared blobless clones register Git's standard promisor/filter settings for configured and literal remotes, preserving later reads of peer-only blobs. An explicit `--no-filter` fetch is refused there; standalone repositories and projections retain their existing choices. No new OpenClaw configuration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Literal URLs do not automatically inherit `origin`'s filter. Publication content hydration also selected `--refetch --stdin` instead of retaining `--filter=blob:none`. Both owners now retain filtering. Pinned-commit acquisition reuses the existing project filter reader after its present-commit fast return.

The agent wrapper lets native Git select named remotes, groups and all/multiple fetches; Git rejects a top-level filter option for multi-remote fetches. Durable Git promisor registration is necessary for subsequent peer-only blob hydration. Relative fetch URLs are anchored using Git’s native transport cwd and URL-rewrite resolution, so other linked worktrees can use those promises; distinct additional URLs and push URLs are preserved. The existing config read supplies an invocation-local snapshot, so correctly configured remotes incur no config writes. One argument scan replaces the previous three scans.

## Evidence

Native regression tests fail on the original owners with an ordinary pack missing its `.promisor` marker. All 85 tests across the four affected files pass, including installed exec → native Git, remote groups, `--all`, `--multiple`, URL/path operands, upload-pack option values, pulls, subsequent peer-only content reads, and standalone behavior. Hosted review caught two additional regressions before landing: cross-worktree hydration through relative peers, and missing trees revealing previously unknown blobs. Both now have failing-before/passing-after native proof. Publication hydration needs at most two filtered batches when trees are absent; blob-only hydration retains identical Git argv and pack bytes.

On a synthetic fixture with 13,006 refs and 1,054 packs, pinned-commit acquisition falls from 9 objects / 3,147,341 bytes to 6 commits-and-trees / 623 bytes. Median wall time falls 358→254 ms and native CPU 310→170 ms. The additional config command raises JS CPU 11.27→15.33 ms and sampled allocation 1.08→1.52 MB; already-present commits still use one offline command and no config read or fetch.

Publication hydration transfers the identical requested blobs and pack bytes before/after, now with the promisor marker. Five paired trials and A/A controls show no demonstrated speedup: median wall 392→408 ms, JS allocation +0.9%, with host-tail contention.

The corrected small local explicit-fetch fixture measures 6→9 Git processes and 46.78→47.97 ms child CPU; wall medians 69.77→103.98 ms, with A/A 68.69 ms. This is added fetch-policy overhead on macOS, not a production Linux latency claim. Subsequent correctly configured fetches make zero config writes. A separate qualified Linux Git allocator interposer reports 2,374→3,586 allocation requests and 5,248,735→5,530,696 cumulative requested bytes per explicit fetch; all five A/B/A2 samples match exactly, with A2 identical to A. These counts exclude shell/Python, mmap and hidden libc allocations and do not measure retained memory. The already-present content path still returns before fetch policy and remains two Git processes with no network or pack changes; its earlier path-specific A/B/A2 control was within noise.

The exact base-root `git diff --quiet <a> <b> -- <path>` with two missing commits was separately verified through exec → Python bare `git`: 36 objects without the wrapper, 6 with it, all promisor; changed and unchanged paths retain native exit codes. The already-merged revision preparation needs no further diff change.

Production growth is 104 lines; tests grow 102 lines with an exact scoped allocation. The growth covers shared native fetch selection, usable promisor registration, and one reused project filter reader; there is no new cache or transport staging layer. The separate `scripts/pr` authoritative-fetch correction is merged in #193670.

Fresh independent Codex autoreview through P3 is scoped-clean after both hosted-review corrections. The corrected `pnpm check:changed` run completed: types, formatting and the other guards pass. It caught a test-only no-shadow error, which was corrected and passed targeted lint/format checks. The remaining repository-wide dead-export scan fails on 33 production / 9 full-tree entries. The canonical checker reproduces identical entries on exact parent `2a41138`, with no module-resolution errors; the causal attribution reuses prior lane evidence, with the new diagnostics export identified below. The test-line guard reproduces the same 128-line deficit on exact parent `2a41138ac9d467e12b33d8981cafe7d13ad6d019` (6,635,428 lines / 6,635,300 ceiling); this PR adds exactly 102 lines and 102 allocation. That deficit was introduced by #196346 (`b91520c`), not this change. The newly detected unused `projectLeaseDiagnosticFrames` export originates in `2c4e34a72f490c710bc155319fcabf872f482b3e` and is a main regression requiring separate repair. No live shared clone was modified for this proof, and the historical observed packs cannot be assigned to a particular caller from the available logs.

## What Problem This Solves

Busy Gateways discard active `sessions.list` delta baselines when old row generations fill the view-cache byte budget, forcing steady sidebar clients to receive full lists again. Related: #193716.

## User Impact

Steady clients retain their newest comparison baseline under history pressure. The existing 32 MiB and 512-view limits remain unchanged. Older generations can retire earlier; stale clients and working sets that cannot fit still fall back to full responses. No config, protocol, or schema change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reclaim older row generations at the existing cache owner before evicting whole views. Keep the newest generation during invalidation, and include it in oversized-view admission so one unretainable view cannot flush healthy readers. Count pressure retains ordinary LRU eviction. Runtime production delta: +32 lines for accounted history retirement; benchmark tooling +51, tests +37.

A committed synthetic workload uses 5,000 sessions, 38 clients / 12 audiences, seven query shapes, 48 updates, and 12,768 calls per process (7,296 sidebar). ## What Problem This Solves

Sandbox preparation rewalks unchanged skill trees after more than 100 other destinations evict their usage records.

## User Impact

Docker and Podman sandboxes retain unchanged skill-copy reuse across large preparation bursts. Source revisions still reconcile the copies. No new configuration options are introduced.

The existing generated manifest now retains the source generation and identity-to-destination facts that previously disappeared with the bounded usage cache. The destination map also owns the identity set, removing duplicated persisted `entryKeys`. Non-local skills retain their identities with null destinations. Discovery still constructs every path; only an exact match to a discovered destination can authorize preservation.

Disk-based reuse is enabled only for Docker/Podman read-only skill mounts. Remote and unknown targets retain reconciliation after eviction because remote mirrors can return guest-written metadata. Their warm cache continues to use producer-owned facts. Legacy manifests reconcile normally; malformed selected mappings cannot authorize reuse. The warm-only defensive clone is removed because cold results already share the same entries and consumers read or remap them.

Production code grows by **17 net lines** across two files to retain and validate the existing manifest facts and preserve the backend trust boundary. There is no new cache, store, SQLite schema, engine queue, or shared writable tree.

## Evidence

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `scripts/pr` landing stalls for up to about 50 minutes per fetch at 100% CPU when merge admission fetches a pinned commit into a large blobless partial clone. Observed on a shared clone with about 244M objects and 16.7k promisor packs, where it blocked serial PR landing.

## User Impact

No user-visible product change. Maintainers landing PRs from a partial clone no longer wait on a full promisor-history parse each time merge admission needs a commit that is not yet local.

## Why This Change Was Made

`merge_outcome_require_commit` fetched by literal URL, and a literal URL does not match the `origin` promisor remote. Git therefore requested no filter and did not treat the result as a promisor pack, so `check_connected` missed its promisor shortcut and spawned the connectivity `rev-list`.

The fetch now uses the promisor projection `fetch_canonical_ref` already had, extracted so it can take an explicit source. It still fetches the exact pinned OID from the observed authoritative repository URL, and still writes no refs or `FETCH_HEAD`. The projection lasts for that one command, so no remote configuration persists.

<details>
<summary>Why it was so slow (Git 2.56 source plus a stack sample)</summary>

- `partial_clone_get_default_filter_spec` finds no promisor named after the URL, so `TRANS_OPT_FROM_PROMISOR` stays unset. Fetch-pack then does not pass `index-pack --promisor`; small fetches go to `unpack-objects` as loose objects.
- `check_connected_promisor` finds the wanted commit outside any promisor pack and falls back to `rev-list --objects --stdin --exclude-promisor-objects --not --all`.
- `prepare_revision_walk` flags every promisor object, including the parent's tree. `mark_tree_uninteresting` then returns early on that flagged tree, so the parent's blob entries are never marked.
- Any new tree with an unchanged sibling blob therefore reaches a missing, unflagged blob, and `process_blob` calls `is_promisor_object`, which parses every promisor object. So ordinary commits trigger this, not an unusual history shape.

A sample of the running `rev-list` showed 4076/4076 samples under `process_blob` → `is_promisor_object` → `add_promisor_object` → `parse_object_with_flags`.

</details>

**Tradeoffs accepted**

- Each such fetch now adds one small promisor pack instead of loose objects, the same as every other canonical fetch. Partial clones with many packs should keep relying on their existing pack maintenance.
- Blobs in these commits are now omitted and lazily fetched from `origin`, as they already are for PR heads. If `origin` is not the authoritative repository, that lazy read depends on `origin` being able to serve the blob, which is expected for a GitHub fork network but was not tested here.
- A clone with `remote.origin.promisor=true` and no `partialclonefilter` keeps the old slow path, because `fetch_canonical_ref` only projects when a filter exists.
- The conflicting-paths diagnostic runs `merge-tree` under `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`. With more blobs omitted it may more often print its existing "paths unavailable" message. This is diagnostic text only, and no admission decision depends on it.

Admission reads that run with lazy fetching disabled were audited and use tree-level commands (`diff --name-only --no-renames`, `ls-tree`, `merge-base`, `cat-file -e`), which do not need blobs at the newly fetched commit.

Other fetches in `scripts/pr` and `scripts/pr-lib`: `fetch_canonical_ref` is the only other one, and it already projected these settings.

## Evidence

**Timed experiment** using task-owned synthetic blobless clones with Git 2.56.0 and a local `file://` remote. The shared clone was never touched. Each row is the range of three trials fetching a one-file edit in a directory with sibling files:

| Clone objects | Literal URL (before) | Projected URL (after) | Connectivity `rev-list` |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 800k | 2.4–3.0s | 0.09–0.11s | before only |
| 4M | 13.8–17.0s | 0.12s | before only |

Control: a literal-URL commit that reaches no unchanged blob also spawns the `rev-list` but stays at about 0.7s at 4M objects, which isolates the expensive parse. At the 4M row that is about 3.7µs per object, or roughly 15 minutes at 244M objects on these small synthetic trees. That is the same order of magnitude as the observed 50 minutes, **not a reproduction of it**. Splitting similar history across 1000 and 4000 promisor packs did not materially change the `rev-list` cost that was measured, but that run covered only the cheap flagging tier. Pack count does affect the fixed route: its median fetch rose from about 0.1s at 1 pack to about 1.6s at 4000 packs, so expect seconds rather than milliseconds at 16.7k packs.

The projected route matched fetching by the `origin` name in every trial, and a lazy read of an omitted sibling blob afterward succeeded.

**Real GitHub:** in a task-owned shallow blobless clone, a projected fetch of a commit by SHA from `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw` returned 0, spawned no `rev-list`, passed `index-pack --promisor`, added a promisor pack, and persisted no new remote config.

**Regression test:** `test/scripts/pr-main-refresh.test.ts` was red on the base with the exact `--exclude-promisor-objects` command in the Git trace, and is green with the fix. Its authoritative repository is separate from `origin` and is the only one holding the commit, so it also proves the fetch did not move to `origin`. It also asserts the blob stays omitted and that shared refs, `FETCH_HEAD`, and config are unchanged.

**Focused suites:** `pr-main-refresh`, `pr-merge-receipt`, `pr-merge-prior-ci-rest-observation`, `pr-merge-head-drift`, `pr-merge-outcome`, and `pr-merge-admission` pass. `pr-merge-prior-ci-main-drift` had 2 of 66 tests fail with exit 143 under heavy local load, when the file took 562s and hit the fixture's 20s process timeout. Run alone, both pass, at 12.3s with the fix and 12.0s on the base; the rest of that file passed in the same run. Lint and the scripts test typecheck pass.

**Not proven:** the fix has not been run on the affected shared clone, because that would write into it. The first real landing from that clone is the remaining end-to-end confirmation.

**Review:** independent local Codex autoreview of the change was scoped-clean at P0–P2. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable in this checkout.

## Follow-up validation and test allocation

The production patch is unchanged. A separate allocation grants exactly 45 net regression-test lines for the native authoritative-fetch test; the shared scalar baseline is unchanged. Against `d2a166c6ac6399e8940718b8c30fb91615e1c281`, the ratchet now passes: 6,494,648 lines, ceiling 6,494,662, slack 14. Before the allocation, the same comparison failed with +45 net lines.

The native regression was rechecked on the original PR head: it passes in 12.05 seconds of test time (15.66 seconds including the runner), and fails on the exact comparison-base owner files at the intended connectivity-walk assertion. Four affected authority-revocation cases pass across the main-drift and auto-replacement suites (61.28 seconds including the runner). This focused repeat supplements the unchanged whole-suite and large-clone proof above; it does not claim a new live affected-clone landing.

A separate small Git 2.56.0 synthetic linked-worktree experiment confirms pack semantics: a literal authoritative fetch receives 1 commit, 1 tree and 128 blobs in a 14,600-byte ordinary pack; the canonical projection receives 1 commit and 1 tree in a 3,303-byte promisor pack. Shared config, tracking ref and root FETCH_HEAD stay unchanged. This is object-shape proof, not a new latency benchmark.

Independent Codex autoreview through P3 of the complete candidate plus allocation is scoped-clean with no actionable findings. The full changed-file check completed with typecheck, lint, format and candidate-relevant ratchets passing. Its historical main failures are preserved rather than described as green:

- The upgrade helper's unused export followed removal of its last external consumer in `0ad8f20a0442cfe87c9022350ea6af593e9215a8` (#193352); the Google helper's unused export was introduced in `6fa925242b85ca4f1202c1f970da0f796522831f` (#193341). Both are fixed on current main by `228f05f55abac410836933a728c8e86d46a7cb45`.
- The old attribution guard rejects 65 maintainer-credit entries added with the 2026.11.1 closeout in `de04fbe0caa9332999bdcc28d5d4e049672afb16` (#193427). Its maintainer-credit policy is corrected on current main by `266a7aa0fe69e2b5fe6445c4ceb1e15b5360c957` (#194364).

Both failed guards were rerun on a clean checkout of the exact comparison parent `d2a166c6ac6399e8940718b8c30fb91615e1c281` with a frozen in-tree dependency install: the same two exports fail in the same scans, and all 65 changelog findings match exactly. These are historical main regressions, not new failures from this PR; their later fixes are already ancestors of current main. The initial borrowed-dependency baseline attempt was rejected for module resolution and is excluded from this proof.

The allocation correction is committed as `9b34fa25d8350cf89294b7784aa3730210ed0d31`. Final exact-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper re-review remain the landing gates.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes long sandbox freezes during ordinary workspace reconciliation, which held the container pause across staged-file materialization, Git patch preparation, and temporary-file cleanup.

## User Impact

The guest can keep running while reconciliation prepares immutable results. Imports pause again before confirming the target and applying changes; concurrent edits remain saved and produce a visible conflict. Each released pause now records its reason, duration, and dominant phase at the quiescence owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing checkpoint snapshot owner for btrfs exports, and delay the import freeze until the existing confirming preflight. Remove the immediate duplicate full-tree verification when the target's writers are already frozen. Host callers retain their verification, and journal recovery and two-sided base refresh retain their pause requirements.

The bounded telemetry distinguishes newly owned pauses from recovered pauses with an unknown earlier start. Failed resumes do not log success. No configuration, schema, cache, or retention change is introduced. Production delta is +172 lines for telemetry and the pause/capture handoff, including a typed extraction of existing acceptance callbacks to respect file-size limits; test delta is +141 lines.

## Evidence

The production-path projection/SQLite/Git regression fails on the original code because patch preparation observes a paused guest. It passes here, verifies mutation stays paused, counts one accepted-target inventory capture, and rejects an injected concurrent guest edit before journaling without losing bytes. A second red/green assertion ensures every actual preflight receives the correct phase label.

Focused proof: 86 projection, 20 quiescence and 60 reconcile/recovery/publication tests passed, with two existing filesystem-platform skips. The acceptance extraction passed 19 affected tests; integration with #196807 passed 31 capture/checkpoint cases. Final telemetry correction passed its owner regression, core/test typechecks, lint and independent Codex review. `pnpm check:changed --staged` passed all gates except the independently reproduced inherited Knip set: 33 production/9 full-tree findings on integrated parent `9c0b1b44bd438c3bbb57cda5856ab4270da27ead`. The additional main regression is the diagnostics export from #196724 (`2c4e34a72f490`). Exact-head CI [42896338687](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42896338687) passed on `60c5cdaf88e00b5f1d52198317d5c89c5a7a6c2d`: 56 successful, 28 skipped jobs, including security, both UI-e2e shards and the aggregate gate. The earlier run failed only on 128 inherited test-line debt from #196346, subsequently repaired on main by #196370; final CI needs no admin exception. Final-head ClawSweeper re-review has zero findings and zero open checkboxes; the completed measurements and explicit acceptance resolved the performance hold.

### Native performance and explicit tradeoff decision

The declared protocol uses the real projection owner, Git/SQLite and native Podman, with 62,000 files (1,100,004,000 bytes), 20,000 changed files, 10,001 synthetic sessions and an actual 35.20 GiB agent database. No production data was copied. Five serial counterbalanced A/B pairs follow two A/A controls; setup, warmup and separate allocation profiling are excluded from timing. Every changed byte, subsequent guest read and later-write freshness passed.

Baseline `6d811790acb43c46e3a7c950f22c3bed22b17f17`; measured candidate `3786ffc96c66b915c4ce313e57a72f38ceb121fc`. This is prior-head evidence: later main integration and the final phase-marker fix were inspected for input equivalence; measured import staging, patch preparation and mutation work/order are unchanged. No final-head native timing is claimed. Linux, 4 CPUs, 16.56 GB RAM, Node 24.22.1, Podman 5.8.4, ordinary filesystem. labels.name: repo-535d150f
labels.description: ClawSweeper has no concrete contributor-facing blocker left for this PR.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `scripts/pr` landing stalls for up to about 50 minutes per fetch at 100% CPU when merge admission fetches a pinned commit into a large blobless partial clone. Observed on a shared clone with about 244M objects and 16.7k promisor packs, where it blocked serial PR landing.

## User Impact

No user-visible product change. Maintainers landing PRs from a partial clone no longer wait on a full promisor-history parse each time merge admission needs a commit that is not yet local.

## Why This Change Was Made

`merge_outcome_require_commit` fetched by literal URL, and a literal URL does not match the `origin` promisor remote. Git therefore requested no filter and did not treat the result as a promisor pack, so `check_connected` missed its promisor shortcut and spawned the connectivity `rev-list`.

The fetch now uses the promisor projection `fetch_canonical_ref` already had, extracted so it can take an explicit source. It still fetches the exact pinned OID from the observed authoritative repository URL, and still writes no refs or `FETCH_HEAD`. The projection lasts for that one command, so no remote configuration persists.

<details>
<summary>Why it was so slow (Git 2.56 source plus a stack sample)</summary>

- `partial_clone_get_default_filter_spec` finds no promisor named after the URL, so `TRANS_OPT_FROM_PROMISOR` stays unset. Fetch-pack then does not pass `index-pack --promisor`; small fetches go to `unpack-objects` as loose objects.
- `check_connected_promisor` finds the wanted commit outside any promisor pack and falls back to `rev-list --objects --stdin --exclude-promisor-objects --not --all`.
- `prepare_revision_walk` flags every promisor object, including the parent's tree. `mark_tree_uninteresting` then returns early on that flagged tree, so the parent's blob entries are never marked.
- Any new tree with an unchanged sibling blob therefore reaches a missing, unflagged blob, and `process_blob` calls `is_promisor_object`, which parses every promisor object. So ordinary commits trigger this, not an unusual history shape.

A sample of the running `rev-list` showed 4076/4076 samples under `process_blob` → `is_promisor_object` → `add_promisor_object` → `parse_object_with_flags`.

</details>

**Tradeoffs accepted**

- Each such fetch now adds one small promisor pack instead of loose objects, the same as every other canonical fetch. Partial clones with many packs should keep relying on their existing pack maintenance.
- Blobs in these commits are now omitted and lazily fetched from `origin`, as they already are for PR heads. If `origin` is not the authoritative repository, that lazy read depends on `origin` being able to serve the blob, which is expected for a GitHub fork network but was not tested here.
- A clone with `remote.origin.promisor=true` and no `partialclonefilter` keeps the old slow path, because `fetch_canonical_ref` only projects when a filter exists.
- The conflicting-paths diagnostic runs `merge-tree` under `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`. With more blobs omitted it may more often print its existing "paths unavailable" message. This is diagnostic text only, and no admission decision depends on it.

Admission reads that run with lazy fetching disabled were audited and use tree-level commands (`diff --name-only --no-renames`, `ls-tree`, `merge-base`, `cat-file -e`), which do not need blobs at the newly fetched commit.

Other fetches in `scripts/pr` and `scripts/pr-lib`: `fetch_canonical_ref` is the only other one, and it already projected these settings.

## Evidence

**Timed experiment** using task-owned synthetic blobless clones with Git 2.56.0 and a local `file://` remote. The shared clone was never touched. Each row is the range of three trials fetching a one-file edit in a directory with sibling files:

| Clone objects | Literal URL (before) | Projected URL (after) | Connectivity `rev-list` |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 800k | 2.4–3.0s | 0.09–0.11s | before only |
| 4M | 13.8–17.0s | 0.12s | before only |

Control: a literal-URL commit that reaches no unchanged blob also spawns the `rev-list` but stays at about 0.7s at 4M objects, which isolates the expensive parse. At the 4M row that is about 3.7µs per object, or roughly 15 minutes at 244M objects on these small synthetic trees. That is the same order of magnitude as the observed 50 minutes, **not a reproduction of it**. Splitting similar history across 1000 and 4000 promisor packs did not materially change the `rev-list` cost that was measured, but that run covered only the cheap flagging tier. Pack count does affect the fixed route: its median fetch rose from about 0.1s at 1 pack to about 1.6s at 4000 packs, so expect seconds rather than milliseconds at 16.7k packs.

The projected route matched fetching by the `origin` name in every trial, and a lazy read of an omitted sibling blob afterward succeeded.

**Real GitHub:** in a task-owned shallow blobless clone, a projected fetch of a commit by SHA from `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw` returned 0, spawned no `rev-list`, passed `index-pack --promisor`, added a promisor pack, and persisted no new remote config.

**Regression test:** `test/scripts/pr-main-refresh.test.ts` was red on the base with the exact `--exclude-promisor-objects` command in the Git trace, and is green with the fix. Its authoritative repository is separate from `origin` and is the only one holding the commit, so it also proves the fetch did not move to `origin`. It also asserts the blob stays omitted and that shared refs, `FETCH_HEAD`, and config are unchanged.

**Focused suites:** `pr-main-refresh`, `pr-merge-receipt`, `pr-merge-prior-ci-rest-observation`, `pr-merge-head-drift`, `pr-merge-outcome`, and `pr-merge-admission` pass. `pr-merge-prior-ci-main-drift` had 2 of 66 tests fail with exit 143 under heavy local load, when the file took 562s and hit the fixture's 20s process timeout. Run alone, both pass, at 12.3s with the fix and 12.0s on the base; the rest of that file passed in the same run. Lint and the scripts test typecheck pass.

**Not proven:** the fix has not been run on the affected shared clone, because that would write into it. The first real landing from that clone is the remaining end-to-end confirmation.

**Review:** independent local Codex autoreview of the change was scoped-clean at P0–P2. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable in this checkout.

## Follow-up validation and test allocation

The production patch is unchanged. A separate allocation grants exactly 45 net regression-test lines for the native authoritative-fetch test; the shared scalar baseline is unchanged. issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes long sandbox freezes during ordinary workspace reconciliation, which held the container pause across staged-file materialization, Git patch preparation, and temporary-file cleanup.

## User Impact

The guest can keep running while reconciliation prepares immutable results. Imports pause again before confirming the target and applying changes; concurrent edits remain saved and produce a visible conflict. Each released pause now records its reason, duration, and dominant phase at the quiescence owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing checkpoint snapshot owner for btrfs exports, and delay the import freeze until the existing confirming preflight. Remove the immediate duplicate full-tree verification when the target's writers are already frozen. Host callers retain their verification, and journal recovery and two-sided base refresh retain their pause requirements.

The bounded telemetry distinguishes newly owned pauses from recovered pauses with an unknown earlier start. Failed resumes do not log success. No configuration, schema, cache, or retention change is introduced. Production delta is +172 lines for telemetry and the pause/capture handoff, including a typed extraction of existing acceptance callbacks to respect file-size limits; test delta is +141 lines.

## Evidence

The production-path projection/SQLite/Git regression fails on the original code because patch preparation observes a paused guest. It passes here, verifies mutation stays paused, counts one accepted-target inventory capture, and rejects an injected concurrent guest edit before journaling without losing bytes. A second red/green assertion ensures every actual preflight receives the correct phase label.

Focused proof: 86 projection, 20 quiescence and 60 reconcile/recovery/publication tests passed, with two existing filesystem-platform skips. The acceptance extraction passed 19 affected tests; integration with #196807 passed 31 capture/checkpoint cases. Final telemetry correction passed its owner regression, core/test typechecks, lint and independent Codex review. `pnpm check:changed --staged` passed all gates except the independently reproduced inherited Knip set: 33 production/9 full-tree findings on integrated parent `9c0b1b44bd438c3bbb57cda5856ab4270da27ead`. The additional main regression is the diagnostics export from #196724 (`2c4e34a72f490`). Exact-head CI [42896338687](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42896338687) passed on `60c5cdaf88e00b5f1d52198317d5c89c5a7a6c2d`: 56 successful, 28 skipped jobs, including security, both UI-e2e shards and the aggregate gate. The earlier run failed only on 128 inherited test-line debt from #196346, subsequently repaired on main by #196370; final CI needs no admin exception. Final-head ClawSweeper re-review has zero findings and zero open checkboxes; the completed measurements and explicit acceptance resolved the performance hold.

### Native performance and explicit tradeoff decision

The declared protocol uses the real projection owner, Git/SQLite and native Podman, with 62,000 files (1,100,004,000 bytes), 20,000 changed files, 10,001 synthetic sessions and an actual 35.20 GiB agent database. No production data was copied. Five serial counterbalanced A/B pairs follow two A/A controls; setup, warmup and separate allocation profiling are excluded from timing. Every changed byte, subsequent guest read and later-write freshness passed.

Baseline `6d811790acb43c46e3a7c950f22c3bed22b17f17`; measured candidate `3786ffc96c66b915c4ce313e57a72f38ceb121fc`. This is prior-head evidence: later main integration and the final phase-marker fix were inspected for input equivalence; measured import staging, patch preparation and mutation work/order are unchanged. No final-head native timing is claimed. Linux, 4 CPUs, 16.56 GB RAM, Node 24.22.1, Podman 5.8.4, ordinary filesystem. The host lacks btrfs kernel support, so snapshot behavior has focused owner proof but no native btrfs performance claim.

| Metric | Baseline median | Candidate median | Change | Baseline / candidate p95 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Total frozen time per operation | 28.78 s | 7.44 s | −74.15% | 31.59 / 9.22 s |
| Longest continuous freeze | 28.78 s | 7.21 s | −74.95% | 31.59 / 8.89 s |
| Owner wall time | 29.62 s | 29.43 s | −0.64% | 32.77 / 35.39 s |
| Owner-period process CPU | 34.19 s | 33.04 s | −3.36% | 39.09 / 40.20 s |
| Main-thread CPU | 2.78 s | 2.97 s | +6.86% | 3.34 / 3.74 s |
| Cgroup CPU, including helpers | 44.38 s | 43.80 s | −1.30% | 51.54 / 54.36 s |

Five samples per arm; nearest-rank p95 is the observed maximum, not a stable tail estimate. Total-freeze ranges were 26.48–31.59 s versus 6.23–9.22 s; owner ranges 26.56–32.77 s versus 26.64–35.39 s. A/A variation: freeze 7.54%, owner 5.12%, process CPU 6.81%, main-thread CPU 12.13%, cgroup CPU 7.94%. No overall CPU or throughput speedup is claimed. The first pair increased owner time 18.84%, cgroup CPU 19.80% and main-thread CPU 39.64%; these unfavorable samples are retained. Separate sampled main-isolate allocation was 1,444,981,416 → 1,438,093,912 bytes (−0.48%); This sampled main-isolate measurement covers the whole measured burst, including fixed correctness reads and cleanup; it is not isolated owner allocation. Node 24 provides no total-allocation counter, and all six worker counters and native-helper allocations are unavailable, not zero.

The first baseline pair held the pause during a 7.82 s patch-construction await, 3.54 s staged-manifest work and 3.25 s staging. Equivalent candidate work ran with the guest resumed. These are overlapping phase intervals and must not be summed. A native guest heartbeat independently measured its maximum stall falling from 26.45 to 8.37 s. One duplicate accepted-target inventory is deleted; final confirming preflight remains.

**Decision under the requested maintainer scope:** accept the observed overhead in exchange for the consistent large-workspace freeze reduction. The 100-file/10-change setup smoke increased total frozen time from 202.83 to 284.41 ms and owner time from 255.17 to 560.47 ms, while longest freeze fell to 107.66 ms. This is one smoke per arm, not a statistical small-workload benchmark. Two extra native pause/resume round trips preserve the opaque outer callback's existing frozen contract. The bounded 305 ms owner cost, +6.86% median main-thread CPU and unfavorable observed tails are accepted for this repair; they are not dismissed as noise. Warm unchanged and checkpoint fast paths remain unchanged. The declared byte/conflict/freeze-reduction acceptance rule is met; this decision explicitly addresses the ≥20% regression stop.

Reproduce through the committed harness (same harness in both source revisions):

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/local-workspace-checkpoint-measure.ts \
  --mode reconcile --reconcile-target projection --reconcile-changed-files 20000 \
  --native-turns --sandbox-backend podman --guest-image docker.io/library/node:24.22.1-trixie \
  --files 62000 --file-bytes 17742 --transcript-mib 12288 --requests 1 --burst 1 \
  --instrument timing --output <task-proof-directory> --report <arm>.json
```

The supplied 214.8 s production incident cannot be assigned to a specific syscall or queue from the old logs. This fixture reproduces the same broad frozen-owner defect at 26–32 s. Base-refresh callback network preparation remains outside this ordinary-reconciliation fix. No production access or deployment was performed. The new unpause log enables post-deployment verification.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Conversation-environment cleanup that exhausted its retry budget ran and warned again on every Gateway restart. Restart-resume summaries also counted parked sessions without saying why each session was parked.

## User Impact

Parked cleanup remains visible in environment/session status with an actionable inspection and explicit Stop retry. Restarts and background sweeps stop repeating the failed provider operation. Lease ownership remains until release is confirmed. Each parked restart-resume session gets one bounded `yield-waiting` diagnostic; that count describes surviving conversation wake sources, not environment cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Persist the parking decision in the existing environment diagnostic, remove the separate process-local display override, and skip parked attachments before session preparation. Explicit Stop retries cleanup and preserves the original bootstrap failure after successful release. Existing unparked records still receive a genuine recovery attempt before a new parking decision; there is no schema migration or new configuration.

Provider identity still matters: Machine0 is direct-only, so another backend's coordinator `not_found` cannot prove its resource is gone. Crabbox already accepts a verified released receipt before Machine0 authentication; existing strict release/absence confirmation remains unchanged. Operators repair the original provider account/state and explicitly retry Stop.

## Evidence

The owner regression failed before the fix with four provider destroys instead of one over three store reopens. Final consolidated cleanup tests: 21 passed; restart-resume: 29 passed; lifecycle/access siblings: 18 passed. The added parking cases cover both ten attempts and one hour, silent restart/sweep suppression, explicit retry, and preserved original bootstrap failure. Restart reason regressions failed in all three waiting scenarios before the diagnostic was added.

Five existing Crabbox stop-confirmation tests also pass (73 focused/sibling tests total). Both full-source Codex reviews and the test-consolidation review are clean at P0–P2. Formatting, lint, core/test/script typechecks, schema guards and import-cycle checks pass. `pnpm check:changed` fails only its dead-export audit: 34 production and 10 full-tree findings in untouched files. Both finding lists reproduce byte-for-byte on exact parent `0409efbc343c579f3d711f723811c58fa9497f05`, with no resolution errors. All 34 symbols are attributed to the changes below. This is a main regression, not a passing check.

| Owner work / metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Provider calls / repeated warnings | 2 / 2 | 0 / 0 |
| Session-path config reads | 38 | 0 |
| Wall time median / p95 | 1150.161 / 1273.199 ms | 0.474 / 0.562 ms |
| Process CPU median / p95 | 1973.490 / 2054.691 ms | 1.067 / 1.208 ms |
| Main-isolate sampled allocation median / p95 | 3,827,536 / 4,121,976 bytes | 101,040 / 154,768 bytes |

Five serial A/B pairs; separate five-sample allocation passes include collected objects. Both A/A controls retain 2/2/38 work counts, but their wall medians differ (1483.937 vs 2462.901 ms), so these are loaded-host owner timings, not a forecast of production boot savings. Main-isolate imports are warm; each sample reopens service/store and includes required worker re-admission. Both unresolved lease IDs and destroying states remain owned in every trial. The fixture database is 14,499,840 bytes on macOS/APFS.

Final test wrappers took 97.90s for the consolidated 21 cleanup cases, 209.84s for 29 restart cases, and 36.56s for the five Crabbox cases, including compilation/worker startup. The combined earlier 41-case cleanup/sibling run took 217.68s; its one new assertion error was corrected and the complete affected cleanup file rerun green. The later consolidation preserves four-hour retry bounds, one-hour parking, status RPC, restart suppression and explicit recovery in one parameterized owner test.

Measurement acceptance was fixed before trials: two already-parked cleanup rows must produce zero provider calls and zero repeated warnings after reconstruction while retaining both lease IDs; owner latency, CPU and allocation must improve or hold. The committed workload uses real service and SQLite worker ownership with 5,000 synthetic session metadata rows, two cleanup rows, serial A/A controls, five paired baseline/candidate runs and separate allocation/profile passes. It does not claim a full Gateway, 35 GiB transcript, workspace scan or btrfs benchmark; the owner does not traverse workspace files, and the available disk could not hold a new populated 35 GiB fixture.

Runtime production delta is +19 lines, justified by durable retry suppression and original-failure preservation; test delta is −10 lines, with no test-line allocation. The benchmark is separate proof tooling. No UI-imported modules changed. No live Gateway state, machine lifecycle, or credentials were changed.

<details>
<summary>Exact-parent unused-export regression attribution</summary>

Parent reproduction: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts` in an isolated archive of `0409efbc343c579f3d711f723811c58fa9497f05`, using the same qualified dependencies. Exit 1; script scan zero, production 34, full-tree 10, identical ordered finding lists to the candidate.

| Owner group | Production / full-tree findings | Introducing change |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Compaction summary helper | 1 / 1 | `c7152f3bda8e5`, #196207 |
| Models/tools/auth/process facades | 8 / 2 | `625945b7ae01d`, #192552 |
| Tool directory helpers | 2 / 0 | `80ba593b8b14b`, #196252 |
| Delivery-generation diagnostic helper | 1 / 0 | `2c4e34a72f490` |
| Gateway key helpers | 5 / 2 | `37a3b162a0c58`, #196380 |
| Billing-warning helper | 1 / 0 | `56617cd000864`, #191326 |
| Provider-runtime/external-auth facades | 11 / 0 | `f63e5cd0f6d38`, #190205 |
| Provider auth type barrel | 4 / 4 | `cf1ae7bb6a729`, #190544 |
| Browser pair constant | 1 / 1 | `d85ebfe8daad4`, #191513 |

The provider facade attribution was also replayed: restoring only the parent wrapper of #190205 in the isolated baseline removes exactly those 11 findings (34 → 23), with no new findings. These are separate main regressions; no exports or audit baselines were changed here. This local-check evidence does not waive any later CI failure.

</details>

The initial CI run (42887176790, head `971a6e7`) failed only the test-line ratchet: the merged tree inherited 128 lines of budget debt from #196346. issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Conversation-environment cleanup that exhausted its retry budget ran and warned again on every Gateway restart. Restart-resume summaries also counted parked sessions without saying why each session was parked.

## User Impact

Parked cleanup remains visible in environment/session status with an actionable inspection and explicit Stop retry. Restarts and background sweeps stop repeating the failed provider operation. Lease ownership remains until release is confirmed. Each parked restart-resume session gets one bounded `yield-waiting` diagnostic; that count describes surviving conversation wake sources, not environment cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Persist the parking decision in the existing environment diagnostic, remove the separate process-local display override, and skip parked attachments before session preparation. Explicit Stop retries cleanup and preserves the original bootstrap failure after successful release. Existing unparked records still receive a genuine recovery attempt before a new parking decision; there is no schema migration or new configuration.

Provider identity still matters: Machine0 is direct-only, so another backend's coordinator `not_found` cannot prove its resource is gone. Crabbox already accepts a verified released receipt before Machine0 authentication; existing strict release/absence confirmation remains unchanged. Operators repair the original provider account/state and explicitly retry Stop.

## Evidence

The owner regression failed before the fix with four provider destroys instead of one over three store reopens. Final consolidated cleanup tests: 21 passed; restart-resume: 29 passed; lifecycle/access siblings: 18 passed. The added parking cases cover both ten attempts and one hour, silent restart/sweep suppression, explicit retry, and preserved original bootstrap failure. Restart reason regressions failed in all three waiting scenarios before the diagnostic was added.

Five existing Crabbox stop-confirmation tests also pass (73 focused/sibling tests total). Both full-source Codex reviews and the test-consolidation review are clean at P0–P2. Formatting, lint, core/test/script typechecks, schema guards and import-cycle checks pass. `pnpm check:changed` fails only its dead-export audit: 34 production and 10 full-tree findings in untouched files. Both finding lists reproduce byte-for-byte on exact parent `0409efbc343c579f3d711f723811c58fa9497f05`, with no resolution errors. All 34 symbols are attributed to the changes below. This is a main regression, not a passing check.

| Owner work / metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Provider calls / repeated warnings | 2 / 2 | 0 / 0 |
| Session-path config reads | 38 | 0 |
| Wall time median / p95 | 1150.161 / 1273.199 ms | 0.474 / 0.562 ms |
| Process CPU median / p95 | 1973.490 / 2054.691 ms | 1.067 / 1.208 ms |
| Main-isolate sampled allocation median / p95 | 3,827,536 / 4,121,976 bytes | 101,040 / 154,768 bytes |

Five serial A/B pairs; separate five-sample allocation passes include collected objects. Both A/A controls retain 2/2/38 work counts, but their wall medians differ (1483.937 vs 2462.901 ms), so these are loaded-host owner timings, not a forecast of production boot savings. Main-isolate imports are warm; each sample reopens service/store and includes required worker re-admission. Both unresolved lease IDs and destroying states remain owned in every trial. The fixture database is 14,499,840 bytes on macOS/APFS.

Final test wrappers took 97.90s for the consolidated 21 cleanup cases, 209.84s for 29 restart cases, and 36.56s for the five Crabbox cases, including compilation/worker startup. The combined earlier 41-case cleanup/sibling run took 217.68s; its one new assertion error was corrected and the complete affected cleanup file rerun green. The later consolidation preserves four-hour retry bounds, one-hour parking, status RPC, restart suppression and explicit recovery in one parameterized owner test.

Measurement acceptance was fixed before trials: two already-parked cleanup rows must produce zero provider calls and zero repeated warnings after reconstruction while retaining both lease IDs; owner latency, CPU and allocation must improve or hold. The committed workload uses real service and SQLite worker ownership with 5,000 synthetic session metadata rows, two cleanup rows, serial A/A controls, five paired baseline/candidate runs and separate allocation/profile passes. It does not claim a full Gateway, 35 GiB transcript, workspace scan or btrfs benchmark; the owner does not traverse workspace files, and the available disk could not hold a new populated 35 GiB fixture.

Runtime production delta is +19 lines, justified by durable retry suppression and original-failure preservation; test delta is −10 lines, with no test-line allocation. The benchmark is separate proof tooling. No UI-imported modules changed. No live Gateway state, machine lifecycle, or credentials were changed.

<details>
<summary>Exact-parent unused-export regression attribution</summary>

Parent reproduction: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts` in an isolated archive of `0409efbc343c579f3d711f723811c58fa9497f05`, using the same qualified dependencies. Exit 1; script scan zero, production 34, full-tree 10, identical ordered finding lists to the candidate.

| Owner group | Production / full-tree findings | Introducing change |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Compaction summary helper | 1 / 1 | `c7152f3bda8e5`, #196207 |
| Models/tools/auth/process facades | 8 / 2 | `625945b7ae01d`, #192552 |
| Tool directory helpers | 2 / 0 | `80ba593b8b14b`, #196252 |
| Delivery-generation diagnostic helper | 1 / 0 | `2c4e34a72f490` |
| Gateway key helpers | 5 / 2 | `37a3b162a0c58`, #196380 |
| Billing-warning helper | 1 / 0 | `56617cd000864`, #191326 |
| Provider-runtime/external-auth facades | 11 / 0 | `f63e5cd0f6d38`, #190205 |
| Provider auth type barrel | 4 / 4 | `cf1ae7bb6a729`, #190544 |
| Browser pair constant | 1 / 1 | `d85ebfe8daad4`, #191513 |

The provider facade attribution was also replayed: restoring only the parent wrapper of #190205 in the isolated baseline removes exactly those 11 findings (34 → 23), with no new findings. These are separate main regressions; no exports or audit baselines were changed here. This local-check evidence does not waive any later CI failure.

</details>

The initial CI run (42887176790, head `971a6e7`) failed only the test-line ratchet: the merged tree inherited 128 lines of budget debt from #196346. The exact CI main parent passes only under the checker’s zero-growth rule, so this was not treated as a qualifying inherited-red exception. Consolidating overlapping cleanup cases removes the PR’s test growth and its allocation; the local ratchet passes. Final-head CI is required.

## Latest-stable data compatibility

A fresh owner-path upgrade from latest stable `v2026.11.3` (`847611dcaa3bf0e2783335f961dd1fd0580e4d9f`) to final head `d7003009793d0a559dd93c791b531109af34f1da` passes. A separate stable checkout with frozen-lockfile dependencies created two real unresolved cleanup records, including the existing failed-bootstrap terminal shape. The candidate consumed those exact SQLite files through the existing backed-up Doctor migration: global state 22→39, agent 27→41, no migration warnings. Both full pre-migration backups pass integrity checks, and their lease/state/error rows match the stable producer.

After upgrade, both old leases and errors survive admission; the first reconciliation persists two parked diagnostics. Two complete store/service reopens each make zero provider calls and warnings. Explicit Stop with successful synthetic provider confirmation settles the normal row and preserves the original bootstrap failure on the failed terminal row; a terminal reopen stays silent. Both fresh producer/consumer commands exit 0. This is isolated database/service-owner proof with a synthetic provider, not a packaged CLI/full Gateway/model/cloud test. No new schema, credentials, or live-state change was required.

The final test-only `pnpm check:changed` replay again passes every affected check except the same 34 production/10 full-tree unused exports. Its ordered finding lists match the exact-parent reproduction byte-for-byte. The initial CI budget failure was addressed by test consolidation; final-head CI uses the ordinary gate, without an inherited-red bypass.
