issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Unrelated session metadata writes make background task PR subscriptions revalidate every watched audience.

**Outcome: not qualified for landing; closing unmerged.** The candidate removes measurable redundant work, but the fixed performance series showed higher median main-thread CPU and two valid pairs with unresolved tail-latency regressions. No change from this PR is being merged.

## User Impact

The proposed routing would reduce background PR subscription allocation. Correctness tests and exact-head CI pass, but the observed CPU/latency tradeoff does not meet the declared performance acceptance rule. Product behavior remains unchanged because the candidate is not landing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session writer already certifies when committed metadata leaves sharing and lineage unchanged. The subscription owner consumes that fact and the prepared session identity to select matching roots, aliases, and selected descendants. Changed or unknown facts remain broad. Receipt notifications remain broad because they can discover newly linked or newly visible children; the existing lifecycle/authority poll remains.

The candidate adds 32 runtime lines across existing owners, with no new cache, revision state, product configuration, or schema. A 22-line regression covers unrelated metadata, roots, and aliases. The committed benchmark/provider add bounded counters and real streamed turns, a native child spawn, receipt assertions, and separate CPU-profile capture.

## Evidence

A real isolated Gateway used 5,000 synthetic sessions, four connected clients, and eighteen subscription keys per client. Every sample completed 30 metadata writes, 10 measured turns, 31 provider responses/1,440 chunks, three concurrent streams, one native spawn, child completion, receipt delivery to every client, and unaffected-snapshot assertions.

The predeclared series completed all fourteen samples: two A/A controls, five serial alternating baseline/candidate pairs, and two separate CPU-profile passes. There were no retries or extra samples. Each run restored the same pristine fixture and verified source pins. Counter passes were separate. The local fixture has a 230 MB agent database; it does not establish 35-GiB/btrfs-scale performance.

| Work per minute, separate count pair | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Publication-row lookups | 16,324.6 | 11,871.9 |
| Key-state checks | 2,820.5 | 1,662.4 |
| Actual row captures | 181.8 | 167.5 |

Certified unchanged metadata scheduled 1,188 cells before versus 36 after. Unknown events still scheduled 954 cells, sharing-changing entry events 180, and receipt refreshes 54. Candidate received one additional legitimate sharing-changing replacement, correctly scheduling eighteen extra cells. Global sharing invalidation attempts were 379 versus 382; the optimization narrows subscription scheduling, not global authority retirement.

| Five-pair metric | Baseline median | Candidate median | Ratio-of-medians change | Median paired change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fixed-workload main CPU | 4,733.06 ms | 4,986.73 ms | +5.36% | +2.65% |
| Main CPU per minute | 4,858.28 ms | 5,115.99 ms | +5.30% | +2.55% |
| Fixed-workload total allocation | 1,143.86 MB | 1,129.18 MB | -1.28% | -0.30% |
| Total allocation per minute | 1,170.08 MB | 1,158.25 MB | -1.01% | -0.37% |
| PR-owner allocation per minute | 56.39 MB | 43.71 MB | -22.48% | -20.53% |

MB means decimal million bytes. A/A main CPU differed 2.58%, allocation 0.54%, and PR-owner allocation 3.98%; patch p95 differed 45.08% even without a code change. This is a limitation, not permission to discard unfavorable candidate samples.

| Valid adverse pair | Patch p95 | Turn p95 | Settlement p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 3 | 46.78 → 66.87 ms (+43.0%) | 1.98 → 2.67 s (+35.0%) | 2.44 → 2.39 s |
| 5 | 37.04 → 47.55 ms (+28.4%) | 1.93 → 3.98 s (+106.0%) | 2.19 → 5.07 s (+131.2%) |

The slower turns occurred in later streamed bursts after root warmup. Saved diagnostics show larger handler/database-worker delays, but do not establish their cause. Ambient load is a possible contributor, not causal exoneration. The stated rule treats a greater-than-20% adverse tail movement as a stop, so favorable allocation results do not qualify this candidate for landing.

The two CPU profiles were independently captured, but an unexplained equality in their inspector duration fields and sparse function samples limits interpretation. Sampled owner-time effects are held as exploratory; the main-thread CPU, counter, and heap-allocation measurements above are independent of those inspector timestamps.

Reproduce the committed workload after generating a private fixture and applying the synthetic model/provider configuration documented in the script header:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-pr-subscriptions-measure.ts \
  --root <private-fixture> --output <fresh-output> --port 42380 --mock-port 42381 \
  --clients 4 --keys 18 --operations 30 --subscribes 4 --mutation label \
  --turn-every 10 --interval-ms 2000 --mixed-invalidation --warmup-ms 10000
```

Baseline replay used byte-exact copies of the eight `benchmarkOwners` from `654789e8dc69e9fe4025473881dc64b7822bc46e` with `--owner-suffix lane2380-base`; candidate omitted the suffix. Add `--count-checks` only for the count passes and `--cpu-profile` only for the separate profile pair.

The new regression fails on the parent and passes with the candidate. Focused Gateway tests passed 94 cases with one existing skip; Chromium component tests passed 10/10; affected real-Gateway UI E2E passed 3/3. Final local Codex autoreview and hosted Codex review found no actionable defects. ClawSweeper reviewed exact head `d6b76ea6f23a81ea97f0563eb935543d1c547048` with no findings or open checkbox items. Exact-head CI run 42883523006, CodeQL, and build-artifact checks succeeded. None of these correctness results waives the failed performance qualification.

`pnpm check:changed --staged` completed. Candidate line-limit, type, and lint findings were repaired; the final repaired owner passed type-aware lint and formatting. Remaining dead-export findings reproduce on the exact parent and are tracked main regressions, not a green full local check.

<details><summary>Inherited dead-code gate attribution</summary>

All 33 candidate production export findings and all 10 full-tree findings reproduce on parent `654789e8dc69e9fe4025473881dc64b7822bc46e`. Introducing consumer/reachability changes: eight cold-start facade exports in #192552 (`625945b7ae01`); summary-heading helper in #196207 (`c7152f3bda8e`); two MCP directory helpers in #196252 (`80ba593b8b14`); billing helper in #191326 (`56617cd00086`); browser pairing constant in #191513 (`d85ebfe8daad`); four provider-auth types in #190544 (`cf1ae7bb6a72`); eleven lazy-provider facade exports in #190205 (`f63e5cd0f6d3`, prior counterfactual isolates all eleven); five ID helpers in #196380 (`37a3b162a0c5`). Affected owner blobs match the prior audited attribution.

Separate exact-parent unused-file checks reproduce three dynamic entrypoint modeling failures: benchmark/preload added by #196685 (`8743f1bfafa4`) and transport fixture added by #196501 (`09723cdcad18`). Parent also reports five additional Talk type exports absent from the candidate scan; the visibility difference is unexplained. No ignore expansion or unrelated export deletion is included.

</details>

comment.body:
Closing this candidate unmerged because it failed its declared performance qualification. The final count pair removes 27.3% of publication-row lookups, and five-pair median PR-owner allocation falls 22.5% per minute, but median main CPU rises 5.3%. Valid pairs 3 and 5 have unresolved adverse tails; pair 5 turn/settlement p95 rises 106%/131%.

All fourteen prescribed runs passed workload assertions, with no retries or discarded samples. The complete comparison, A/A controls, diagnostic limits, commands, and correctness/CI proof are in the PR body. Green correctness checks and zero code-review findings do not override this performance result. No merge was requested, and main is unchanged by this candidate.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes retained preparation state when a sandbox browser bridge stays cached after its initiating agent turn finishes.

## User Impact

Cached browser bridges release the originating turn's ambient async context while continuing to authenticate requests. No configuration, schema, or permission changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The HTTP listening handle inherited the preparation's AsyncLocalStorage scopes and kept them reachable for the server's lifetime. Start listening through the existing detached-context owner. issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway shutdown rejecting an old service-child cleanup error after the originating run has already finished, even when its native process tree has subsequently disappeared.

## User Impact

Later shutdown reports the earlier cleanup failure as a warning and can finish draining current work. The original run and scope still receive their failed cleanup result. A failure while shutdown is joining a current run still rejects shutdown.

## Why This Change Was Made

The supervisor already removes terminal cleanup attempts from its owned-run set, but its process-wide first-error latch was rethrown on every later shutdown. That historical diagnostic was therefore reported as live plugin-runtime ownership. Keep the diagnostic without replaying it as a new shutdown failure. Native signaling, descendant reaping, receipts, output drainage, and deadlines are unchanged; runtime production LOC is **-3**. Shutdown now calls the existing complete admission join once instead of wrapping it in a redundant outer retry loop.

The deadline's `pending` fields are negated conditions: `stdoutEnd:false` means stdout already ended. Linux descendant extinction is established by the subreaper's kernel wait returning ECHILD, independently of pipe EOF. Background `sleep`, `setsid`, and `nohup` remain owned and are reaped on cancellation.

## Evidence

- The new real Linux regression fails on base `6d811790acb43c46e3a7c950f22c3bed22b17f17`: pause only the fixture's native owner after root output, expire a 100ms cleanup budget, resume it, verify both owner and descendant disappear in `/proc`, then observe the old error incorrectly reject shutdown. The fixed code passes. Three additional real background-process controls pass (sleep, setsid, nohup).
- The existing supervisor regression also fails before the production change and passes afterward, preserving original run/scope errors and checking the historical shutdown warning. Existing tests still reject failures occurring during an active shutdown join.
- 104 focused tests pass across six supervisor, service-lifecycle, relay-host, and spawn-broker files on macOS. Four real Linux fixture cases pass in 1.55s of test time (4.46s shard wall time after shared worker preparation). The macOS combined run takes 139.73s including 87% worker compilation; no per-test timeout increase.
- Before/after owner probe: one warm-up, two A/A controls, three measured samples per side on isolated Linux aarch64 / Node 24.22.1. Stale shutdown rejection **3/3 → 0/3**. Final warm shutdown itself **0.02675 → 0.02713ms**. These noisy measurements support a correctness fix, not a speedup claim.
- A/A elapsed controls **158.294/161.483 → 154.224/160.339ms**; CPU **4.194/4.491 → 3.659/3.757ms**; sampled allocation **44,136/40,400 → 55,320/40,744B**. The fixed cold diagnostic import costs 6.83ms in the warm-up. The measured slice includes the intentional 100ms deadline and polling observation; CPU excludes descendant CPU. This owner does no database or workspace traversal.
- Test-line allocation grants exactly the **81 net added test lines** for the real process-tree regression/controls and historical warning assertion; the shared baseline is unchanged.

- Final Linux validation passes all five cases, including the existing subreaper fixture; final supervisor/readiness and relay-host reruns pass 43 + 41 cases. The minimal correction uses signal 35 and keeps the timeout and extinction assertions. It passes in 1.55s on the final source.

An independent clean checkout of exact parent `6d811790acb43c46e3a7c950f22c3bed22b17f17` reproduces identical normalized lists, with no resolution errors. issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Conversation-environment cleanup that exhausted its retry budget ran and warned again on every Gateway restart. Restart-resume summaries also counted parked sessions without saying why each session was parked.

## User Impact

Parked cleanup remains visible in environment/session status with an actionable inspection and explicit Stop retry. Restarts and background sweeps stop repeating the failed provider operation. Lease ownership remains until release is confirmed. Each parked restart-resume session gets one bounded `yield-waiting` diagnostic; that count describes surviving conversation wake sources, not environment cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Persist the parking decision in the existing environment diagnostic, remove the separate process-local display override, and skip parked attachments before session preparation. Explicit Stop retries cleanup and preserves the original bootstrap failure after successful release. Existing unparked records still receive a genuine recovery attempt before a new parking decision; there is no schema migration or new configuration.

Provider identity still matters: Machine0 is direct-only, so another backend's coordinator `not_found` cannot prove its resource is gone. Crabbox already accepts a verified released receipt before Machine0 authentication; existing strict release/absence confirmation remains unchanged. Operators repair the original provider account/state and explicitly retry Stop.

## Evidence

The owner regression failed before the fix with four provider destroys instead of one over three store reopens. Final consolidated cleanup tests: 21 passed; restart-resume: 29 passed; lifecycle/access siblings: 18 passed. The added parking cases cover both ten attempts and one hour, silent restart/sweep suppression, explicit retry, and preserved original bootstrap failure. Restart reason regressions failed in all three waiting scenarios before the diagnostic was added.

Five existing Crabbox stop-confirmation tests also pass (73 focused/sibling tests total). Both full-source Codex reviews and the test-consolidation review are clean at P0–P2. Formatting, lint, core/test/script typechecks, schema guards and import-cycle checks pass. `pnpm check:changed` fails only its dead-export audit: 34 production and 10 full-tree findings in untouched files. Main-isolate imports are warm; each sample reopens service/store and includes required worker re-admission. Both unresolved lease IDs and destroying states remain owned in every trial. issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #196743: ordinary `git rev-parse <missing-commit>:path` and `<missing-commit>^{tree}` bypass revision preparation, allowing Git's noop promisor fetch to retransmit existing commit/tree history.

## User Impact

Explicit content expressions use the existing negotiated missing-object fetch before native Git runs. ID-only expansion, optional defaults, metadata queries, offline probes, and implicit path arguments preserve native behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command dispatcher omitted ordinary rev-parse. The wrapper now lets offline native Git qualify its positional expressions in one batch. Valid expressions need one extra Git process, including a path whose blob is deliberately absent. On a miss, expressions are handled in order: qualify, acquire only necessary traversal roots through the existing owner, then qualify again before considering later arguments. This preserves Git's implicit transition from revisions to paths, instead of reproducing that parser in the wrapper.

Python subprocesses already inherit the installed shim through the exported agent PATH. The shared base checkout already resolves the same common Git directory as linked worktrees. This PR proves those paths without adding installation or detection mechanisms.

## Evidence

Each command-shape case uses a fresh explicitly unshallowed blobless clone with a registered linked worktree and an origin-only commit. Python cases run through the actual `createExecTool` shell wrapper, a heredoc, and `subprocess.run(["git", ...])`, with cwd at the base clone root.

| Requested check | Before | Final result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (a) Python → bare Git from base root | `show` and `cat-file -p <sha>:path` already negotiate | Pass through the installed PATH shim |
| (b) `rev-parse <sha>:path` | 16 objects, no haves | At most four objects, haves, correct blob OID |
| (b) `rev-parse <sha>^{tree}` | 16 objects, no haves | At most four objects, haves, correct tree OID |
| (b) `cat-file -p <sha>:path` | Already bounded | Pass with correct content |
| (c) Shared base root | Already detected | All Python cases pass at the root; linked-worktree controls retained |

The final owner suite passes 2/2. Native regressions also preserve unused defaults, ID-only two-dot endpoints and exclusions, mixed ID/content endpoints, three-dot traversal, implicit paths, invalid suffixes, empty arguments, and paths containing spaces. Before repair, the unused-default, two-dot, and implicit-path regressions each failed with an unnecessary rejected fetch. A missing-root/invalid-path case proves the wrapper stops before fetching a later unavailable object. Marker collision is covered.

Independent Codex review of the final staged candidate is scoped-clean through P2. Runtime delta is **+63 net lines**; regression delta **+64**, with an exact scoped allocation and shared fixture setup. Growth delegates argument acceptance to Git while preserving ordered acquisition; regular commands reuse their existing batched root checks and negotiated fetch. No persistent cache, new configuration, dependency, or UI import.

A separate network-disabled Linux fixture has 20,001 commits, 140,064 trees, and 62,000 metadata paths representing 1.116 GB of logical content. It is explicitly unshallowed, blobless, and shared with a linked worktree. No production data was used. Git 2.47.3, five counterbalanced 250-call batches per arm plus A2 controls:

| Present expression | Baseline → final median wall | Baseline → final CPU | Peak child RSS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HEAD^{tree}` | 1.519 → 3.115 ms | 1.481 → 3.033 ms | Unchanged, 5,226,496 B |
| `HEAD:path` with promised blob absent | 1.412 → 4.161 ms | 1.345 → 3.683 ms | Unchanged, 5,263,360 B |

Both cases run one probe plus the original Git command, with zero fetches, unchanged packs, correct output, and the promised blob still absent. Added median cost is 1.596/2.749 ms; relative cost is +105%/+195%. A/A median drift is 0.290/0.088 ms, and tails are host-noisy; this is not a production btrfs latency claim. Minor faults rise about 195→392 and 190→388 per call. A separate Git-only allocator-interposition run measures cumulative requested allocation: tree 379→770 requests and 899,273→1,799,642 bytes; promised blob 313→719 requests and 218,515→1,169,478 bytes. Five counterbalanced 20-call batches plus A2 match exactly. The nine-entrypoint qualification probe passes (nine calls/549 bytes). This excludes shell allocations, mmap, and hidden libc paths; requested bytes are not live heap or RSS. The original million-object transfer proof from #196743 was reused, not repeated.

`pnpm check:changed` reports 33 production and 10 full-tree unused exports outside changed files. The canonical checker reproduces identical symbol sets on exact parent `47b0ce478c8141b52ec4631b4ddbe3d8b018ff21` (zero script findings). All other checks passed, including the final repetition. Five additional production/two full-tree entries originate in #196380 / `37a3b162a0c58aaceb1634aaef726d0e178a529c`; unchanged findings and source attribution are documented in #196743. These are reported main regressions, not passing checks or noise. Earlier heads' CI was green.

Scope limit: optional `rev-parse --default` values and invocations containing newline arguments retain native handling and can still lazy-fetch. This follow-up protects the requested explicit revision forms and does not claim universal Git argument coverage.

Final-head CI run [42885010852](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42885010852), attempt 1, completed with one root failure: test-line ceiling in job 130071724878 (and aggregate 130077673436). CI tested merge `8b55bcb7f4425eeac0fdac47059e86ece31a27a4` of main `a693086999a4180f99a5b41555dcb70685b0312a` and this head. The merged tree has 6,635,240 test lines / 6,635,112 ceiling: 128 over. Exact main reproduces 6,635,176 / 6,635,048: the same 128 over. This PR's +64 lines and +64 scoped allocation leave the inherited debt unchanged. All other selected CI jobs pass.

The new main regression originates in #196346 / `b91520c16b620adf2222b6f9aa245d61b3e0d139`: +138 counted test lines without a grant consumed 10 lines of available slack, leaving 128 debt. Earlier #196680 debt had already been cleared; it is not the cause of this failure. Landing uses the authorized inherited-failure exception with exact-head evidence, while retaining the failed CI result.

ClawSweeper reviewed final head `fa0b3d4d91aff6676ff577ea81d3a2edc95bfb7a` with zero open items and no actionable findings. All three prior items were addressed by number in [the re-review response](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196784#issuecomment-6777072772).

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Colored, high-volume command output spends unnecessary main-thread CPU and allocation on each decoded chunk.

## User Impact

Exec output consumes substantially less CPU and transient memory while preserving the exact output, ANSI state, cursor-mode notifications, progress updates, and retained tails. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The streaming parser already handles each byte once and retains state across chunks; there is no accumulated-output rescan or duplicate completion pass. Its text state nevertheless appended one array element per visible character. Copying visible spans removes those allocations. Binary sanitization now matches only controls that need escaping, instead of invoking JavaScript for every preserved tab, newline and carriage return.

The production diff is +4 lines after formatting (including two required narrow control-regex lint annotations): one matcher and a span endpoint replace per-character appends. No cache or extra output owner is introduced. The two added contract table rows protect preserved whitespace/control boundaries and text around split CSI; their +2 lines and the +2-line intentional-regex inventory entry have an exact +4-line allocation. This is a performance repair, with no functional failure found; the contract cases protect unchanged behavior, with baseline equivalence established by the corpus comparison.

## Evidence

Acceptance selected before measurement: byte-identical output and lower CPU/allocation in five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, with A/A controls and no material regression in plain output or elapsed time.

The existing `scripts/perf/bash-output-measure.ts` now supports synthetic ANSI-colored pnpm/Vitest-style output, CR progress, tabs and binary noise. It exercises real subprocesses through the production supervisor, decoder, sanitizer, output registry, aggregate, tail and poll consumers. It does not claim a real Gateway/model round trip. Database size and workspace inventory are not inputs to this boundary.

Warm 50 MiB stream, 4096-byte producer writes, five pairs per phase, local macOS/Node 26.12.1. Allocation sampling runs separately from CPU timing. Host load was approximately 12/14/19.

| Metric | Baseline median (p95) | Candidate median (p95) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU ms/MiB | 16.185 (16.317) | 5.149 (5.244) |
| Sanitizer elapsed ms/MiB | 15.200 (15.278) | 4.261 (4.368) |
| Process CPU ms/MiB | 16.611 (16.772) | 5.535 (5.616) |
| Subprocess flow elapsed ms | 909.940 (915.719) | 358.383 (369.314) |
| Sampled allocated bytes/input byte | 43.039 | 10.553 |

Main-thread CPU improves 68.2%; allocation improves 75.5%. Main-thread sample ranges: baseline 15.988–16.317, candidate 5.019–5.244 ms/MiB. Two CPU A/A pairs drifted 0.36% and 0.16%; a separate allocation A/A pair measured 42.349/42.017 bytes per input byte (0.78% drift). Median event-loop p95: 32.571 → 10.387 ms; GC: 0.291 → 0.092 ms/MiB.

Additional boundary checks: 18 concurrent 1 MiB children, 17.467 → 6.228 main-thread CPU ms/MiB; plain 50 MiB output, 2.603 → 2.533 ms/MiB. Separate 10 MiB CPU profiles confirm less sanitizer work; these profiled timings are excluded from the table.

Reproduce with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/bash-output-measure.ts --turns 1 --mib 50 --fixture ansi --phase cpu` (or `allocation`). `--sanitizer-module` selects a frozen baseline module; `--concurrency 18 --turns 18 --mib 1` covers interleaved children. `--verify-against` compares output and CSI callbacks against the baseline: 275 corpus entries spanning every Unicode code point and malformed/split ANSI, with chunk widths 1/2/7/64/4096. All compared outputs are identical.

Focused ANSI, shell-utils, exec-runtime and process-registry tests: 144 passed, 1 skipped; 56.55s wall including compilation. UI unit/browser checks: 19 passed, 4.73s wall. UI E2E logs lifecycle and chat tool-output fidelity: 3 passed, 159.19s including compilation and isolated Gateway startup. `pnpm check:changed` passed typechecks and structural ratchets but reported intentional-regex lint annotations (fixed and targeted lint passed) and inherited dead exports (reproduced on the exact parent). Test-line ratchet and diff whitespace checks passed. The UI E2E prerequisite completed the application and Control UI builds.

Independent Codex autoreview of the complete local diff against `654789e8dc69e9fe4025473881dc64b7822bc46e`, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Simplify pass retained only the owner optimizations, focused contract cases, and reproducible benchmark extensions. The comment-only lint repair also received a scoped-clean Codex P0–P2 review. Hosted ClawSweeper must show zero open items on the final head before merge.


<details>
<summary>Inherited local main regression: dead-export scan</summary>

The production/full-tree export scans fail with identical finding sets on this branch and exact main parent `654789e8dc69e9fe4025473881dc64b7822bc46e`: 34 reported entries, 33 distinct path/symbol pairs (one namespace-labeled duplicate). A separate clean parent checkout with frozen dependencies reproduced exit 1. This is a main regression, not noise; no dead-export ignore or baseline was added here. All other changed checks pass after the intentional-regex lint repair.

Source-history attribution (parent-relative consumer/export diffs):

| Introducing cutover | Flagged owner/group |
| --- | --- |
| #192552 (`625945b7ae01d`) | Models planning, client tool caps, session auth/model types, OOM spawn facades: consumers moved to core owners, old facades remained. |
| #196207 (`c7152f3bda8e5`) | `nestRequiredSummaryHeadings`: remaining use moved into its defining module. |
| #196380 (`37a3b162a0c58`) | Gateway key/keyfile helpers exported with only internal production calls. |
| #196252 (`80ba593b8b14b`) | MCP directory constant/sanitizer exported with only internal production calls. |
| #190544 (`cf1ae7bb6a729`) | Four auth-type barrel reexports retained after consumers moved to the type owner. |
| #191326 (`56617cd000864`) | Billing-warning helper exported with only an internal production caller. |
| #191513 (`d85ebfe8daad4`) | Browser-pair code length exported with only an internal caller. |
| #190205 (`f63e5cd0f6d38`) | Provider runtime dynamic namespace replaced with direct auth/catalog owners, leaving six facade exports unused and exposing older stale facades. |
| #132716 (`964fa991c0aff`), #139911 (`071f606eae77a`), `a7436c8b4a93b`, #129184 (`33d8f24c9926f`) | Earlier provider failover/external-auth/hook/model-reference cutovers left the remaining stale facade exports. |

These are source-level causal attributions, not claims of historical Knip bisects. Removing the broad provider namespace in #190205 may be the scanner visibility trigger for its older stale facades. Exact-parent reproduction establishes inheritance of the current failure.

</details>

CI follow-up: initial head 0f41eaa failed the production lint-suppression inventory; the exact shell-utils control-regex entry is now recorded and all 14 guard tests pass (7.16s wall). This repair passed an independent Codex P0–P2 review. issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #196743: ordinary `git rev-parse <missing-commit>:path` and `<missing-commit>^{tree}` bypass revision preparation, allowing Git's noop promisor fetch to retransmit existing commit/tree history.

## User Impact

Explicit content expressions use the existing negotiated missing-object fetch before native Git runs. ID-only expansion, optional defaults, metadata queries, offline probes, and implicit path arguments preserve native behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command dispatcher omitted ordinary rev-parse. The wrapper now lets offline native Git qualify its positional expressions in one batch. Valid expressions need one extra Git process, including a path whose blob is deliberately absent. On a miss, expressions are handled in order: qualify, acquire only necessary traversal roots through the existing owner, then qualify again before considering later arguments. This preserves Git's implicit transition from revisions to paths, instead of reproducing that parser in the wrapper.

Python subprocesses already inherit the installed shim through the exported agent PATH. The shared base checkout already resolves the same common Git directory as linked worktrees. This PR proves those paths without adding installation or detection mechanisms.

## Evidence

Each command-shape case uses a fresh explicitly unshallowed blobless clone with a registered linked worktree and an origin-only commit. Python cases run through the actual `createExecTool` shell wrapper, a heredoc, and `subprocess.run(["git", ...])`, with cwd at the base clone root.

| Requested check | Before | Final result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (a) Python → bare Git from base root | `show` and `cat-file -p <sha>:path` already negotiate | Pass through the installed PATH shim |
| (b) `rev-parse <sha>:path` | 16 objects, no haves | At most four objects, haves, correct blob OID |
| (b) `rev-parse <sha>^{tree}` | 16 objects, no haves | At most four objects, haves, correct tree OID |
| (b) `cat-file -p <sha>:path` | Already bounded | Pass with correct content |
| (c) Shared base root | Already detected | All Python cases pass at the root; linked-worktree controls retained |

The final owner suite passes 2/2. Native regressions also preserve unused defaults, ID-only two-dot endpoints and exclusions, mixed ID/content endpoints, three-dot traversal, implicit paths, invalid suffixes, empty arguments, and paths containing spaces. Before repair, the unused-default, two-dot, and implicit-path regressions each failed with an unnecessary rejected fetch. A missing-root/invalid-path case proves the wrapper stops before fetching a later unavailable object. Marker collision is covered.

Independent Codex review of the final staged candidate is scoped-clean through P2. Runtime delta is **+63 net lines**; regression delta **+64**, with an exact scoped allocation and shared fixture setup. Growth delegates argument acceptance to Git while preserving ordered acquisition; regular commands reuse their existing batched root checks and negotiated fetch. No persistent cache, new configuration, dependency, or UI import.

A separate network-disabled Linux fixture has 20,001 commits, 140,064 trees, and 62,000 metadata paths representing 1.116 GB of logical content. It is explicitly unshallowed, blobless, and shared with a linked worktree. No production data was used. Git 2.47.3, five counterbalanced 250-call batches per arm plus A2 controls:

| Present expression | Baseline → final median wall | Baseline → final CPU | Peak child RSS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HEAD^{tree}` | 1.519 → 3.115 ms | 1.481 → 3.033 ms | Unchanged, 5,226,496 B |
| `HEAD:path` with promised blob absent | 1.412 → 4.161 ms | 1.345 → 3.683 ms | Unchanged, 5,263,360 B |

Both cases run one probe plus the original Git command, with zero fetches, unchanged packs, correct output, and the promised blob still absent. Added median cost is 1.596/2.749 ms; relative cost is +105%/+195%. A/A median drift is 0.290/0.088 ms, and tails are host-noisy; this is not a production btrfs latency claim. Minor faults rise about 195→392 and 190→388 per call. A separate Git-only allocator-interposition run measures cumulative requested allocation: tree 379→770 requests and 899,273→1,799,642 bytes; promised blob 313→719 requests and 218,515→1,169,478 bytes. Five counterbalanced 20-call batches plus A2 match exactly. The nine-entrypoint qualification probe passes (nine calls/549 bytes). This excludes shell allocations, mmap, and hidden libc paths; requested bytes are not live heap or RSS. The original million-object transfer proof from #196743 was reused, not repeated.

`pnpm check:changed` reports 33 production and 10 full-tree unused exports outside changed files. The canonical checker reproduces identical symbol sets on exact parent `47b0ce478c8141b52ec4631b4ddbe3d8b018ff21` (zero script findings). All other checks passed, including the final repetition. Five additional production/two full-tree entries originate in #196380 / `37a3b162a0c58aaceb1634aaef726d0e178a529c`; unchanged findings and source attribution are documented in #196743. These are reported main regressions, not passing checks or noise. Earlier heads' CI was green.

Scope limit: optional `rev-parse --default` values and invocations containing newline arguments retain native handling and can still lazy-fetch. This follow-up protects the requested explicit revision forms and does not claim universal Git argument coverage.

Final-head CI run [42885010852](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42885010852), attempt 1, completed with one root failure: test-line ceiling in job 130071724878 (and aggregate 130077673436). CI tested merge `8b55bcb7f4425eeac0fdac47059e86ece31a27a4` of main `a693086999a4180f99a5b41555dcb70685b0312a` and this head. The merged tree has 6,635,240 test lines / 6,635,112 ceiling: 128 over. Exact main reproduces 6,635,176 / 6,635,048: the same 128 over. This PR's +64 lines and +64 scoped allocation leave the inherited debt unchanged. All other selected CI jobs pass.

The new main regression originates in #196346 / `b91520c16b620adf2222b6f9aa245d61b3e0d139`: +138 counted test lines without a grant consumed 10 lines of available slack, leaving 128 debt. Earlier #196680 debt had already been cleared; it is not the cause of this failure. Landing uses the authorized inherited-failure exception with exact-head evidence, while retaining the failed CI result.

ClawSweeper reviewed final head `fa0b3d4d91aff6676ff577ea81d3a2edc95bfb7a` with zero open items and no actionable findings. All three prior items were addressed by number in [the re-review response](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196784#issuecomment-6777072772).

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway shutdown rejecting an old service-child cleanup error after the originating run has already finished, even when its native process tree has subsequently disappeared.

## User Impact

Later shutdown reports the earlier cleanup failure as a warning and can finish draining current work. The original run and scope still receive their failed cleanup result. A failure while shutdown is joining a current run still rejects shutdown.

## Why This Change Was Made

The supervisor already removes terminal cleanup attempts from its owned-run set, but its process-wide first-error latch was rethrown on every later shutdown. That historical diagnostic was therefore reported as live plugin-runtime ownership. Keep the diagnostic without replaying it as a new shutdown failure. Native signaling, descendant reaping, receipts, output drainage, and deadlines are unchanged; runtime production LOC is **-3**. Shutdown now calls the existing complete admission join once instead of wrapping it in a redundant outer retry loop.

The deadline's `pending` fields are negated conditions: `stdoutEnd:false` means stdout already ended. Linux descendant extinction is established by the subreaper's kernel wait returning ECHILD, independently of pipe EOF. Background `sleep`, `setsid`, and `nohup` remain owned and are reaped on cancellation.

## Evidence

- The new real Linux regression fails on base `6d811790acb43c46e3a7c950f22c3bed22b17f17`: pause only the fixture's native owner after root output, expire a 100ms cleanup budget, resume it, verify both owner and descendant disappear in `/proc`, then observe the old error incorrectly reject shutdown. The fixed code passes. Three additional real background-process controls pass (sleep, setsid, nohup).
- The existing supervisor regression also fails before the production change and passes afterward, preserving original run/scope errors and checking the historical shutdown warning. Existing tests still reject failures occurring during an active shutdown join.
- 104 focused tests pass across six supervisor, service-lifecycle, relay-host, and spawn-broker files on macOS. Four real Linux fixture cases pass in 1.55s of test time (4.46s shard wall time after shared worker preparation). The macOS combined run takes 139.73s including 87% worker compilation; no per-test timeout increase.
- Before/after owner probe: one warm-up, two A/A controls, three measured samples per side on isolated Linux aarch64 / Node 24.22.1. Median cancellation-through-retirement-and-shutdown: **162.047 → 155.379ms**; maximum **163.213 → 164.438ms**. Parent CPU **4.243 → 4.084ms**; sampled JavaScript allocations **56,184 → 49,848B**. Stale shutdown rejection **3/3 → 0/3**. Final warm shutdown itself **0.02675 → 0.02713ms**. These noisy measurements support a correctness fix, not a speedup claim.
- A/A elapsed controls **158.294/161.483 → 154.224/160.339ms**; CPU **4.194/4.491 → 3.659/3.757ms**; sampled allocation **44,136/40,400 → 55,320/40,744B**. The fixed cold diagnostic import costs 6.83ms in the warm-up. The measured slice includes the intentional 100ms deadline and polling observation; CPU excludes descendant CPU. This owner does no database or workspace traversal.
- Test-line allocation grants exactly the **81 net added test lines** for the real process-tree regression/controls and historical warning assertion; the shared baseline is unchanged.

- Final Linux validation passes all five cases, including the existing subreaper fixture; final supervisor/readiness and relay-host reruns pass 43 + 41 cases. Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, the line cap, core production typecheck, and all core test typecheck shards pass. A provisional local rerun was invalidated when the signal fixture changed during compilation; its frozen-source relay rerun passes all 41 cases.
- The additional native fixture failure reproduced on the exact main parent: Node 24.22.1 Linux ARM64 ignores signal 34 (confirmed from the child's SigIgn mask), so the fixture from #168942 (`698cac4c78b806`) never killed its child. The minimal correction uses signal 35 and keeps the timeout and extinction assertions. It passes in 1.55s on the final source.
- `pnpm check:changed` reports unrelated dead exports: **34 production / 10 full-tree / 0 script**. An independent clean checkout of exact parent `6d811790acb43c46e3a7c950f22c3bed22b17f17` reproduces identical normalized lists, with no resolution errors. The initial line-count finding in the changed supervisor was corrected and its lint/line-cap gates pass. The full changed-file command is recorded as failed, not relabeled green.
- The additional main unused-export regression is `projectLeaseDiagnosticFrames`, introduced by **#196724 / `2c4e34a72f490`**: the new helper is exported but only tests import it externally. Prior 33/10 findings trace to #196207, #192552, #196252, #191326, #190205, #132716, #139911, #129184, direct commit `a7436c8b4a93`, #190544, #191513, and #196380; their established causal cutovers were reused. None involves this change's exports.

Final Codex autoreview of the full local diff against `6d811790acb43` is **scoped-clean through P2**, with complete supervisor context and no accepted/actionable findings. The originating production native stall is not established by this fixture. No production deployment or live-data copying occurred.

The initial PR CI exposed five stale historical-shutdown assertions. Commit `192617895f7d0` updates the CLI construction, one-shot tools, forced settlement, and source-loaded matrix consumers to retain failure on the original run/scope and let later shutdown finish. The awaited-output fixture now starts shutdown before injecting failure, preserving active-join rejection coverage. All five files pass locally on Linux (16 tests); final awaited-output also passes all eight tests on macOS. Focused lint, formatting, tooling typecheck, and fresh Codex autoreview through P2 pass. This follow-up adds zero test lines and changes no production code.

Initial CI run `42884793648` also fails the test-line ratchet by **128 lines** on merge `656842736defbeab7a3351a3672c5e465e586bad`. This is independently reproduced on exact main parent `924a3bc9ffb3d359fc3a8709768ef0e2fa305d91` (6,635,176 total / 6,635,048 ceiling). Causal proof: **#196346 / `b91520c16b620adf2222b6f9aa245d61b3e0d139`** adds 138 test lines without allocation; its parent `e2c3702f6758760842dc649232188873e273b100` passes with ten lines slack, and the introducing commit fails by 128. This PR adds exactly 81 lines and 81 allocation, preserving that debt. This is a main regression for follow-up, not a passing broad gate.

Final-head status at `192617895f7d0065115abe7f4c95683f8ffc75bc`: [CI run42887726734](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42887726734) is complete. The pinned-head inherited-failure exception is selected; failed CI is not represented as green. issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes host disk and I/O stalls when an agent command crashes and inherits the Gateway’s unlimited core-size limit.

## User Impact

Linux agent commands and descendants receive a zero core-size limit, while the Gateway, spawn broker and internal workers retain their crash diagnostics. This covers ordinary and durable host commands, execa, PTYs and default Docker sandbox limits. Explicit sandbox `docker.ulimits.core` overrides remain supported.

Linux host execution requires util-linux `prlimit` in a trusted system directory (including the NixOS system profile). The kernel limit prevents direct-file cores; Linux pipe-based collectors apply their own policy. No host configuration or retention changes are made.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the existing agent execution intent before the dedicated command owner execs, with the same preparation for execa and PTY targets. `prlimit` execs in place and never changes the Gateway or broker limits. The dedicated anchor retains the target’s exact environment and custom `argv0`; the generic raw-spawn transport remains unchanged. Durable units receive `LimitCORE=0`, and the sandbox default participates in its existing reuse hash.

Production growth is 38 lines for the shared invocation preparation and owner wiring. No new configuration option, cache, schema or dependency package. The 106-line regression allocation covers a seeded positive parent limit, descendant inheritance, preserved internal limits/argv0, sandbox defaults/overrides the durable-unit contract, and NixOS binary resolution/missing dependency guidance.

## Evidence

- The seeded-limit regression is red on parent `ecbad2efa1d7e89d041965612b2237760a024c50` and green on the candidate. Agent root/descendant limits become `0/0`; parent/internal limits and custom target `argv0` remain intact.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway shutdown can report `Plugin runtime still owns resources ... | service child cleanup identity lost: write EPIPE` when a service child exits while its stdin shutdown notification is being delivered.

## User Impact

Shutdown accepts completed child cleanup when the existing process owner verifies it. A missing closing receipt, lost lineage, or unverifiable process tree still fails cleanup. No configuration, schema, timeout, or public API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stdin-end rejection permanently discarded cleanup authority before the closing receipt and native exit could settle. It now records the transport error and joins the existing bounded authority-close path. The same callback handles the existing control-stream and closing-acknowledgement errors; runtime production LOC is net zero.

The apparent plugin-close delay is separate: `plugin-registry` and `plugin-metadata` spans include process-supervisor and database closure. Disposal is already concurrent. Existing span evidence attributes 4,929ms of a 5,116ms metadata close to agent databases; no plugin scheduling change is justified. The database's internal wait remains unproven and is not fixed here.

Unrelated session metadata writes make background task PR subscriptions revalidate every watched audience.

**Outcome: not qualified for landing; closing unmerged.** The candidate removes measurable redundant work, but the fixed performance series showed higher median main-thread CPU and two valid pairs with unresolved tail-latency regressions. No change from this PR is being merged.

## User Impact

The proposed routing would reduce background PR subscription allocation. Correctness tests and exact-head CI pass, but the observed CPU/latency tradeoff does not meet the declared performance acceptance rule. Product behavior remains unchanged because the candidate is not landing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session writer already certifies when committed metadata leaves sharing and lineage unchanged. The subscription owner consumes that fact and the prepared session identity to select matching roots, aliases, and selected descendants. Changed or unknown facts remain broad. Receipt notifications remain broad because they can discover newly linked or newly visible children; the existing lifecycle/authority poll remains.

The candidate adds 32 runtime lines across existing owners, with no new cache, revision state, product configuration, or schema. A 22-line regression covers unrelated metadata, roots, and aliases. The committed benchmark/provider add bounded counters and real streamed turns, a native child spawn, receipt assertions, and separate CPU-profile capture.

## Evidence

A real isolated Gateway used 5,000 synthetic sessions, four connected clients, and eighteen subscription keys per client. Every sample completed 30 metadata writes, 10 measured turns, 31 provider responses/1,440 chunks, three concurrent streams, one native spawn, child completion, receipt delivery to every client, and unaffected-snapshot assertions.

The predeclared series completed all fourteen samples: two A/A controls, five serial alternating baseline/candidate pairs, and two separate CPU-profile passes. There were no retries or extra samples. Each run restored the same pristine fixture and verified source pins. Counter passes were separate. The local fixture has a 230 MB agent database; it does not establish 35-GiB/btrfs-scale performance.

Candidate received one additional legitimate sharing-changing replacement, correctly scheduling eighteen extra cells. Global sharing invalidation attempts were 379 versus 382; the optimization narrows subscription scheduling, not global authority retirement.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #196743: ordinary `git rev-parse <missing-commit>:path` and `<missing-commit>^{tree}` bypass revision preparation, allowing Git's noop promisor fetch to retransmit existing commit/tree history.

## User Impact

Explicit content expressions use the existing negotiated missing-object fetch before native Git runs. ID-only expansion, optional defaults, metadata queries, offline probes, and implicit path arguments preserve native behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command dispatcher omitted ordinary rev-parse. The wrapper now lets offline native Git qualify its positional expressions in one batch. Valid expressions need one extra Git process, including a path whose blob is deliberately absent. On a miss, expressions are handled in order: qualify, acquire only necessary traversal roots through the existing owner, then qualify again before considering later arguments. This preserves Git's implicit transition from revisions to paths, instead of reproducing that parser in the wrapper.

Python subprocesses already inherit the installed shim through the exported agent PATH. The shared base checkout already resolves the same common Git directory as linked worktrees. This PR proves those paths without adding installation or detection mechanisms.

## Evidence

Each command-shape case uses a fresh explicitly unshallowed blobless clone with a registered linked worktree and an origin-only commit. Python cases run through the actual `createExecTool` shell wrapper, a heredoc, and `subprocess.run(["git", ...])`, with cwd at the base clone root.

| Requested check | Before | Final result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (a) Python → bare Git from base root | `show` and `cat-file -p <sha>:path` already negotiate | Pass through the installed PATH shim |
| (b) `rev-parse <sha>:path` | 16 objects, no haves | At most four objects, haves, correct blob OID |
| (b) `rev-parse <sha>^{tree}` | 16 objects, no haves | At most four objects, haves, correct tree OID |
| (b) `cat-file -p <sha>:path` | Already bounded | Pass with correct content |
| (c) Shared base root | Already detected | All Python cases pass at the root; linked-worktree controls retained |

The final owner suite passes 2/2. Native regressions also preserve unused defaults, ID-only two-dot endpoints and exclusions, mixed ID/content endpoints, three-dot traversal, implicit paths, invalid suffixes, empty arguments, and paths containing spaces. Before repair, the unused-default, two-dot, and implicit-path regressions each failed with an unnecessary rejected fetch. A missing-root/invalid-path case proves the wrapper stops before fetching a later unavailable object. Marker collision is covered.

Independent Codex review of the final staged candidate is scoped-clean through P2. Runtime delta is **+63 net lines**; regression delta **+64**, with an exact scoped allocation and shared fixture setup. Growth delegates argument acceptance to Git while preserving ordered acquisition; regular commands reuse their existing batched root checks and negotiated fetch. No persistent cache, new configuration, dependency, or UI import.

A separate network-disabled Linux fixture has 20,001 commits, 140,064 trees, and 62,000 metadata paths representing 1.116 GB of logical content. It is explicitly unshallowed, blobless, and shared with a linked worktree. No production data was used. Git 2.47.3, five counterbalanced 250-call batches per arm plus A2 controls:

| Present expression | Baseline → final median wall | Baseline → final CPU | Peak child RSS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HEAD^{tree}` | 1.519 → 3.115 ms | 1.481 → 3.033 ms | Unchanged, 5,226,496 B |
| `HEAD:path` with promised blob absent | 1.412 → 4.161 ms | 1.345 → 3.683 ms | Unchanged, 5,263,360 B |

Both cases run one probe plus the original Git command, with zero fetches, unchanged packs, correct output, and the promised blob still absent. Added median cost is 1.596/2.749 ms; relative cost is +105%/+195%. A/A median drift is 0.290/0.088 ms, and tails are host-noisy; this is not a production btrfs latency claim. Minor faults rise about 195→392 and 190→388 per call. A separate Git-only allocator-interposition run measures cumulative requested allocation: tree 379→770 requests and 899,273→1,799,642 bytes; promised blob 313→719 requests and 218,515→1,169,478 bytes. Five counterbalanced 20-call batches plus A2 match exactly. The nine-entrypoint qualification probe passes (nine calls/549 bytes). This excludes shell allocations, mmap, and hidden libc paths; requested bytes are not live heap or RSS. The original million-object transfer proof from #196743 was reused, not repeated.

`pnpm check:changed` reports 33 production and 10 full-tree unused exports outside changed files. The canonical checker reproduces identical symbol sets on exact parent `47b0ce478c8141b52ec4631b4ddbe3d8b018ff21` (zero script findings). All other checks passed, including the final repetition. Five additional production/two full-tree entries originate in #196380 / `37a3b162a0c58aaceb1634aaef726d0e178a529c`; unchanged findings and source attribution are documented in #196743. These are reported main regressions, not passing checks or noise. Earlier heads' CI was green.

Scope limit: optional `rev-parse --default` values and invocations containing newline arguments retain native handling and can still lazy-fetch. This follow-up protects the requested explicit revision forms and does not claim universal Git argument coverage.

Final-head CI run [42885010852](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42885010852), attempt 1, completed with one root failure: test-line ceiling in job 130071724878 (and aggregate 130077673436). issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A checkpoint pause can still take seconds after atomic snapshot capture was introduced. Existing pause logs do not show whether a checkpoint used a snapshot, selected direct capture, or fell back because its source could not be snapshotted. They also cannot separate snapshot creation from work before capture and runtime resume.

## User Impact

Each attempted checkpoint reports a bounded capture path and reason in its existing owner log. The rendered message retains these facts in plain journals, including an attempted snapshot followed by nested-subvolume fallback. Operation-local timings distinguish pre-copy settlement, the native copy helper, post-copy inspection, and resume. No paths, file contents, new scan, cache, schema or configuration are added.

This is diagnostic visibility, not a claim that copy time measures a particular syscall or dirty writeback. Existing capture selection, fallback, canonical acceptance and read-after-command behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follow-up to #196662 and #196727. Read-only inspection of the affected production workspaces found btrfs subvolume roots, so the non-subvolume eligibility guard does not explain the observed slow pauses. Two slow workspaces contain roughly 240k–288k filesystem entries and 4.1–5.9 GB, substantially more than the 62k-file/1.1 GB synthetic fixture. No immediate resume/re-pause signature established nested fallback; these observations do not prove its absence or attribute a syscall delay.

The historical 21-second pause predates snapshot capture. Its owner-level cause was synchronization under pause, while its lower-level time distribution is unavailable. The new diagnostics make future capture-path and phase attribution possible without adding production tracing.

## Evidence

The checkpoint owner suite exercises adaptive direct capture, successful snapshots, unavailable clone capability, non-subvolume roots, clone failure, nested fallback, interrupted acceptance and cleanup overlap. The log observer runs synchronously at the owner boundary, allowing emission ordering and canonical consistency to be checked together. The corrected final observer fails on exact parent d7f90ec because no capture record is emitted, then passes on the restored candidate. All 12 focused cases pass; the final observer wiring is additionally verified by the restored small-workspace case. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2. `pnpm build:runtime` passes.

Production growth is 59 lines for an operation-local bounded reason/timing record and one rendered log; no extra scan or probe is introduced. Regression growth is 83 lines, allocated to the existing test budget; the guard passes with seven lines of slack. No UI-imported module changes.

`pnpm check:changed --base d7f90ec35cffc25b8472ac1aa0d9ed871aafd907` completed: every category passes except the unused-export scans (33 production / 10 full-tree). Five production entries and two full-tree entries beyond the earlier 28/8 set were introduced by #196380 (`37a3b162a0c58aaceb1634aaef726d0e178a529c`); the changed diagnostic owners are not among them. The prior set retains its previously established introducing commits. These are main regressions. Both failed Knip commands reproduce on exact parent d7f90ec with identical normalized 33/10 sets and no resolution errors. The parent archive verified all 66,362 tracked blobs; isolated dependency copies resolve workspace links into that parent, not the candidate. Only the two failed scans were replayed.

The preserved native fixture remains available, but a bounded readiness check found concurrent host activity exceeding its quiet limits. No timing campaign was started, and no new performance claim depends on it. No production restart, configuration change, deployment, tracing or data copy was performed.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #196743: ordinary `git rev-parse <missing-commit>:path` and `<missing-commit>^{tree}` bypass revision preparation, allowing Git's noop promisor fetch to retransmit existing commit/tree history.

## User Impact

Explicit content expressions use the existing negotiated missing-object fetch before native Git runs. ID-only expansion, optional defaults, metadata queries, offline probes, and implicit path arguments preserve native behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command dispatcher omitted ordinary rev-parse. The wrapper now lets offline native Git qualify its positional expressions in one batch. Valid expressions need one extra Git process, including a path whose blob is deliberately absent. On a miss, expressions are handled in order: qualify, acquire only necessary traversal roots through the existing owner, then qualify again before considering later arguments. This preserves Git's implicit transition from revisions to paths, instead of reproducing that parser in the wrapper.

Python subprocesses already inherit the installed shim through the exported agent PATH. The shared base checkout already resolves the same common Git directory as linked worktrees. This PR proves those paths without adding installation or detection mechanisms.

## Evidence

Each command-shape case uses a fresh explicitly unshallowed blobless clone with a registered linked worktree and an origin-only commit. Python cases run through the actual `createExecTool` shell wrapper, a heredoc, and `subprocess.run(["git", ...])`, with cwd at the base clone root.

| Requested check | Before | Final result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (a) Python → bare Git from base root | `show` and `cat-file -p <sha>:path` already negotiate | Pass through the installed PATH shim |
| (b) `rev-parse <sha>:path` | 16 objects, no haves | At most four objects, haves, correct blob OID |
| (b) `rev-parse <sha>^{tree}` | 16 objects, no haves | At most four objects, haves, correct tree OID |
| (b) `cat-file -p <sha>:path` | Already bounded | Pass with correct content |
| (c) Shared base root | Already detected | All Python cases pass at the root; linked-worktree controls retained |

The final owner suite passes 2/2. Native regressions also preserve unused defaults, ID-only two-dot endpoints and exclusions, mixed ID/content endpoints, three-dot traversal, implicit paths, invalid suffixes, empty arguments, and paths containing spaces. Before repair, the unused-default, two-dot, and implicit-path regressions each failed with an unnecessary rejected fetch. A missing-root/invalid-path case proves the wrapper stops before fetching a later unavailable object. Marker collision is covered.

Independent Codex review of the final staged candidate is scoped-clean through P2. Runtime delta is **+63 net lines**; regression delta **+64**, with an exact scoped allocation and shared fixture setup. Growth delegates argument acceptance to Git while preserving ordered acquisition; regular commands reuse their existing batched root checks and negotiated fetch. No persistent cache, new configuration, dependency, or UI import.

A separate network-disabled Linux fixture has 20,001 commits, 140,064 trees, and 62,000 metadata paths representing 1.116 GB of logical content. It is explicitly unshallowed, blobless, and shared with a linked worktree. No production data was used. Git 2.47.3, five counterbalanced 250-call batches per arm plus A2 controls:

| Present expression | Baseline → final median wall | Baseline → final CPU | Peak child RSS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HEAD^{tree}` | 1.519 → 3.115 ms | 1.481 → 3.033 ms | Unchanged, 5,226,496 B |
| `HEAD:path` with promised blob absent | 1.412 → 4.161 ms | 1.345 → 3.683 ms | Unchanged, 5,263,360 B |

Both cases run one probe plus the original Git command, with zero fetches, unchanged packs, correct output, and the promised blob still absent. Added median cost is 1.596/2.749 ms; relative cost is +105%/+195%. A/A median drift is 0.290/0.088 ms, and tails are host-noisy; this is not a production btrfs latency claim. Minor faults rise about 195→392 and 190→388 per call. A separate Git-only allocator-interposition run measures cumulative requested allocation: tree 379→770 requests and 899,273→1,799,642 bytes; promised blob 313→719 requests and 218,515→1,169,478 bytes. Five counterbalanced 20-call batches plus A2 match exactly. The nine-entrypoint qualification probe passes (nine calls/549 bytes). issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Colored, high-volume command output spends unnecessary main-thread CPU and allocation on each decoded chunk.

## User Impact

Exec output consumes substantially less CPU and transient memory while preserving the exact output, ANSI state, cursor-mode notifications, progress updates, and retained tails. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The streaming parser already handles each byte once and retains state across chunks; there is no accumulated-output rescan or duplicate completion pass. Its text state nevertheless appended one array element per visible character. Copying visible spans removes those allocations. Binary sanitization now matches only controls that need escaping, instead of invoking JavaScript for every preserved tab, newline and carriage return.

The production diff is +4 lines after formatting (including two required narrow control-regex lint annotations): one matcher and a span endpoint replace per-character appends. No cache or extra output owner is introduced. The two added contract table rows protect preserved whitespace/control boundaries and text around split CSI; their +2 lines and the +2-line intentional-regex inventory entry have an exact +4-line allocation. This is a performance repair, with no functional failure found; the contract cases protect unchanged behavior, with baseline equivalence established by the corpus comparison.

## Evidence

Acceptance selected before measurement: byte-identical output and lower CPU/allocation in five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, with A/A controls and no material regression in plain output or elapsed time.

The existing `scripts/perf/bash-output-measure.ts` now supports synthetic ANSI-colored pnpm/Vitest-style output, CR progress, tabs and binary noise. It exercises real subprocesses through the production supervisor, decoder, sanitizer, output registry, aggregate, tail and poll consumers. It does not claim a real Gateway/model round trip. Database size and workspace inventory are not inputs to this boundary.

Warm 50 MiB stream, 4096-byte producer writes, five pairs per phase, local macOS/Node 26.12.1. Allocation sampling runs separately from CPU timing. Host load was approximately 12/14/19.

| Metric | Baseline median (p95) | Candidate median (p95) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU ms/MiB | 16.185 (16.317) | 5.149 (5.244) |
| Sanitizer elapsed ms/MiB | 15.200 (15.278) | 4.261 (4.368) |
| Process CPU ms/MiB | 16.611 (16.772) | 5.535 (5.616) |
| Subprocess flow elapsed ms | 909.940 (915.719) | 358.383 (369.314) |
| Sampled allocated bytes/input byte | 43.039 | 10.553 |

Main-thread CPU improves 68.2%; allocation improves 75.5%. Main-thread sample ranges: baseline 15.988–16.317, candidate 5.019–5.244 ms/MiB. Two CPU A/A pairs drifted 0.36% and 0.16%; a separate allocation A/A pair measured 42.349/42.017 bytes per input byte (0.78% drift). Median event-loop p95: 32.571 → 10.387 ms; GC: 0.291 → 0.092 ms/MiB.

Additional boundary checks: 18 concurrent 1 MiB children, 17.467 → 6.228 main-thread CPU ms/MiB; plain 50 MiB output, 2.603 → 2.533 ms/MiB. Separate 10 MiB CPU profiles confirm less sanitizer work; these profiled timings are excluded from the table.

Reproduce with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/bash-output-measure.ts --turns 1 --mib 50 --fixture ansi --phase cpu` (or `allocation`). `--sanitizer-module` selects a frozen baseline module; `--concurrency 18 --turns 18 --mib 1` covers interleaved children. `--verify-against` compares output and CSI callbacks against the baseline: 275 corpus entries spanning every Unicode code point and malformed/split ANSI, with chunk widths 1/2/7/64/4096. All compared outputs are identical.

Focused ANSI, shell-utils, exec-runtime and process-registry tests: 144 passed, 1 skipped; 56.55s wall including compilation. UI unit/browser checks: 19 passed, 4.73s wall. UI E2E logs lifecycle and chat tool-output fidelity: 3 passed, 159.19s including compilation and isolated Gateway startup. `pnpm check:changed` passed typechecks and structural ratchets but reported intentional-regex lint annotations (fixed and targeted lint passed) and inherited dead exports (reproduced on the exact parent). Test-line ratchet and diff whitespace checks passed. The UI E2E prerequisite completed the application and Control UI builds.

Independent Codex autoreview of the complete local diff against `654789e8dc69e9fe4025473881dc64b7822bc46e`, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Simplify pass retained only the owner optimizations, focused contract cases, and reproducible benchmark extensions. The comment-only lint repair also received a scoped-clean Codex P0–P2 review. Hosted ClawSweeper must show zero open items on the final head before merge.


<details>
<summary>Inherited local main regression: dead-export scan</summary>

The production/full-tree export scans fail with identical finding sets on this branch and exact main parent `654789e8dc69e9fe4025473881dc64b7822bc46e`: 34 reported entries, 33 distinct path/symbol pairs (one namespace-labeled duplicate). A separate clean parent checkout with frozen dependencies reproduced exit 1. This is a main regression, not noise; no dead-export ignore or baseline was added here. All other changed checks pass after the intentional-regex lint repair.

Source-history attribution (parent-relative consumer/export diffs):

| Introducing cutover | Flagged owner/group |
| --- | --- |
| #192552 (`625945b7ae01d`) | Models planning, client tool caps, session auth/model types, OOM spawn facades: consumers moved to core owners, old facades remained. |
| #196207 (`c7152f3bda8e5`) | `nestRequiredSummaryHeadings`: remaining use moved into its defining module. |
| #196380 (`37a3b162a0c58`) | Gateway key/keyfile helpers exported with only internal production calls. |
| #196252 (`80ba593b8b14b`) | MCP directory constant/sanitizer exported with only internal production calls. |
| #190544 (`cf1ae7bb6a729`) | Four auth-type barrel reexports retained after consumers moved to the type owner. |
| #191326 (`56617cd000864`) | Billing-warning helper exported with only an internal production caller. |
| #191513 (`d85ebfe8daad4`) | Browser-pair code length exported with only an internal caller. |
| #190205 (`f63e5cd0f6d38`) | Provider runtime dynamic namespace replaced with direct auth/catalog owners, leaving six facade exports unused and exposing older stale facades. |
| #132716 (`964fa991c0aff`), #139911 (`071f606eae77a`), `a7436c8b4a93b`, #129184 (`33d8f24c9926f`) | Earlier provider failover/external-auth/hook/model-reference cutovers left the remaining stale facade exports. |

These are source-level causal attributions, not claims of historical Knip bisects. Removing the broad provider namespace in #190205 may be the scanner visibility trigger for its older stale facades. Exact-parent reproduction establishes inheritance of the current failure.

</details>

CI follow-up: initial head 0f41eaa failed the production lint-suppression inventory; the exact shell-utils control-regex entry is now recorded and all 14 guard tests pass (7.16s wall). This repair passed an independent Codex P0–P2 review. Initial CI also reported two worker containment error-text assertions and one sidebar test DOM-detachment error; both worker failures reproduce on exact parent 654789e8dc69e9fe4025473881dc64b7822bc46e (2 failed, 67 filtered; 72.45s including compilation). #194473 / 5d5c90e1e4e5a02faccf20c8f16d4ec6d9dad3a7 changed containment guidance to source-specific config/session messages but left the two expectations in worker-runtime-permissions.suite.ts:298 unchanged. This is another main regression for follow-up. The sidebar passed once on the parent (23.43s), which does not prove a fix or establish inheritance; its original CI error was a virtualized row detaching during scrollIntoViewIfNeeded. That failure remains an unproven intermittent test failure, not an inherited exception.

Final-head landing evidence: CI run [42871419991, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42871419991) completed at `034d4399a47d3bb85f1f43f625305ef1fcdd4f4e`. Its only failed root job is the two attributed worker assertions above; security, lint/type/guard jobs and UI E2E passed. Actual CI checkout `716e7da7b6d1d34de698b0f97eca6ede58816053` merges main `358722b1a46c58387f783f87b02b8299ea497df3` with the final head. The failing test and hint-owner blobs are identical in the reproduced original main parent, CI main parent and tested merge. The earlier sidebar failure did not recur; no fix is claimed. issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #196743: ordinary `git rev-parse <missing-commit>:path` and `<missing-commit>^{tree}` bypass revision preparation, allowing Git's noop promisor fetch to retransmit existing commit/tree history.

## User Impact

Explicit content expressions use the existing negotiated missing-object fetch before native Git runs. ID-only expansion, optional defaults, metadata queries, offline probes, and implicit path arguments preserve native behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command dispatcher omitted ordinary rev-parse. The wrapper now lets offline native Git qualify its positional expressions in one batch. Valid expressions need one extra Git process, including a path whose blob is deliberately absent. On a miss, expressions are handled in order: qualify, acquire only necessary traversal roots through the existing owner, then qualify again before considering later arguments. This preserves Git's implicit transition from revisions to paths, instead of reproducing that parser in the wrapper.

Python subprocesses already inherit the installed shim through the exported agent PATH. The shared base checkout already resolves the same common Git directory as linked worktrees. This PR proves those paths without adding installation or detection mechanisms.

## Evidence

Each command-shape case uses a fresh explicitly unshallowed blobless clone with a registered linked worktree and an origin-only commit. Python cases run through the actual `createExecTool` shell wrapper, a heredoc, and `subprocess.run(["git", ...])`, with cwd at the base clone root.

| Requested check | Before | Final result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (a) Python → bare Git from base root | `show` and `cat-file -p <sha>:path` already negotiate | Pass through the installed PATH shim |
| (b) `rev-parse <sha>:path` | 16 objects, no haves | At most four objects, haves, correct blob OID |
| (b) `rev-parse <sha>^{tree}` | 16 objects, no haves | At most four objects, haves, correct tree OID |
| (b) `cat-file -p <sha>:path` | Already bounded | Pass with correct content |
| (c) Shared base root | Already detected | All Python cases pass at the root; linked-worktree controls retained |

The final owner suite passes 2/2. Native regressions also preserve unused defaults, ID-only two-dot endpoints and exclusions, mixed ID/content endpoints, three-dot traversal, implicit paths, invalid suffixes, empty arguments, and paths containing spaces. Before repair, the unused-default, two-dot, and implicit-path regressions each failed with an unnecessary rejected fetch. A missing-root/invalid-path case proves the wrapper stops before fetching a later unavailable object. Marker collision is covered.

Independent Codex review of the final staged candidate is scoped-clean through P2. Runtime delta is **+63 net lines**; regression delta **+64**, with an exact scoped allocation and shared fixture setup. Growth delegates argument acceptance to Git while preserving ordered acquisition; regular commands reuse their existing batched root checks and negotiated fetch. No persistent cache, new configuration, dependency, or UI import.

A separate network-disabled Linux fixture has 20,001 commits, 140,064 trees, and 62,000 metadata paths representing 1.116 GB of logical content. It is explicitly unshallowed, blobless, and shared with a linked worktree. No production data was used. Git 2.47.3, five counterbalanced 250-call batches per arm plus A2 controls:

| Present expression | Baseline → final median wall | Baseline → final CPU | Peak child RSS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HEAD^{tree}` | 1.519 → 3.115 ms | 1.481 → 3.033 ms | Unchanged, 5,226,496 B |
| `HEAD:path` with promised blob absent | 1.412 → 4.161 ms | 1.345 → 3.683 ms | Unchanged, 5,263,360 B |

Both cases run one probe plus the original Git command, with zero fetches, unchanged packs, correct output, and the promised blob still absent.
