issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long CPU-profile batches pause a large Gateway to start profiling, then discard the entire capture when its graph exceeds the RPC response limits. This follows #196422: batching amortized startup, but its earlier 64–140-node fixture missed the large-graph refusal.

## User Impact

Explicit batches and oversized single profiles now return a private host-local `.cpuprofile` path, byte count, window boundaries and node/sample summary. Small single calls remain inline. Twelve or thirty five-second windows retain their complete sanitized timeline with one start/stop; operators retrieve the file from the Gateway host.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing capture owner streams sanitized JSON in chunks with a 64 MiB artifact cap. CPU and heap snapshots share diagnostics-directory reservation and owner-only permissions. Successful files remain until manually removed; failed captures remove partial files. Busy, cancellation and authority behavior remain at the shared capture owner. Requested durations stay capped at 150 seconds; batch destination and 64 MiB free-space checks run before profiler startup. Future graph size cannot be predicted before sampling, so actual file overflow can still fail afterward. No configuration, environment or database change, cache or persistent sampler.

Production growth is 148 lines, chiefly chunked serialization and shared file reservation. The bounded worker-GC summary contract remains unchanged.

## Evidence

Five alternating pairs used a real Node 24.22.1 dist Gateway: 10,800 synthetic sessions, four agents, 4,300 settled runs, 40 registered synthetic plugins, 37 real provider entrypoints imported/retained without registration, five WebSocket clients and four mock-model warmup turns per launch. Distinct deep synthetic call chains create graphs above 33,000 nodes. All ten old captures refused `profile-too-large`; all ten candidate captures returned complete files. Every request used exactly one start/stop, and all twenty concurrent-request busy probes passed.

Medians in milliseconds, five captures per cell; heartbeat stalls are those at least 50 ms and are observed through the RPC reply:

| Capture | Start before → after | Native stop before → after | All stalls before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 12 × 5 s | 562.09 → 528.68 | 120.95 → 121.22 | 678.09 → 637.71 |
| 30 × 5 s | 494.29 → 459.59 | 120.91 → 131.83 | 594.79 → 584.74 |

Twelve-window files were 5,043,976–5,073,931 bytes in 605–610-byte RPC receipts; thirty-window files were 5,238,516–5,325,478 bytes in 859–865-byte receipts. All node/sample counts, sample IDs and signed deltas, timeline hashes, window partitioning, file sizes and 0600 permissions passed. Nine exports had no post-stop-only stall; one had 69.15 ms. Outliers remain: all-stall p95 before/after was 698.87/1,049.01 ms for twelve windows and 661.79/2,186.10 ms for thirty, with extra stalls mostly mid-capture.

This proves preservation and one-start behavior, not a causal startup speedup: the preserved old dist and candidate include intervening main changes, and the host is shared. Same-arm startup spread was 6.15–12.03%. Build-overlapped calibration is excluded from these formal distributions. The fixture is a 268 MB agent DB on macOS/APFS, not a 35 GiB/btrfs qualification. Allocation volume was not measured; raw-profile retention by instrumentation also limits memory conclusions. Source/dist hashes stayed fixed; all synthetic Gateway listeners closed after proof. No production process or data was used.

80 focused CPU/RPC/heap-snapshot/worker-GC tests pass, and the new artifact regression fails on the old implementation. Runtime build, core/test types, focused scripts types, typed lint and formatting pass. Fresh independent Codex reviews are clean. The 112-line test allocation covers full-file preservation, preflight/byte bounds, privacy and cleanup; CPU test bodies total 7.97 seconds including the existing 5.1-second native capture.

`pnpm check:changed` exposed benchmark union/listener defects, fixed with passing scoped reruns. Its remaining 28 production/eight full-tree unused-export signatures reproduce exactly on parent 5ac21026addd, with all twelve failing owners byte-identical. Eleven newly observed main regressions trace to #192552 (eight), #196207 (one) and #196252 (two); the other seventeen retain prior source/caller-migration attribution. These are inherited main regressions, not ignored noise.

Hosted CI also caught this PR's missing wrapper inventory entry; all three failed closure cases pass after the one-line repair. Hosted review caught the benchmark example's missing artifact root; preflight now rejects before any capture and the verifier accepts oversized-single file receipts. Exact-head CI run [42815822040](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42815822040) is green on e3d5e61b988245901cbac580c699bad17d175b19. issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Changed sandbox commands freeze the guest throughout workspace discovery, Git capture, and canonical reconciliation. With large workspaces, scanning alone can take seconds while every process in the container is paused.

## User Impact

For provisioned btrfs subvolumes, checkpoint now pauses for the existing native snapshot operation, resumes the guest, and synchronizes canonical state from that captured tree. Command completion still waits for canonical acceptance, preserving read-after-command consistency. Initial recovery and imports retain their existing pause boundaries. No configuration, schema, dependency, or cache is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The checkpoint owner reuses the template backend's native copy primitive under its existing lease. Snapshot fingerprints translate only the proven snapshot device back to the source identity, preserving unchanged probes. Btrfs omits nested subvolumes: the manifest walker detects its inode-2 placeholders before accepting a receipt, then re-pauses under the same lease and uses the existing complete Git capture. Unsupported backends and ordinary directories also retain that path, resuming after durable capture.

The owner removes its private capture after resume and removes leftovers on the next lease. Native removal now repairs inaccessible directories only after a permission failure; it does not follow symlinks or change live source permissions. This is required for snapshots containing ordinary read-only workspace directories.

Snapshot creation can wait for btrfs dirty-data writeback, so this bounds the paused work rather than promising a fixed wall-clock limit. Recursive snapshot cleanup adds work after resume; the native comparison will report that cost explicitly.

## Evidence

The real Podman+btrfs comparison completed all five counterbalanced pairs: 50 measured mutating commands per arm, plus two A/A controls. Every command passed canonical and subsequent guest read checks. The fixture contains 62,000 synthetic files / 1.1 GB, 10,001 session metadata rows, and a 33.65 GiB synthetic database. No production data was used.

| Metric | Parent | Atomic capture |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Pause p50 / p95 / max | 1,619.63 / 1,830.52 / 4,497.19 ms | 194.23 / 241.48 / 269.72 ms |
| Command p50 / p95 / max | 2,374.14 / 2,854.99 / 7,252.07 ms | 3,038.07 / 3,665.20 / 4,221.59 ms |
| Whole-cgroup CPU per command | 3,493.06 ms | 4,472.75 ms |
| Main-isolate allocation per command | 19.22 MB | 20.49 MB |

Median pause improves 88%; median command latency and whole-cgroup CPU increase 28%. A/A pause, command and CPU spread was about 1–1.3%; allocation spread was 9.4%, so no allocation benefit is claimed. All pairs, including the slower first candidate arm, are retained. The 1.36–1.42 s manifest scan runs paused on the parent and unpaused on the candidate in all 50 commands. Native snapshot copy takes 106 ms median; recursive cleanup takes 511 ms after resume. Cleanup explains most of the extra command latency. The maximum guest heartbeat gap falls from 4.43 s to 243 ms.

Timing uses parent `3f17d921f6cc1cf03d52054a74ba3a5e885f5c35` and implementation `64147937916763407221bef031a138af43dd40a8`, with the same frozen harness. Final head `32b8f86f7fc49989f7ae6ab5c1346831b82b5be6` changes only type placement and emits byte-identical JavaScript. The harness runs on a task-owned Linux ARM64 rig with four CPUs and 12 GiB memory, Podman 4.3.1, btrfs 6.2, and Node 26.12.1 for allocation accounting. CPU includes native helpers, Git and the guest; allocation covers only the main V8 isolate. Separate baseline/candidate profiles passed and are excluded from these timing distributions. Final-head native nested-subvolume fallback also passed: two pauses of 180.84 and 5,387.44 ms, complete nested canonical contents, correct next guest read, preserved 0555 source permissions, and no capture artifact. The matching baseline paused 5,947.87 ms; both perform full hashing because the existing fingerprint format rejects mixed-device reuse. This single diagnostic pair is excluded from performance statistics and is not a timing-improvement claim. An oversized 20-command functional run hit its 240-second deadline after at least 17 completed commands; that partial run is retained, and the bounded follow-up changed only the proof driver loop count to one.

- Atomic ordering regressions fail on the prior head because manifest scanning still observes a paused guest. Final affected replay: 17 passed, including seven authority-loss cases. Broader touched-owner proof before the operation-file extraction: 125 passed, two existing platform skips.
- Read-only artifact removal regression fails before the fix with EACCES; all ten native-owner tests now pass. Real Linux btrfs create/copy/remove also passes as UID 501 with no effective capabilities, preserving live nested contents and read-only modes.
- Final `pnpm check:changed --base 3f17d921f6cc1cf03d52054a74ba3a5e885f5c35`: all categories pass except the exact inherited unused-export set below. These are existing main regressions, not passing checks.
- Independent Codex review of the final atomic implementation: scoped-clean through P2, with final source-integrity verification. Prior-head green CI and hosted reviews do not cover this revision; fresh exact-head checks remain required.

Production delta: +199 lines, including snapshot lifecycle/cleanup, nested-subvolume fallback, and source identity preservation. Moving the existing projection operation whole keeps one lifecycle owner within the line cap. Test delta: +245 lines for ordering, recovery, fingerprint reuse, fallback, authority loss, and artifact permissions. Benchmark code is proof-only.

CI on `64147937916763407221bef031a138af43dd40a8` found one introduced static type-import cycle. The repair moves the capture contract into the existing workspace types module and imports it directly. The exact failing guard is red on that head and green after repair; targeted typechecking passes. All six changed files emit byte-identical JavaScript, so the native comparison remains runtime-equivalent. The repair is committed as `32b8f86f7fc49989f7ae6ab5c1346831b82b5be6` and passes fresh Codex review. Final exact-head CI [42832460455](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42832460455) passed. ClawSweeper re-reviewed this head with zero findings and zero open items; [item 1 response](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196662#issuecomment-6769669864). No admin exception or CI rerun was needed.

<details>
<summary>Exact-parent unused-export regression attribution</summary>

Both Knip scans exit 1 on parent `3f17d921f6cc1cf03d52054a74ba3a5e885f5c35`; normalized symbol sets match the final candidate check exactly, with no module-resolution failures. Owner history and consumer-removal patches identify these sources:

| models-config: planOpenClawModelsJsonSource; openclaw-tools: filterToolsByClientCaps; auth-storage: AuthCredential, AuthStatus, AuthStorageBackend; model-registry: ResolvedRequestAuth; linux-oom-score: resolveOomScoreWrappedCommand, spawnWithInheritedOomScore | 625945b7ae01d / #192552 | Consumers moved to leaf owners; facade exports retained. |
| tool-search-directory: MAX_MCP_TOOL_DIRECTORY_BYTES, sanitizeMcpToolDirectoryDescription | 80ba593b8b14b / #196252 | Added exports with only test external consumers. |
| config-write-flow: replyWithBillingRouteWarnings | 56617cd000864 / #191326 | Export only externally used by tests; #196570 adds a test use, not the regression. |
| provider-external-auth: resolveExternalAuthProfilesWithPlugins | 071f606eae77a / #139911 | Native binding bypasses facade. |
| provider-runtime: augmentModelCatalogWithProviderPlugins, formatProviderAuthProfileApiKeyWithPlugin, loginProviderOAuthWithPlugin, refreshProviderOAuthCredentialWithPlugin, resolveProviderOAuthCredentialWithPlugin, resolveProviderOAuthRefreshCapabilityWithPlugin | f63e5cd0f6d38 / #190205 | Lazy runtime binders moved to auth/catalog owners. |
| provider-runtime: classifyProviderFailoverSignalWithPlugin, resolveExternalAuthProfilesWithPlugins | 964fa991c0aff / #132716 | Callers moved to leaf owners. |
| provider-runtime: resolveProviderModernModelRef | 33d8f24c9926f / #129184 | Caller moved to test helper. |
| provider-runtime: resolveProviderRuntimePlugin | a7436c8b4a93bff59d099661d2b206bb0627ac2b | Split provider hook runtime seam; transcript-policy moved to leaf owner. No PR number in commit message. |
| plugins/types: ProviderAuthOptionBag, ProviderNonInteractiveApiKeyCredentialParams, ProviderNonInteractiveApiKeyResult, ProviderResolveNonInteractiveApiKeyParams | cf1ae7bb6a729 / #190544 | Consumers moved to provider-auth-types. |
| shared/browser-pair: BROWSER_PAIR_CODE_LENGTH | d85ebfe8daad4 / #191513 | Export introduced with internal use only. |


The full-scan set is the heading helper, client-cap facade, four provider auth types, spawnWithInheritedOomScore facade, and browser constant. This identifies unused export surfaces, not necessarily unused implementations.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway memory retained after non-announcing subagents finish and their cleanup is acknowledged.

## User Impact

Completed non-announcing children release their captured execution authority. Kept child history remains available; pending wakes, paused delivery, and required completion delivery retain their existing protection. No configuration, schema, or prompt changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Non-announcing children intentionally keep their requester-turn ID. The custody owner previously required that ID to disappear before release, even though these children have no completion message to deliver. The one-line predicate now recognizes explicit `expectsCompletionMessage: false` once the existing cleanup gates pass. Production LOC is +1/-1, net zero.

The synthetic Gateway rig creates continuously arriving parents, each with a kept subagent, a verified Code Mode error, and a text turn. It supports native synthetic database preparation and quiet GC checkpoints. A separate source-import benchmark measures the actual settlement owner. Owner-census diagnostics landed in #196653. Broader custody changes in #194732 and #183715 are outside this fix.

## Evidence

The final lifetime-table regression fails with the original predicate because the captured source authority remains live. All 16 table cases pass with the fix, including pending-wake retention; the initial full 68-test completion-authority suite and 17 tooling tests also passed. Targeted lint, line-cap checks and the candidate artifact build pass. Independent Codex review is scoped-clean through P2.

A built Gateway using the real Responses transport and a synthetic loopback provider completed 1,000 parents, 1,000 kept children, 3,000 parent turns, and 1,000 provider-observed Code Mode errors in each arm. Sessions were neither archived nor deleted. Both fixtures used a 37,581,905,920-byte synthetic agent database, 62,000 workspace files (1,181,162,000 bytes), two list clients, and Node 26.12.1 on APFS.

| Completed parent/child pairs | Baseline old-gen MiB | Candidate old-gen MiB | Baseline / candidate custody entries |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 264.460 | 271.592 | 0 / 0 |
| 250 | 511.063 | 445.708 | 250 / 0 |
| 500 | 653.931 | 507.202 | 500 / 0 |
| 750 | 760.118 | 526.983 | 750 / 0 |
| 1,000, then quiet GC | 837.446 | 518.122 | 1,000 / 0 |

The final candidate owner Map is located and empty. Both arms retain 1,000 historical child records, 9,000 projection rows, 4,162 materializations, and 1,000 HTTP continuation baselines. Final old-gen is 334,835,728 bytes lower; baseline-adjusted growth is 342,313,512 bytes lower. Projection display bytes are slightly higher in the candidate, and HTTP/actor payload differences are small, so those caches do not explain the savings. Earlier fresh-state, smaller-DB A/A controls ended at 813.646 / 812.877 MiB (0.095% spread), each retaining 1,000 stale custodies. The large result is one A/B pair, not five large-fixture replicates.

The actual settlement owner was also measured in five independent processes per arm, interleaved after an adjacent A/A control. Each process pooled 20 fresh 1,000-row trials; setup, warm-up, GC and final teardown were outside timing. The callback is intentionally small, so this excludes full operator/source teardown and database commits.

| Owner cost per acknowledgement | Baseline median [p95] | Candidate median [p95] |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Wall time, µs | 5.803 [5.860] | 0.720 [0.756] |
| Thread CPU, µs | 5.960 [6.023] | 0.868 [0.918] |
| Late 250-run round wall time, µs | 10.615 [10.733] | 0.713 [0.735] |

The timing A/A ratio was 0.9285; all timing pairs passed the predeclared 1.20 limit. Allocation was measured separately with collected objects included and only ancestry under the actual settlement method counted. Its A/A control passed (231.663 / 225.619 sampled bytes per acknowledgement), then the first candidate measured 1,925.035 bytes and the series stopped at the declared limit. No later allocation pairs were run.

**Accepted allocation tradeoff:** releasing the previously leaked custody adds about 1,699 temporary sampled bytes per acknowledgement in this owner benchmark. The saved sites are the existing owner lookup, Sets/iterators, Map deletion and abort-listener removal—not benchmark assertions. We accept this bounded release cost to eliminate accumulating custody and its retained graph, while settlement CPU falls. The allocation threshold failure is preserved; it is not reported as passing or within spread. Alias/rekey lifetime contracts do not justify deleting the existing release lookup merely to improve this microbenchmark.

A separate whole-Gateway cost series stopped before candidate runs because unchanged A/A CPU rose 595→786 ms/parent and elapsed time 845→1,752 ms/parent, exceeding the same 1.20 control limit. Host load rose substantially. No Gateway throughput/latency speedup or full-flow allocation claim is made from those unstable controls.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and measurement limits</summary>

Build baseline and candidate artifacts in isolated checkouts. The matching Gateway workload is documented in `scripts/perf/per-run-retention.md`; command shape:

```sh
node scripts/gateway-heap-rig.mjs --root "$PWD/.local/retention-arm" \
  --fixture-gib 35 --minutes 120 --sessions 2000 --clients 2 \
  --port 45810 --snapshot-minutes none --new-turn-sessions 1000 \
  --retention-round-size 750 --turn-interval-ms 1 --retention-mode retained \
  --retention-snapshots --idle-minutes 6 \
  --ready-file "$PWD/.local/retention.ready" --start-file "$PWD/.local/retention.start"
```

Populate the synthetic 62,000-file workspace at the ready gate, then write a future epoch-millisecond start timestamp. Use `--runtime-root` for the isolated baseline build. Both captured runtime builds retain base commit metadata; source hashes and distinct build timestamps distinguish the candidate release predicate. The production owner file is unchanged by the later benchmark-only addition.

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs \
  /absolute/candidate/scripts/perf/subagent-custody-settlement.mjs \
  "$PWD" "$PWD/.local/owner-timing-a1"
```

Use fresh directories/processes, A0/A1/B1/A2/B2/A3/B3/A4/B4/A5/B5, and separate `allocation` runs. The locally recorded protocol stopped a control or pair above 1.20 and flagged a final median above 1.10; failed gates and sample counts are retained above. With five process observations, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum.

Retained sampling measures surviving new allocations, not net growth. Dominator-group unions overlap and are not additive or hypothetical collective-removal sizes. Request-building/admission allocations plateau with the existing HTTP continuation bound; full-request retention also supports replay/recovery contracts, so no speculative equality or baseline deletion is included. Presentation has no independent numeric variant cap and remains unchanged. Native-created production allocations and all real-world error paths are not fully attributed by this fixture.

All data are synthetic; no production access or data was used. APFS data shape does not establish btrfs performance, and this does not claim the entire production staircase is resolved.

</details>

`pnpm check:changed` found inherited dead-export failures (34 production and 13 full-tree), reproduced identically on untouched parent `5f27b11f9f135d0e57bbab6eb44e545df5087f08`; routed typechecks passed. Attributed owner changes include #196207, #192552, #196252, #191326, #191513, #196472, #190544, #190205, #132716, #139911, and `a7436c8b4a93bff59d099661d2b206bb0627ac2b`. These are main regressions, not ignored noise; no unrelated exports or guards are changed.

Final-head CI run [42828073309](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42828073309), attempt 1, failed only the worktree-spawn case expecting GitHub+`worktree:false` sandbox rejection; the aggregate gate failed downstream and `security-fast` passed. The unchanged case reproduces identically on its exact main parent `401a1de38b9a4c7ee3f1b19908df777a2f02506d` (one failed / 26 skipped, 68.90 s Vitest, clean checkout). #196206 (`97e91a16d636cbf25fff55728de21afc1578ac53`) changed those URLs to use managed worktrees, leaving that expectation stale. The failed inputs are blob-identical in tested merge `62365684997e97a995a8cbd42e36366c0af78ad5`. This is a newly observed main test regression requiring follow-up, not noise. The authorized inherited-only landing exception retains this failed result; it does not relabel CI green.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A running child session shifts its elapsed label and squeezes its title when `9s` becomes `10s`. Tabular digits make each numeral the same width, but do not reserve room for the added digit.

## User Impact

The elapsed label and session title stay in place while the visible clock ticks, on desktop and in the mobile drawer. The existing clock, offscreen pause, accessibility description, and snooze display retain their owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reserve a 7ch minimum slot only for the elapsed trail and align its text at the leading edge. Longer localized durations can still grow; nothing is clipped. This reserves about 40 px more than the initial single-digit label on the measured font, trading some title width for stable ticking. No new state, timer, listener, abstraction, stylesheet, or import.

## Evidence

Production bundle with the census synthetic Gateway and idle-sidebar-running-1 / idle-sidebar-clock-mobile-open-1 scenarios, Firefox 157. The rAF computed-style record measures the clock text through a DOM Range because its host uses display: contents. The filmstrip contains the same transition.

| Desktop clock/title displacement, 9s → 10s | 6.600006px→0px |
| Mobile clock/title displacement, 9s → 10s | 6.600006px→0px |
| Existing row-render owner suite | 25/25 pass |
| UI typecheck | Pass |
| Scoped lint/format/diff check | Pass |
| Independent Codex review, P0–P2 | No actionable findings |
| Startup normalizedJS / CSS requests | 91,889 B →91,889 B / 1 → 1 |
| Chat/New normalizedJS delta | +36 B gzip (+85 B raw), within 64 B build variance; no ceiling change |
| Comparative performance checker |No violations or warnings |
| Production Knip | Ran; same three unlisted benchmark binaries (taskkill.exe and btrfs twice) as the other owner baselines |

All 120 observations passed: twenty rotated base/head/base triplets per viewport. Five-second idle wall median/p95 (ms): desktop base 5001.399/5002.491, head 5001.339/5002.538, A/A 5001.037/5002.443; mobile base 5001.821/5002.554, head 5001.647/5002.277, A/A 5001.781/5002.617. The desktop p95 movement is under 0.05 ms; no meaningful timing regression was detected. Every base/control sample incurred one resize-observer callback and one animation-frame callback during the digit-count transition; the head incurred zero, while clock interval callbacks were unchanged. Firefox does not expose native CLS/CPU counters here, so geometry is the displacement proof. Chromium headless shell is unavailable on this host (even blank-page screenshots time out); WebKit launch times out. The extended existing E2E checks actual text position and title width across9s → 10s in its desktop/mobile/text-scale variants; PR CI runs it.

The first CI run (42796216515) caught a fixture error in all seven new clock assertions: the row builder defaults to `status: "done"`, while this test only set `hasActiveRun: true`. issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway memory retained after non-announcing subagents finish and their cleanup is acknowledged.

## User Impact

Completed non-announcing children release their captured execution authority. Kept child history remains available; pending wakes, paused delivery, and required completion delivery retain their existing protection. No configuration, schema, or prompt changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Non-announcing children intentionally keep their requester-turn ID. The custody owner previously required that ID to disappear before release, even though these children have no completion message to deliver. The one-line predicate now recognizes explicit `expectsCompletionMessage: false` once the existing cleanup gates pass. Production LOC is +1/-1, net zero.

The synthetic Gateway rig creates continuously arriving parents, each with a kept subagent, a verified Code Mode error, and a text turn. It supports native synthetic database preparation and quiet GC checkpoints. A separate source-import benchmark measures the actual settlement owner. Owner-census diagnostics landed in #196653. Broader custody changes in #194732 and #183715 are outside this fix.

## Evidence

The final lifetime-table regression fails with the original predicate because the captured source authority remains live. All 16 table cases pass with the fix, including pending-wake retention; the initial full 68-test completion-authority suite and 17 tooling tests also passed. Targeted lint, line-cap checks and the candidate artifact build pass. Independent Codex review is scoped-clean through P2.

A built Gateway using the real Responses transport and a synthetic loopback provider completed 1,000 parents, 1,000 kept children, 3,000 parent turns, and 1,000 provider-observed Code Mode errors in each arm. Sessions were neither archived nor deleted. Both fixtures used a 37,581,905,920-byte synthetic agent database, 62,000 workspace files (1,181,162,000 bytes), two list clients, and Node 26.12.1 on APFS.

| Completed parent/child pairs | Baseline old-gen MiB | Candidate old-gen MiB | Baseline / candidate custody entries |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 264.460 | 271.592 | 0 / 0 |
| 250 | 511.063 | 445.708 | 250 / 0 |
| 500 | 653.931 | 507.202 | 500 / 0 |
| 750 | 760.118 | 526.983 | 750 / 0 |
| 1,000, then quiet GC | 837.446 | 518.122 | 1,000 / 0 |

The final candidate owner Map is located and empty. Both arms retain 1,000 historical child records, 9,000 projection rows, 4,162 materializations, and 1,000 HTTP continuation baselines. Final old-gen is 334,835,728 bytes lower; baseline-adjusted growth is 342,313,512 bytes lower. Projection display bytes are slightly higher in the candidate, and HTTP/actor payload differences are small, so those caches do not explain the savings. Earlier fresh-state, smaller-DB A/A controls ended at 813.646 / 812.877 MiB (0.095% spread), each retaining 1,000 stale custodies. The large result is one A/B pair, not five large-fixture replicates.

The actual settlement owner was also measured in five independent processes per arm, interleaved after an adjacent A/A control. Each process pooled 20 fresh 1,000-row trials; setup, warm-up, GC and final teardown were outside timing. The callback is intentionally small, so this excludes full operator/source teardown and database commits.

| Owner cost per acknowledgement | Baseline median [p95] | Candidate median [p95] |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Wall time, µs | 5.803 [5.860] | 0.720 [0.756] |
| Thread CPU, µs | 5.960 [6.023] | 0.868 [0.918] |
| Late 250-run round wall time, µs | 10.615 [10.733] | 0.713 [0.735] |

The timing A/A ratio was 0.9285; all timing pairs passed the predeclared 1.20 limit. Allocation was measured separately with collected objects included and only ancestry under the actual settlement method counted. Its A/A control passed (231.663 / 225.619 sampled bytes per acknowledgement), then the first candidate measured 1,925.035 bytes and the series stopped at the declared limit. No later allocation pairs were run.

**Accepted allocation tradeoff:** releasing the previously leaked custody adds about 1,699 temporary sampled bytes per acknowledgement in this owner benchmark. The saved sites are the existing owner lookup, Sets/iterators, Map deletion and abort-listener removal—not benchmark assertions. We accept this bounded release cost to eliminate accumulating custody and its retained graph, while settlement CPU falls. The allocation threshold failure is preserved; it is not reported as passing or within spread. Alias/rekey lifetime contracts do not justify deleting the existing release lookup merely to improve this microbenchmark.

A separate whole-Gateway cost series stopped before candidate runs because unchanged A/A CPU rose 595→786 ms/parent and elapsed time 845→1,752 ms/parent, exceeding the same 1.20 control limit. Host load rose substantially. No Gateway throughput/latency speedup or full-flow allocation claim is made from those unstable controls.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and measurement limits</summary>

Build baseline and candidate artifacts in isolated checkouts. The matching Gateway workload is documented in `scripts/perf/per-run-retention.md`; command shape:

```sh
node scripts/gateway-heap-rig.mjs --root "$PWD/.local/retention-arm" \
  --fixture-gib 35 --minutes 120 --sessions 2000 --clients 2 \
  --port 45810 --snapshot-minutes none --new-turn-sessions 1000 \
  --retention-round-size 750 --turn-interval-ms 1 --retention-mode retained \
  --retention-snapshots --idle-minutes 6 \
  --ready-file "$PWD/.local/retention.ready" --start-file "$PWD/.local/retention.start"
```

Populate the synthetic 62,000-file workspace at the ready gate, then write a future epoch-millisecond start timestamp. Use `--runtime-root` for the isolated baseline build. Both captured runtime builds retain base commit metadata; source hashes and distinct build timestamps distinguish the candidate release predicate. The production owner file is unchanged by the later benchmark-only addition.

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs \
  /absolute/candidate/scripts/perf/subagent-custody-settlement.mjs \
  "$PWD" "$PWD/.local/owner-timing-a1"
```

Use fresh directories/processes, A0/A1/B1/A2/B2/A3/B3/A4/B4/A5/B5, and separate `allocation` runs. The locally recorded protocol stopped a control or pair above 1.20 and flagged a final median above 1.10; failed gates and sample counts are retained above. With five process observations, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum.

Retained sampling measures surviving new allocations, not net growth. Dominator-group unions overlap and are not additive or hypothetical collective-removal sizes. Request-building/admission allocations plateau with the existing HTTP continuation bound; full-request retention also supports replay/recovery contracts, so no speculative equality or baseline deletion is included. Presentation has no independent numeric variant cap and remains unchanged. Native-created production allocations and all real-world error paths are not fully attributed by this fixture.

All data are synthetic; no production access or data was used. APFS data shape does not establish btrfs performance, and this does not claim the entire production staircase is resolved.

</details>

`pnpm check:changed` found inherited dead-export failures (34 production and 13 full-tree), reproduced identically on untouched parent `5f27b11f9f135d0e57bbab6eb44e545df5087f08`; routed typechecks passed. Attributed owner changes include #196207, #192552, #196252, #191326, #191513, #196472, #190544, #190205, #132716, #139911, and `a7436c8b4a93bff59d099661d2b206bb0627ac2b`. These are main regressions, not ignored noise; no unrelated exports or guards are changed.

Final-head CI run [42828073309](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42828073309), attempt 1, failed only the worktree-spawn case expecting GitHub+`worktree:false` sandbox rejection; the aggregate gate failed downstream and `security-fast` passed. The unchanged case reproduces identically on its exact main parent `401a1de38b9a4c7ee3f1b19908df777a2f02506d` (one failed / 26 skipped, 68.90 s Vitest, clean checkout). #196206 (`97e91a16d636cbf25fff55728de21afc1578ac53`) changed those URLs to use managed worktrees, leaving that expectation stale. The failed inputs are blob-identical in tested merge `62365684997e97a995a8cbd42e36366c0af78ad5`. This is a newly observed main test regression requiring follow-up, not noise. The authorized inherited-only landing exception retains this failed result; it does not relabel CI green.

The final head is `d9f3b19dcf5436b9fd21c32a527d27a8c8a2907f`. The previous review had no open checkbox findings. Its runtime-evidence note is now addressed in the PR body with completed, matched built-Gateway results:

- After 1,000 kept children, the located completion-custody Map is 1,000 entries before / zero after; all 1,000 historical run records remain. The separately measured allocation increase and stopped whole-Gateway controls are explicitly disclosed, with the bounded release-allocation tradeoff accepted in the body. issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Changed sandbox commands freeze the guest throughout workspace discovery, Git capture, and canonical reconciliation. With large workspaces, scanning alone can take seconds while every process in the container is paused.

## User Impact

For provisioned btrfs subvolumes, checkpoint now pauses for the existing native snapshot operation, resumes the guest, and synchronizes canonical state from that captured tree. Command completion still waits for canonical acceptance, preserving read-after-command consistency. Initial recovery and imports retain their existing pause boundaries. No configuration, schema, dependency, or cache is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The checkpoint owner reuses the template backend's native copy primitive under its existing lease. Snapshot fingerprints translate only the proven snapshot device back to the source identity, preserving unchanged probes. Btrfs omits nested subvolumes: the manifest walker detects its inode-2 placeholders before accepting a receipt, then re-pauses under the same lease and uses the existing complete Git capture. Unsupported backends and ordinary directories also retain that path, resuming after durable capture.

The owner removes its private capture after resume and removes leftovers on the next lease. Native removal now repairs inaccessible directories only after a permission failure; it does not follow symlinks or change live source permissions. This is required for snapshots containing ordinary read-only workspace directories.

Snapshot creation can wait for btrfs dirty-data writeback, so this bounds the paused work rather than promising a fixed wall-clock limit. Recursive snapshot cleanup adds work after resume; the native comparison will report that cost explicitly.

## Evidence

The real Podman+btrfs comparison completed all five counterbalanced pairs: 50 measured mutating commands per arm, plus two A/A controls. Every command passed canonical and subsequent guest read checks. The fixture contains 62,000 synthetic files / 1.1 GB, 10,001 session metadata rows, and a 33.65 GiB synthetic database. No production data was used.

| Metric | Parent | Atomic capture |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Pause p50 / p95 / max | 1,619.63 / 1,830.52 / 4,497.19 ms | 194.23 / 241.48 / 269.72 ms |
| Command p50 / p95 / max | 2,374.14 / 2,854.99 / 7,252.07 ms | 3,038.07 / 3,665.20 / 4,221.59 ms |
| Whole-cgroup CPU per command | 3,493.06 ms | 4,472.75 ms |
| Main-isolate allocation per command | 19.22 MB | 20.49 MB |

Median pause improves 88%; median command latency and whole-cgroup CPU increase 28%. A/A pause, command and CPU spread was about 1–1.3%; allocation spread was 9.4%, so no allocation benefit is claimed. All pairs, including the slower first candidate arm, are retained. The 1.36–1.42 s manifest scan runs paused on the parent and unpaused on the candidate in all 50 commands. Native snapshot copy takes 106 ms median; recursive cleanup takes 511 ms after resume. Cleanup explains most of the extra command latency. The maximum guest heartbeat gap falls from 4.43 s to 243 ms.

Timing uses parent `3f17d921f6cc1cf03d52054a74ba3a5e885f5c35` and implementation `64147937916763407221bef031a138af43dd40a8`, with the same frozen harness. Final head `32b8f86f7fc49989f7ae6ab5c1346831b82b5be6` changes only type placement and emits byte-identical JavaScript. The harness runs on a task-owned Linux ARM64 rig with four CPUs and 12 GiB memory, Podman 4.3.1, btrfs 6.2, and Node 26.12.1 for allocation accounting. CPU includes native helpers, Git and the guest; allocation covers only the main V8 isolate. Separate baseline/candidate profiles passed and are excluded from these timing distributions. Final-head native nested-subvolume fallback also passed: two pauses of 180.84 and 5,387.44 ms, complete nested canonical contents, correct next guest read, preserved 0555 source permissions, and no capture artifact. The matching baseline paused 5,947.87 ms; both perform full hashing because the existing fingerprint format rejects mixed-device reuse. This single diagnostic pair is excluded from performance statistics and is not a timing-improvement claim. An oversized 20-command functional run hit its 240-second deadline after at least 17 completed commands; that partial run is retained, and the bounded follow-up changed only the proof driver loop count to one.

- Atomic ordering regressions fail on the prior head because manifest scanning still observes a paused guest. Final affected replay: 17 passed, including seven authority-loss cases. Broader touched-owner proof before the operation-file extraction: 125 passed, two existing platform skips.
- Read-only artifact removal regression fails before the fix with EACCES; all ten native-owner tests now pass. Real Linux btrfs create/copy/remove also passes as UID 501 with no effective capabilities, preserving live nested contents and read-only modes.
- Final `pnpm check:changed --base 3f17d921f6cc1cf03d52054a74ba3a5e885f5c35`: all categories pass except the exact inherited unused-export set below. These are existing main regressions, not passing checks.
- Independent Codex review of the final atomic implementation: scoped-clean through P2, with final source-integrity verification. Prior-head green CI and hosted reviews do not cover this revision; fresh exact-head checks remain required.

Production delta: +199 lines, including snapshot lifecycle/cleanup, nested-subvolume fallback, and source identity preservation. Moving the existing projection operation whole keeps one lifecycle owner within the line cap. Test delta: +245 lines for ordering, recovery, fingerprint reuse, fallback, authority loss, and artifact permissions. Benchmark code is proof-only.

CI on `64147937916763407221bef031a138af43dd40a8` found one introduced static type-import cycle. The repair moves the capture contract into the existing workspace types module and imports it directly. The exact failing guard is red on that head and green after repair; targeted typechecking passes. All six changed files emit byte-identical JavaScript, so the native comparison remains runtime-equivalent. The repair is committed as `32b8f86f7fc49989f7ae6ab5c1346831b82b5be6` and passes fresh Codex review. Final exact-head CI [42832460455](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42832460455) passed. ClawSweeper re-reviewed this head with zero findings and zero open items; [item 1 response](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196662#issuecomment-6769669864). No admin exception or CI rerun was needed.

<details>
<summary>Exact-parent unused-export regression attribution</summary>

Both Knip scans exit 1 on parent `3f17d921f6cc1cf03d52054a74ba3a5e885f5c35`; normalized symbol sets match the final candidate check exactly, with no module-resolution failures. Owner history and consumer-removal patches identify these sources:

| Export owner / symbols | Introducing commit / PR | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| compaction-safeguard-quality: nestRequiredSummaryHeadings | c7152f3bda8e5 / #196207 | Formatting moved into owner; external consumer removed. |
| models-config: planOpenClawModelsJsonSource; openclaw-tools: filterToolsByClientCaps; auth-storage: AuthCredential, AuthStatus, AuthStorageBackend; model-registry: ResolvedRequestAuth; linux-oom-score: resolveOomScoreWrappedCommand, spawnWithInheritedOomScore | 625945b7ae01d / #192552 | Consumers moved to leaf owners; facade exports retained. |
| tool-search-directory: MAX_MCP_TOOL_DIRECTORY_BYTES, sanitizeMcpToolDirectoryDescription | 80ba593b8b14b / #196252 | Added exports with only test external consumers. |
| config-write-flow: replyWithBillingRouteWarnings | 56617cd000864 / #191326 | Export only externally used by tests; #196570 adds a test use, not the regression. |
| provider-external-auth: resolveExternalAuthProfilesWithPlugins | 071f606eae77a / #139911 | Native binding bypasses facade. |
| provider-runtime: augmentModelCatalogWithProviderPlugins, formatProviderAuthProfileApiKeyWithPlugin, loginProviderOAuthWithPlugin, refreshProviderOAuthCredentialWithPlugin, resolveProviderOAuthCredentialWithPlugin, resolveProviderOAuthRefreshCapabilityWithPlugin | f63e5cd0f6d38 / #190205 | Lazy runtime binders moved to auth/catalog owners. |
| provider-runtime: classifyProviderFailoverSignalWithPlugin, resolveExternalAuthProfilesWithPlugins | 964fa991c0aff / #132716 | Callers moved to leaf owners. |
| provider-runtime: resolveProviderModernModelRef | 33d8f24c9926f / #129184 | Caller moved to test helper. |
| provider-runtime: resolveProviderRuntimePlugin | a7436c8b4a93bff59d099661d2b206bb0627ac2b | Split provider hook runtime seam; transcript-policy moved to leaf owner. No PR number in commit message. |
| plugins/types: ProviderAuthOptionBag, ProviderNonInteractiveApiKeyCredentialParams, ProviderNonInteractiveApiKeyResult, ProviderResolveNonInteractiveApiKeyParams | cf1ae7bb6a729 / #190544 | Consumers moved to provider-auth-types. |
| shared/browser-pair: BROWSER_PAIR_CODE_LENGTH | d85ebfe8daad4 / #191513 | Export introduced with internal use only. |


The full-scan set is the heading helper, client-cap facade, four provider auth types, spawnWithInheritedOomScore facade, and browser constant. This identifies unused export surfaces, not necessarily unused implementations.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the chat transcript jumping through partially measured rows when fresh history arrives just after the cached conversation reaches its end.

Related: scheduled CI [42807391153](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42807391153), `chat-snapshot-text-fidelity.e2e.test.ts`, cached-end refresh with eight appended pairs.

## User Impact

The refreshed conversation reaches its measured final position without moving the latest reply through successive estimated positions. Existing reader positioning, smooth scrolling, and same-row growth remain covered.

## Why This Change Was Made

Completing an end journey started another dynamic end command after clearing the application command. That leftover command could follow newly appended rows before the normal preparation code measured them. Retire it at the current native offset; the existing end anchor and preparation code continue to own later measurements and new destinations. This removes the extra dynamic command without adding state.

## Evidence

The strengthened existing E2E fails on the base: the final reply reaches the bottom with a 120px modeled size and a 71px native height, then moves as the remaining estimates settle. It passes with this change. All six transcript-fidelity E2E cases, all 31 neighboring end-follow browser tests, the default UI typecheck (tsrs), focused lint, and formatting pass.

Independent Codex autoreview of the complete local change against `225afda642e9632775d7cfc520d1862736f50a19`, through P3, found no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable because its built runner is absent; a hosted review is requested on the ready PR.

The scheduled job failed earlier in the same case on a retained-row height change from 3202.65625px to 50px. That exact collapse did not reproduce locally; this PR fixes the independently reproduced premature end-follow and retains the height assertion. It does not claim that a passing replay proves the separate collapse resolved.

![Before: baseline replay after settling; transient jump is shown by the failing test](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/315ebabc-753f-4670-a0fe-fac66cfa3f3c)

![After: fixed replay reaches the same final layout with measured rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cbb29bf4-6dd8-48a7-b196-72b7e21d33ec)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Access controls restoring an older remembered choice when toggled again before the previous selection finishes saving.

Related: scheduled CI [42807391153](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42807391153), `chat-daybreak.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` — `persists visible selections and refreshes queued requests on desktop`.

Access controls wait for the full selection operation before accepting another toggle. Keyboard focus stays on the selected control.

## Why This Change Was Made

The selection callback already waits for both the session update and the preference save. The control discarded its completion, allowing a quick off/on toggle to restore the old remembered choice. Its saving state now follows that callback using the existing focus-preserving switch behavior. Session and preference authority stay with their existing owners.

The production change adds seven net lines for the action and activation guards. It adds no new preference state, persistence path, or loading effects.

The new browser regression holds callback completion after the requested selection updates, checks that further activation is blocked without losing focus, and verifies the control becomes available after successful or unsuccessful settlement. issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Changed sandbox commands freeze the guest throughout workspace discovery, Git capture, and canonical reconciliation. With large workspaces, scanning alone can take seconds while every process in the container is paused.

## User Impact

For provisioned btrfs subvolumes, checkpoint now pauses for the existing native snapshot operation, resumes the guest, and synchronizes canonical state from that captured tree. Command completion still waits for canonical acceptance, preserving read-after-command consistency. Initial recovery and imports retain their existing pause boundaries. No configuration, schema, dependency, or cache is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The checkpoint owner reuses the template backend's native copy primitive under its existing lease. Snapshot fingerprints translate only the proven snapshot device back to the source identity, preserving unchanged probes. Btrfs omits nested subvolumes: the manifest walker detects its inode-2 placeholders before accepting a receipt, then re-pauses under the same lease and uses the existing complete Git capture. Unsupported backends and ordinary directories also retain that path, resuming after durable capture.

The owner removes its private capture after resume and removes leftovers on the next lease. Native removal now repairs inaccessible directories only after a permission failure; it does not follow symlinks or change live source permissions. This is required for snapshots containing ordinary read-only workspace directories.

Snapshot creation can wait for btrfs dirty-data writeback, so this bounds the paused work rather than promising a fixed wall-clock limit. Recursive snapshot cleanup adds work after resume; the native comparison will report that cost explicitly.

## Evidence

The real Podman+btrfs comparison completed all five counterbalanced pairs: 50 measured mutating commands per arm, plus two A/A controls. Every command passed canonical and subsequent guest read checks. The fixture contains 62,000 synthetic files / 1.1 GB, 10,001 session metadata rows, and a 33.65 GiB synthetic database. No production data was used.

| Metric | Parent | Atomic capture |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Pause p50 / p95 / max | 1,619.63 / 1,830.52 / 4,497.19 ms | 194.23 / 241.48 / 269.72 ms |
| Command p50 / p95 / max | 2,374.14 / 2,854.99 / 7,252.07 ms | 3,038.07 / 3,665.20 / 4,221.59 ms |
| Whole-cgroup CPU per command | 3,493.06 ms | 4,472.75 ms |
| Main-isolate allocation per command | 19.22 MB | 20.49 MB |

Median pause improves 88%; median command latency and whole-cgroup CPU increase 28%. A/A pause, command and CPU spread was about 1–1.3%; allocation spread was 9.4%, so no allocation benefit is claimed. All pairs, including the slower first candidate arm, are retained. The 1.36–1.42 s manifest scan runs paused on the parent and unpaused on the candidate in all 50 commands. Native snapshot copy takes 106 ms median; recursive cleanup takes 511 ms after resume. Cleanup explains most of the extra command latency. The maximum guest heartbeat gap falls from 4.43 s to 243 ms.

Timing uses parent `3f17d921f6cc1cf03d52054a74ba3a5e885f5c35` and implementation `64147937916763407221bef031a138af43dd40a8`, with the same frozen harness. Final head `32b8f86f7fc49989f7ae6ab5c1346831b82b5be6` changes only type placement and emits byte-identical JavaScript. The harness runs on a task-owned Linux ARM64 rig with four CPUs and 12 GiB memory, Podman 4.3.1, btrfs 6.2, and Node 26.12.1 for allocation accounting. CPU includes native helpers, Git and the guest; allocation covers only the main V8 isolate. Separate baseline/candidate profiles passed and are excluded from these timing distributions. Final-head native nested-subvolume fallback also passed: two pauses of 180.84 and 5,387.44 ms, complete nested canonical contents, correct next guest read, preserved 0555 source permissions, and no capture artifact. The matching baseline paused 5,947.87 ms; both perform full hashing because the existing fingerprint format rejects mixed-device reuse. This single diagnostic pair is excluded from performance statistics and is not a timing-improvement claim. An oversized 20-command functional run hit its 240-second deadline after at least 17 completed commands; that partial run is retained, and the bounded follow-up changed only the proof driver loop count to one.

- Atomic ordering regressions fail on the prior head because manifest scanning still observes a paused guest. Final affected replay: 17 passed, including seven authority-loss cases. Broader touched-owner proof before the operation-file extraction: 125 passed, two existing platform skips.
- Read-only artifact removal regression fails before the fix with EACCES; all ten native-owner tests now pass. Real Linux btrfs create/copy/remove also passes as UID 501 with no effective capabilities, preserving live nested contents and read-only modes.
- Final `pnpm check:changed --base 3f17d921f6cc1cf03d52054a74ba3a5e885f5c35`: all categories pass except the exact inherited unused-export set below. These are existing main regressions, not passing checks.
- Independent Codex review of the final atomic implementation: scoped-clean through P2, with final source-integrity verification. Prior-head green CI and hosted reviews do not cover this revision; fresh exact-head checks remain required.

Production delta: +199 lines, including snapshot lifecycle/cleanup, nested-subvolume fallback, and source identity preservation. Moving the existing projection operation whole keeps one lifecycle owner within the line cap. Test delta: +245 lines for ordering, recovery, fingerprint reuse, fallback, authority loss, and artifact permissions. Benchmark code is proof-only.

CI on `64147937916763407221bef031a138af43dd40a8` found one introduced static type-import cycle. The repair moves the capture contract into the existing workspace types module and imports it directly. The exact failing guard is red on that head and green after repair; targeted typechecking passes. All six changed files emit byte-identical JavaScript, so the native comparison remains runtime-equivalent. The repair is committed as `32b8f86f7fc49989f7ae6ab5c1346831b82b5be6` and passes fresh Codex review. Final exact-head CI [42832460455](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42832460455) passed. ClawSweeper re-reviewed this head with zero findings and zero open items; [item 1 response](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196662#issuecomment-6769669864). No admin exception or CI rerun was needed.

<details>
<summary>Exact-parent unused-export regression attribution</summary>

Both Knip scans exit 1 on parent `3f17d921f6cc1cf03d52054a74ba3a5e885f5c35`; normalized symbol sets match the final candidate check exactly, with no module-resolution failures. Owner history and consumer-removal patches identify these sources:

| Export owner / symbols | Introducing commit / PR | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| compaction-safeguard-quality: nestRequiredSummaryHeadings | c7152f3bda8e5 / #196207 | Formatting moved into owner; external consumer removed. |
| models-config: planOpenClawModelsJsonSource; openclaw-tools: filterToolsByClientCaps; auth-storage: AuthCredential, AuthStatus, AuthStorageBackend; model-registry: ResolvedRequestAuth; linux-oom-score: resolveOomScoreWrappedCommand, spawnWithInheritedOomScore | 625945b7ae01d / #192552 | Consumers moved to leaf owners; facade exports retained. |
| tool-search-directory: MAX_MCP_TOOL_DIRECTORY_BYTES, sanitizeMcpToolDirectoryDescription | 80ba593b8b14b / #196252 | Added exports with only test external consumers. |
| config-write-flow: replyWithBillingRouteWarnings | 56617cd000864 / #191326 | Export only externally used by tests; #196570 adds a test use, not the regression. |
| provider-external-auth: resolveExternalAuthProfilesWithPlugins | 071f606eae77a / #139911 | Native binding bypasses facade. |
| provider-runtime: augmentModelCatalogWithProviderPlugins, formatProviderAuthProfileApiKeyWithPlugin, loginProviderOAuthWithPlugin, refreshProviderOAuthCredentialWithPlugin, resolveProviderOAuthCredentialWithPlugin, resolveProviderOAuthRefreshCapabilityWithPlugin | f63e5cd0f6d38 / #190205 | Lazy runtime binders moved to auth/catalog owners. |
| provider-runtime: classifyProviderFailoverSignalWithPlugin, resolveExternalAuthProfilesWithPlugins | 964fa991c0aff / #132716 | Callers moved to leaf owners. |
| provider-runtime: resolveProviderModernModelRef | 33d8f24c9926f / #129184 | Caller moved to test helper. |
| provider-runtime: resolveProviderRuntimePlugin | a7436c8b4a93bff59d099661d2b206bb0627ac2b | Split provider hook runtime seam; transcript-policy moved to leaf owner. No PR number in commit message. |
| plugins/types: ProviderAuthOptionBag, ProviderNonInteractiveApiKeyCredentialParams, ProviderNonInteractiveApiKeyResult, ProviderResolveNonInteractiveApiKeyParams | cf1ae7bb6a729 / #190544 | Consumers moved to provider-auth-types. |
| shared/browser-pair: BROWSER_PAIR_CODE_LENGTH | d85ebfe8daad4 / #191513 | Export introduced with internal use only. |


The full-scan set is the heading helper, client-cap facade, four provider auth types, spawnWithInheritedOomScore facade, and browser constant. This identifies unused export surfaces, not necessarily unused implementations.

</details>

comment.body:
Performance acceptance is not met by the current head. The first matched native Podman/btrfs pair measured pause median 1600.88 → 1582.71 ms (-1.1%), versus 1.1% spread between baseline control medians; complete command median rose 2323.88 → 2490.04 ms (+7.2%). Manifest scanning dominates the pause. All read-after-command assertions passed, but these measurements do not justify claiming the long-freeze issue is solved.

I am revising the implementation to use the existing atomic btrfs snapshot primitive for provisioned subvolumes, with nested-subvolume omission detection before acceptance and a paused retry when needed. Snapshot disposal cost will be measured outside the pause. The current PR is held as draft until this path and its native proof are complete. No merge is requested.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Context assembly scans long system instructions and pending user text twice to compute the same history budget.

## User Impact

Reduces CPU spent preparing long prompts. Compaction decisions, history budgets, provider messages, and configuration remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both assembly entry points now compute the budget once within the source scope and pass it to the engine and final host bound, including the assembly-failure fallback. This adds no cache or invalidation mechanism. Existing immutable transcript estimates and attempt-owned tool-schema estimates remain in place; those consumers price different request components.

Production delta is +7 lines, including the scalar parameter and expanded call. This is the smallest complete change after the simplification pass. #196551 independently changes result metadata in the same module; #194545 touches the broader estimator modules, which this change leaves alone.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: ten synthetic sessions with 360 mixed Latin/CJK user, assistant/tool-call, tool-result, and image messages each; 40,600-character system instructions and 5,160-character pending input. Measure 1,000 warm preparations per process, five interleaved pairs plus five A/A pairs; run timing and collected-inclusive allocation sampling separately. Require identical output/history-budget fingerprints, half the rendered-prompt scans, lower CPU, and no metric regression above 20%.

The committed workload is `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/context-engine-lifecycle-bench.ts --long-context --iterations 1000`. Use `--owner <baseline-source-snapshot>` for baseline, `--allocations` for allocation samples, and `--counts` separately for scan counts.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| String scans per preparation | 4 | 2 |
| Characters scanned per preparation | 91,520 | 45,760 |
| Median main-thread CPU per preparation | 1.433 ms | 0.757 ms |
| Median per-process p95 latency | 1.582 ms | 0.813 ms |
| Median sampled allocation per preparation | 315,430 B | 310,768 B |

CPU improves 47.2%, sampled allocation improves 1.5%; A/A median CPU differs by 0.2% and allocation by 0.15%. All 40 output/history-budget fingerprints match. CPU ranges are 1.406–1.443 ms baseline and 0.731–0.777 ms candidate; allocation ranges are 313,463–316,347 B and 309,112–311,732 B. Separate CPU profiles attribute the eliminated duplicate work to the character estimator. This workload exercises the real in-memory lifecycle owner; it does not claim Gateway, provider-network, database, or filesystem performance.

81 focused tests pass across lifecycle, token-pressure, preemptive-compaction, replay, and prompt-prefix stability suites. The 25 lifecycle cases also passed again after the baseline restoration. The new regression covers both entry points and engine-failure fallback, asserting the unchanged 4,952-token history budget and one rendered-prompt estimate. `pnpm check:changed` passed formatting, lint, core/test/script typechecks, and all structural guards; it failed only on pre-existing unused exports outside this patch. All three new cases fail on the baseline owner because the rendered-prompt estimator is called twice instead of once. A clean checkout of exact parent `5ac21026addd1` reproduces all 28 production and 8 full-tree unused-export entries byte-for-byte. These are main check regressions, not dismissed as noise.

Codex autoreview of the local candidate against `5ac21026addd1`, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The reviewer inspected the supplied diff; unchanged source and runtime results were not part of that isolated review. Hosted ClawSweeper and exact-head CI remain required before landing.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long CPU-profile batches pause a large Gateway to start profiling, then discard the entire capture when its graph exceeds the RPC response limits. This follows #196422: batching amortized startup, but its earlier 64–140-node fixture missed the large-graph refusal.

## User Impact

Explicit batches and oversized single profiles now return a private host-local `.cpuprofile` path, byte count, window boundaries and node/sample summary. Small single calls remain inline. Twelve or thirty five-second windows retain their complete sanitized timeline with one start/stop; operators retrieve the file from the Gateway host.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing capture owner streams sanitized JSON in chunks with a 64 MiB artifact cap. CPU and heap snapshots share diagnostics-directory reservation and owner-only permissions. Successful files remain until manually removed; failed captures remove partial files. Busy, cancellation and authority behavior remain at the shared capture owner. Requested durations stay capped at 150 seconds; batch destination and 64 MiB free-space checks run before profiler startup. Future graph size cannot be predicted before sampling, so actual file overflow can still fail afterward. No configuration, environment or database change, cache or persistent sampler.

Production growth is 148 lines, chiefly chunked serialization and shared file reservation. The bounded worker-GC summary contract remains unchanged.

## Evidence

Five alternating pairs used a real Node 24.22.1 dist Gateway: 10,800 synthetic sessions, four agents, 4,300 settled runs, 40 registered synthetic plugins, 37 real provider entrypoints imported/retained without registration, five WebSocket clients and four mock-model warmup turns per launch. Distinct deep synthetic call chains create graphs above 33,000 nodes. All ten old captures refused `profile-too-large`; all ten candidate captures returned complete files. Every request used exactly one start/stop, and all twenty concurrent-request busy probes passed.

Medians in milliseconds, five captures per cell; heartbeat stalls are those at least 50 ms and are observed through the RPC reply:

| Capture | Start before → after | Native stop before → after | All stalls before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 12 × 5 s | 562.09 → 528.68 | 120.95 → 121.22 | 678.09 → 637.71 |
| 30 × 5 s | 494.29 → 459.59 | 120.91 → 131.83 | 594.79 → 584.74 |

Twelve-window files were 5,043,976–5,073,931 bytes in 605–610-byte RPC receipts; thirty-window files were 5,238,516–5,325,478 bytes in 859–865-byte receipts. All node/sample counts, sample IDs and signed deltas, timeline hashes, window partitioning, file sizes and 0600 permissions passed. Nine exports had no post-stop-only stall; one had 69.15 ms. Outliers remain: all-stall p95 before/after was 698.87/1,049.01 ms for twelve windows and 661.79/2,186.10 ms for thirty, with extra stalls mostly mid-capture.

This proves preservation and one-start behavior, not a causal startup speedup: the preserved old dist and candidate include intervening main changes, and the host is shared. Same-arm startup spread was 6.15–12.03%. Build-overlapped calibration is excluded from these formal distributions. The fixture is a 268 MB agent DB on macOS/APFS, not a 35 GiB/btrfs qualification. Allocation volume was not measured; raw-profile retention by instrumentation also limits memory conclusions. Source/dist hashes stayed fixed; all synthetic Gateway listeners closed after proof. No production process or data was used.

80 focused CPU/RPC/heap-snapshot/worker-GC tests pass, and the new artifact regression fails on the old implementation. Runtime build, core/test types, focused scripts types, typed lint and formatting pass. Fresh independent Codex reviews are clean. The 112-line test allocation covers full-file preservation, preflight/byte bounds, privacy and cleanup; CPU test bodies total 7.97 seconds including the existing 5.1-second native capture.

`pnpm check:changed` exposed benchmark union/listener defects, fixed with passing scoped reruns. Its remaining 28 production/eight full-tree unused-export signatures reproduce exactly on parent 5ac21026addd, with all twelve failing owners byte-identical. Eleven newly observed main regressions trace to #192552 (eight), #196207 (one) and #196252 (two); the other seventeen retain prior source/caller-migration attribution. These are inherited main regressions, not ignored noise.

Hosted CI also caught this PR's missing wrapper inventory entry; all three failed closure cases pass after the one-line repair. Hosted review caught the benchmark example's missing artifact root; preflight now rejects before any capture and the verifier accepts oversized-single file receipts. Exact-head CI run [42815822040](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42815822040) is green on e3d5e61b988245901cbac580c699bad17d175b19. [ClawSweeper's completed review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196652#issuecomment-6767542056) has zero findings and zero unchecked items on that head. Its advisory RPC-fixture simplification is not a correctness blocker; the inexpensive receipt-forwarding assertion remains at the transport boundary.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Changed sandbox commands freeze the guest throughout workspace discovery, Git capture, and canonical reconciliation. With large workspaces, scanning alone can take seconds while every process in the container is paused.

## User Impact

For provisioned btrfs subvolumes, checkpoint now pauses for the existing native snapshot operation, resumes the guest, and synchronizes canonical state from that captured tree. Command completion still waits for canonical acceptance, preserving read-after-command consistency. Initial recovery and imports retain their existing pause boundaries. No configuration, schema, dependency, or cache is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The checkpoint owner reuses the template backend's native copy primitive under its existing lease. Snapshot fingerprints translate only the proven snapshot device back to the source identity, preserving unchanged probes. Btrfs omits nested subvolumes: the manifest walker detects its inode-2 placeholders before accepting a receipt, then re-pauses under the same lease and uses the existing complete Git capture. Unsupported backends and ordinary directories also retain that path, resuming after durable capture.

The owner removes its private capture after resume and removes leftovers on the next lease. Native removal now repairs inaccessible directories only after a permission failure; it does not follow symlinks or change live source permissions. This is required for snapshots containing ordinary read-only workspace directories.

Snapshot creation can wait for btrfs dirty-data writeback, so this bounds the paused work rather than promising a fixed wall-clock limit. Recursive snapshot cleanup adds work after resume; the native comparison will report that cost explicitly.

## Evidence

The real Podman+btrfs comparison completed all five counterbalanced pairs: 50 measured mutating commands per arm, plus two A/A controls. Every command passed canonical and subsequent guest read checks. The fixture contains 62,000 synthetic files / 1.1 GB, 10,001 session metadata rows, and a 33.65 GiB synthetic database. No production data was used.

| Metric | Parent | Atomic capture |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Pause p50 / p95 / max | 1,619.63 / 1,830.52 / 4,497.19 ms | 194.23 / 241.48 / 269.72 ms |
| Command p50 / p95 / max | 2,374.14 / 2,854.99 / 7,252.07 ms | 3,038.07 / 3,665.20 / 4,221.59 ms |
| Whole-cgroup CPU per command | 3,493.06 ms | 4,472.75 ms |
| Main-isolate allocation per command | 19.22 MB | 20.49 MB |

Median pause improves 88%; median command latency and whole-cgroup CPU increase 28%. A/A pause, command and CPU spread was about 1–1.3%; allocation spread was 9.4%, so no allocation benefit is claimed. All pairs, including the slower first candidate arm, are retained. The 1.36–1.42 s manifest scan runs paused on the parent and unpaused on the candidate in all 50 commands. Native snapshot copy takes 106 ms median; recursive cleanup takes 511 ms after resume. Cleanup explains most of the extra command latency. The maximum guest heartbeat gap falls from 4.43 s to 243 ms.

Timing uses parent `3f17d921f6cc1cf03d52054a74ba3a5e885f5c35` and implementation `64147937916763407221bef031a138af43dd40a8`, with the same frozen harness. Final head `32b8f86f7fc49989f7ae6ab5c1346831b82b5be6` changes only type placement and emits byte-identical JavaScript. The harness runs on a task-owned Linux ARM64 rig with four CPUs and 12 GiB memory, Podman 4.3.1, btrfs 6.2, and Node 26.12.1 for allocation accounting. CPU includes native helpers, Git and the guest; allocation covers only the main V8 isolate. Separate baseline/candidate profiles passed and are excluded from these timing distributions. Final-head native nested-subvolume fallback also passed: two pauses of 180.84 and 5,387.44 ms, complete nested canonical contents, correct next guest read, preserved 0555 source permissions, and no capture artifact. The matching baseline paused 5,947.87 ms; both perform full hashing because the existing fingerprint format rejects mixed-device reuse. This single diagnostic pair is excluded from performance statistics and is not a timing-improvement claim. An oversized 20-command functional run hit its 240-second deadline after at least 17 completed commands; that partial run is retained, and the bounded follow-up changed only the proof driver loop count to one.

- Atomic ordering regressions fail on the prior head because manifest scanning still observes a paused guest. Final affected replay: 17 passed, including seven authority-loss cases. Broader touched-owner proof before the operation-file extraction: 125 passed, two existing platform skips.
- Read-only artifact removal regression fails before the fix with EACCES; all ten native-owner tests now pass. Real Linux btrfs create/copy/remove also passes as UID 501 with no effective capabilities, preserving live nested contents and read-only modes.
- Final `pnpm check:changed --base 3f17d921f6cc1cf03d52054a74ba3a5e885f5c35`: all categories pass except the exact inherited unused-export set below. These are existing main regressions, not passing checks.
- Independent Codex review of the final atomic implementation: scoped-clean through P2, with final source-integrity verification. Prior-head green CI and hosted reviews do not cover this revision; fresh exact-head checks remain required.

Production delta: +199 lines, including snapshot lifecycle/cleanup, nested-subvolume fallback, and source identity preservation. Moving the existing projection operation whole keeps one lifecycle owner within the line cap. Test delta: +245 lines for ordering, recovery, fingerprint reuse, fallback, authority loss, and artifact permissions. Benchmark code is proof-only.

CI on `64147937916763407221bef031a138af43dd40a8` found one introduced static type-import cycle. The repair moves the capture contract into the existing workspace types module and imports it directly. The exact failing guard is red on that head and green after repair; targeted typechecking passes. All six changed files emit byte-identical JavaScript, so the native comparison remains runtime-equivalent. The repair is committed as `32b8f86f7fc49989f7ae6ab5c1346831b82b5be6` and passes fresh Codex review. Final exact-head CI [42832460455](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42832460455) passed. issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

HTTP 400 model-fetch logs omit the provider's error message, making request validation failures indistinguishable from upstream credit exhaustion.

## User Impact

Operators can diagnose HTTP 400 failures from a bounded, credential-redacted `providerError` in the existing model-fetch record. Request-format failures still surface without switching models; ClawRouter's documented depleted-credit exception still tries configured fallbacks without cooling the shared key. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Live native Messages requests for `claude-opus-5-5` and `claude-fable-5-1` both returned `invalid_request_error` with “Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API.” The same failure survived removal of tools, thinking, cache control, and system prompt. No payload incompatibility or classification defect was established; Anthropic also documents HTTP 400 for spend-limit failures.

The fetch owner reuses existing error reading, credential redaction, and message extraction, redacting decoded JSON strings before formatting/truncation on an HTTP 400 response clone. It reads at most 16 KiB under a one-second deadline and caps the logged detail; the SDK retains its original body. Non-JSON/unreadable diagnostics are omitted. issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a fork or a second chat pane synchronously measures a closed composer menu while the new transcript is still being laid out.

## User Impact

Chat composer mounts do less layout work. The capability menu keeps its viewport limit, keyboard navigation, and resize behavior. This candidate is not qualified to land. Auto-merge is off; the remaining WebKit mixed-stream input-delay regression is listed below.

## Why This Change Was Made

The menu is the only consumer of the measured height. Size it on the existing bubbling `overlay-show` event, after lazy content insertion and before native opening/focus. Observe resize only while that panel is actually open. This removes the initial geometry read and subtree MutationObserver without adding a visibility state or cache.

The observer retains at most one panel reference until its next opening or composer disposal. A removed panel no longer matches `:popover-open`.

Related: #183800.

## Evidence

Synthetic production UI, localhost, desktop, 20 rotating base/head/base-control triplets per action; Chromium 4×. These measure renderer work, not provider latency. Acceptance: a useful measured CPU/latency gain, no attributable user-facing regression over 20%, and preserved menu/stream/scroll behavior. A/A and thread CPU distinguish host noise from changes.

| Chromium 4×, median / p95 ms | Base | Head | A/A |

| Fork longest task | 276 / 300.25 | 265.5 / 291.35 | 278.5 / 328.75 |
| Fork style CPU | 195.569 / 216.307 | 152.308 / 166.818 | 197.019 / 227.495 |
| Split-view renderer Task CPU | 1845.471 / 1936.861 | 1828.371 / 1943.848 | 1853.883 / 1996.205 |
| Edit/resubmit renderer Task CPU | 1291.363 / 1477.007 | 1259.289 / 1385.288 | 1256.367 / 1802.852 |

180/180 functional observations passed. Fork Task median improves 4.37%, style CPU 22.12%, median long-task count 5→4. Split-view is effectively flat. Residuals: fork input-frame p95 60.95→64.15 ms (+5.25%; A/A 62.23); edit longest-task p95 217.3→223.5 ms (+2.85%; A/A 295.2). No claim that every metric improves.

- Chromium capability menu: base/head first-open sizing before focus, 36-skill keyboard reachability, open resize, Escape/reopen, zero errors pass; screenshots inspected. WebKit base/head pass the same native first-open, keyboard, resize and reopen checks with zero errors; screenshots inspected.
- Chromium/WebKit 1× action qualification completed: 360/360 observations pass. Chromium 4× streaming qualification completed: 120/120 observations pass. Native-speed streaming and final preservation checks remain pending. Full CI `42168264403` completed: all selected UI jobs passed; the performance budget and aggregate gate failed on the +137 B Chat growth described below. Auto-merge remains off.

Linux CI measured Chat 1,288,321→1,288,458 B and New Session 796,279→796,416 B (+137 B each), with startup unchanged. The Chat growth is PR-owned and exceeds its inherited cap’s 64 B allowance. The campaign’s explicit small-byte allowance for measured CPU wins covers this route growth; a scoped correction to the largest measured Chat head (1,289,143 B on Node 26) is pending. CSS remains unchanged and no CSS cap will change.

Native-speed results, 20 rotating triplets per cell (median / p95 ms):

Reproduce actions with `scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts`, `--steps chat-actions-fork,chat-actions-split-view,chat-actions-edit-resubmit --pairs 20 --network-profiles localhost`, three frozen bundle slots, `--engines chromium --cpu-throttle 4` or `--engines chromium,webkit --cpu-throttle 1`. The 200 ms onset window includes two frames in 11/20 head runs versus 9/20 base and 6/20 control; that threshold count is sensitive to when the second frame starts. Across the first two frames in every run, blocking is 90.05/113.78 → 84.55/103.51 ms (A/A 89.30/126.745), so this does not indicate an added frame. The large-stream per-delta MessageChannel delay p95 rises 1.704→2.965 ms across runs; this includes scheduling delay and is not CPU duration. Native-speed results and any necessary follow-up will remain visible before landing.


## Qualification blocker

The full streaming matrix completed: 120/120 Chromium 4× observations and 240/240 native-speed Chromium/WebKit observations pass functional checks. Ten additional mixed-stream triplets per engine/throttle also pass (90 observations). Every original observation remains in the pooled analysis.
