## Status: rejected performance candidate — do not merge

This PR remains draft with auto-merge off. Published head is `00585700a7f1d204227e6f4a5567211d8dfc6a0e`. The local follow-up through `c82980d7a598449351e314edf8a71a012b1e29c1` is not pushed and also does **not** meet the revised acceptance rule. No landing is requested.

A foreground reply with 200 tools repeatedly scans and rebuilds the turn while the reader types and scrolls. The changes share fixed-snapshot causal bounds, skip unnecessary ownership scans, reuse the run's group inventory, and preserve native reader/end-anchor ownership. The local continuation also merges sorted sibling placements with common bounds in one pass and prevents incoming content from rearming follow between accepted PageUp and native movement.

Related: #194892 and #194751. No background-session optimization, new dependency, timer, or authoritative state owner.

## The 133 ms plateau is real renderer starvation

The producer pump was varied at 20, 50, 133 and 250 ms on matched base/old-head bundles. Base scroll-frame p95 stayed 133.4 ms in every cell; old head varied between 116.7 and 133.3 ms. All eight observations passed. Tool deadlines/output stages stayed fixed; only pump interval changed.

Representative Chromium callback gaps were 133.570/134.225 ms, with recorded renderer tasks occupying 99.49%/99.71%. Paint-start intervals were 133.909/136.656 ms and compositor feedback intervals 131.329/151.577 ms. Incoming-message tasks and Solid flushes fill the gaps. Eight-frame quantization fits missed 60 Hz deadlines; no configured 133 ms timer or exact engine scheduling policy was established. Paint recording and compositor feedback are distinct, and headless feedback is not physical-display proof.

## The mutation storm had a separate trigger

The exact amplified phenotype was not established as inherited: a matched 200-tool/50 ms dwell run produced 442,274 mutations/81 live-row identities on old head versus 143,957/2 on base, with a base final assertion failure. A simple tool-count/output-size threshold was not established.

The old driver returned to exact bottom after reader takeover, re-enabled following, then fought smooth end motion with raw upward offsets. Tail rows were repeatedly evicted and re-admitted. Correcting the driver to native PageUp, settled reader separation, and a sweep from captured reader top removed the loop on both builds: 65,661/64,871 mutations, one live-row identity each, all original exactness/ordering/retention/final checks passed. The ordinary 133 ms stalls remained. The local PageUp fix addresses a separately reproduced native-input rearm gap; it does not relabel the artificial driver conflict as normal scrolling.

## Final loaded qualification

Comparison: base `ef1b8b2ef8637652db627c392909cda37df535fc` versus local `c82980d7a598449351e314edf8a71a012b1e29c1`. Same frozen 46-source corrected harness, six rotated role orders, 20 base/head/identical-base triplets per cell, serial headless execution. Every failed observation was retained. All 180 loaded identities/hashes were independently checked; all 60 candidate runs passed the original 200-result, live-output, ordering, retention and final-visibility assertions.

| Cell | Valid base/head pairs | Scroll-p95 median base → head | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Chromium 1× | 20 | 133.4 → 133.3 ms | −0.075% paired median; no qualifying gain |
| Firefox 1× | 9 | 116.68 → 116.68 ms | No qualifying gain; worse frame tails |
| Chromium 4× | 11 | 250 → 216.7 ms | −13.32% paired median; real improvement, insufficient full acceptance |

Chromium 1× renderer main-thread CPU falls 22.04%, but input-delay p95 median is 13.4→13.7 ms (+4.54% paired), and scroll does not improve meaningfully. Firefox's all-record worst-frame median is 133.49→150 ms; its per-run worst-frame p95 is 183.32→200 ms (identical-base control 150 ms). Firefox's 0/1 ms input-delay values cannot support a meaningful percentage win.

All 11 valid Chromium 4× base/head pairs improve scroll-p95 by 6.68–13.32%, including pairs whose control failed. Only five triplets pass all three roles. Candidate worst frames still reach 433.3 ms, including an unmatched row that would disappear from a passing-only subset. Input-delay medians are 53.55→52.95 ms, with p95 57.2→58.7 ms; no meaningful input win.

Exact failures: Firefox has 11 base and 12 control `foreground-visible-end` timeouts after completion/all 200 results. Chromium 4× has 9 base and 11 control “Event-load PageUp did not settle away from the transcript end” failures before wave two. No candidate failures. Maximum candidate mutation records are 66,150 / 62,744 / 60,432 in Chromium 1× / Firefox / Chromium 4×; no storm recurred.

**Verdict: do not land.** The 4× improvement does not override Firefox tails or supply the required 20 valid paired scroll observations. CPU alone does not qualify. After the loaded cells rejected the candidate, additional unloaded/text acceptance controls were skipped; the first unloaded base startup was interrupted and is not classified as a product failure. WebKit remains unqualified because of the recorded host WindowServer access failure. No claim is made for those unrun controls.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated full-history downloads when repository tools or managed repair acquire missing Git commits in full-history partial clones. Related: #194577.

## User Impact

Missing commit acquisition reuses resident history before comparisons or checkout read trees. Local-only readiness probes preserve their existing failure/delegation contracts. Recovery from corrupt ancestry remains supported. No configuration, cache, schema, or migration is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Git's native promisor lazy fetch does not negotiate common history, so requesting a missing commit can download its complete reachable commit/tree closure. Comparison tools now share negotiated acquisition through the existing Git revision owner. Installer and evidence helpers reach their explicit fetches; local-only probes stay offline.

Managed repair uses a physically present commit from its existing inventory, including inside temporary metadata without refs. It checks only the requested missing IDs afterward and retains one unnegotiated fallback when incomplete ancestry prevents repair. Cancellation, timeout, uncertain cleanup, and authority failures remain terminal.

The `scripts/pr` checkout and hosted-CI owners already received this fix in #194577 and remain unchanged. CI's `ensure-base-commit` deliberately uses depth/deepen recovery, which would be inappropriate for shared full-history worktrees. Existing frozen-tooling inventories already include the shared revision module; no parallel helper or inventory was introduced.

## Evidence

Native regressions fail before the fixes and pass afterward. All 22 repair tests, 255 installer/evidence tests, 202 acquisition-consumer tests, and 14 selected local-probe tests passed (counts overlap). The existing PR checkout regression also passes. Independent review identified the missing-ancestor case; its native regression now verifies the retained fallback. No simulator run is claimed for the one-line iOS Git change.

Five interleaved pairs exercise actual project refresh/repair on an explicitly unshallowed blobless fixture with 80,000 commits and 560,000 trees:

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Received objects | 640,008 | 8 |
| Pack bytes | 34,737,708 | 465 |
| Median / p95 owner wall | 4,629 / 4,951 ms | 457 / 461 ms |
| Median native CPU | 4,490 ms | 50 ms |
| Median native peak RSS | 234.7 MB | 10.6 MB |
| Median exact V8 allocation | 39.8 MB | 35.8 MB |
| Git commands | 17 | 18 |

Five A/A pairs show 0.019% wall drift. JS thread CPU median changes 53.84→54.60 ms; observed p95 changes 54.89→65.57 ms. The extra command verifies only requested IDs to preserve corruption recovery. Native CPU includes the local server; RSS is not cumulative native allocation.

The committed raw-restore workload separately proves 640,009 objects / 34,737,773 bytes → 9 objects / 530 bytes when a negotiated commit fetch precedes restore. Packet traces show the subsequent restore wants only a blob. An isolated single-pair check on actual OpenClaw history confirms 1,014,940 objects / 291,582,168 bytes → 28 objects / 205,372 bytes. These local macOS fixtures establish the mechanism and owner costs, not WAN, database, btrfs, or whole-Gateway latency.

Production growth is 50 lines: one shared acquisition owner replaces the old private resolver, remaining entry points use it, and bounded verification preserves corrupt-ancestry repair. The 148 ratcheted regression lines plus 7 installer-fixture lines prove native negotiation and local-only contracts; the shared scalar remains unchanged. Benchmarks extend existing workloads.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: editing a busy plugin's configuration can repeatedly hold readiness at 503 and delay unrelated runs for 60 seconds, while Settings reports “Saved” even though the previous configuration remains active.

## User Impact

Automatic edits keep the Gateway available and report **Saved; waiting to apply**, with the reason and application condition. Saved values remain visible; the message clears when the active revision catches up. The previous plugin configuration remains active until its work settles or the Gateway restarts. Explicit plugin reload commands retain their existing bounded drain behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Turn custody now follows actual capability resolution/invocation instead of every loaded plugin. Nested resolution records the exact instance it uses, including instances outside the initial registry; the loader owns construction outside turn-use tracking. Hooks and model providers keep advance custody for late finalization/fallback, and overlap-capable plugins preserve their existing admitted-consumer contract.

The automatic reload owner defers before reserving replacement or fencing admission. It records that saved revision's outcome and reuses it for watcher echoes until work and cleanup settle. `config.set` now awaits the same owner receipt as `config.patch`/`config.apply`; deferred application returns an unsuccessful response with additive structured details and the persisted revision. The UI adopts that saved receipt without pretending it applied. Current main already returned generic application failures for hot-applicable patch/apply writes; the reproduced false-success Settings path was `config.set`.

No config options, protocol version bump, SQLite schema changes, or new scan caches. Net production growth is **255 lines**: exact-instance custody, deferred outcome ownership, and API/UI reconciliation replace the blanket self-hold scans. The **357-line** test allocation covers the distinct custody, nonblocking reload, and saved/deferred UI regressions.

The review follow-up also resolves handover from each retained instance’s own declaration, including plugins discovered outside the initial model registry. This removes the old ID-based registry scan and preserves both whole-run yielding and model-step handover.

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateway and Control UI, synthetic plugins and sessions, deterministic local Responses model. Five interleaved A/B runs on the same Node version, with 40 plugins, ten unrelated held turns, one plugin-using held turn, and additional unrelated replacements during deferral:

| Observed behavior | Exact parent | Fixed candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median config.patch receipt | 60,495 ms | 457 ms |
| Median unrelated new-run admission | 61,994 ms | 255 ms |
| Failed readiness probes across held-work windows | 5,243 / 5,366 | 0 / 117 |
| Empty-plugin retained work after unrelated turns | 30 | 0 |
| Median application after plugin holder releases | eventual retry | 1,024 ms |

Several baseline runs repeated the drain and stayed unready for roughly 115–117 seconds. The invoked plugin retains its real work; a fresh actual tool call after application returns the new configuration revision. Owner measurements pinned to `8c4ec655ebad` use 4,000 leases per run, 40 plugins, and 16 resolved tools, with five interleaved pairs and five A/A controls. CPU falls from 62.485 to 55.195 µs/lease (−11.7%), median elapsed time from 50.750 to 43.750 µs (−13.8%), and sampled allocation from 138,520 to 116,423 B/lease (−16.0%). P95 changes from 72.167 to 73.125 µs (+1.3%); no tail-latency improvement is claimed. A/A CPU medians are 58.944/58.258 µs, elapsed time 48.459/48.042 µs, and allocation 138,844/138,162 B. Measurement snapshots and final correctness evidence are recorded separately.

**Full synthetic-scale proof on `8c4ec655ebad`:** real btrfs, a 35.19 GiB agent database, 10,800 sessions, 212,888 transcript events, and 62,002 workspace files; Linux/Node 26.12.1 in a 4-CPU/16-GiB container. Save reports deferred in **580 ms**, unrelated admission takes **696 ms**, and readiness passes **57/57** probes. Releasing the plugin holder applies the edit in **2.7 seconds**; a fresh actual tool invocation returns revision 2. Empty-plugin holds remain zero. Native database integrity checking took about 400 seconds before startup and is excluded from the measured reload window; it was not bypassed. The original retained fixture image was never mounted or modified.

Focused `8c4ec655ebad` source: **55/55** lease/loader tests and **328 passed, one existing skip** across six Gateway suites. UI: **58/58** config owner tests, **32/32** footer/plugin browser tests, **5/5** Settings E2E tests, and the plugin mutation E2E. Regressions fail before the corresponding fixes. `pnpm check:changed` passes typechecks, lint, format and other guards except the exact-parent dead-export findings described below. Codex autoreview of the complete final change (`8c4ec655ebad` against `cdd7ee54ee8d`), including loader-owner context, reports zero actionable P0–P2 findings.

Follow-up proof for `fd1dccd06ce1` (two naming-only test renames followed, with targeted lint passing): **23/23** handover, real nested-loader, inventory, and borrowed-tool tests; **30/30** config-auth, channel lifecycle, and reload-owner tests. The two foreign-instance handover regressions fail before repair. Fresh Codex autoreview of the complete follow-up reports zero actionable P0–P2 findings. Inventory custody is explicitly checked at 2 → 1 → 0, and the channel test requires eventual application within ten seconds while preserving the untouched sibling. The scale, package-upgrade, and real-model artifacts remain pinned to `8c4ec655ebad`; the follow-up changes handover eligibility and consumer tests, with targeted proof for that delta.

The canonical full package build passes, including SDK declarations and the Control UI. The isolated published `2026.11.2` → exact `8c4ec655ebad` package upgrade passes in 437 seconds through the updater, Doctor, restart, readiness, health, and status checks; no fallback repair was needed. The manual-restart upgrade lane does not run live models.

A separate real-model proof on `8c4ec655ebad` uses one `gpt-4.1-mini` turn with two successful Responses requests. The model invokes the actual plugin; its second request is held across the config edit. The deferred receipt takes **526 ms**, unrelated admission **191 ms**, and readiness passes **18/18** probes. Releasing the holder applies the edit in **2.25 seconds**, and a subsequent actual tool call verifies revision 2. Unrelated and post-application model responses remain deterministic. This supplements the synthetic timing fixture rather than relabeling it as real-model traffic.

<details>
<summary>Inherited checks and investigated local failure</summary>

The full build's nonfatal UI budget report flags largest JS gzip (551.5 KiB versus 551.3 KiB), chat boot (1,269.5 versus 1,268.3 KiB), and new boot (784.9 versus 784.5 KiB). These warnings are not described as passing budgets or all classified inherited; no budget baseline was changed.

The exact parent reproduces the same 32 production / 10 full-tree unused exports; the final scan introduces none. Per-symbol history attribution includes #192552, #196207, #196252, #191326, #139911, #190205, #132716, #129184, #190544, #191513, #194455, #130634, #103537, #121929, #151777, and direct commit `a7436c8b4a93`. These remain main regressions, not passing checks.

The test-line ratchet remains 293 lines over its absolute ceiling on both the exact parent and candidate. This change allocates exactly its own 357-line increase. Existing debt comes from #194996 (+71), #188748 (+223), and #194429 (−1); no baseline exception or unrelated budget increase was added.

CI run 42793106430 tested merge `cb60a5886b50` with main parent `8c9a5cf064ff`. Three formatter failures reproduce on that exact main parent and were introduced by #196501 (`09723cdcad18`); the original branch parent predates them. Two worker context-engine failures also reproduce on that exact main parent, while all three tests pass on #196337’s exact predecessor (`54e0bc0c2132`). Commit `d7aaafe92edf` moves input persistence after prompt/context assembly, causing the missing transcript fences. These are recorded as main regressions requiring owner repair; the worker assertions remain unchanged.

Final CI run **42800384505**, attempt 1, tested head `fd1dccd06ce18` in merge `50f53af9fff1` over exact main `3a1a9cf0de3a`. All UI and UI E2E shards, type/lint/guards, PostgreSQL, and security-fast pass. The only failed test shard contains those same two worker fence cases: they reproduce on that exact main parent (two failures, one pass), with the causal predecessor proof above. The old formatting failure is fixed on newer main by `5f27b11f9f135`; final docs CI passes. The scoped inherited-failure landing exception retains CI as failed and leaves the worker assertions intact. Final-head ClawSweeper re-review has **zero open items and zero findings**.

An earlier run under concurrent workload observed `recovering` instead of `reloading` in the separate-registry memory recovery case. Narrow baseline/candidate replays and the final six-suite run pass. A full exact-parent run independently fails the sibling early-checkpoint recovery case at the same phase assertion. The fixture/assertion originated in #167756; that establishes provenance, not the causal introduction of an intermittent defect. The original candidate-only failure remains investigated but unattributed; a passing replay is not claimed as a fix or grounds for an inherited-CI waiver.

</details>

![Before: Settings reports Saved while the previous plugin configuration still serves](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2999f63-e3a9-4d8b-a13b-9fde6493a963)

![After: Settings preserves the saved values and explains why application is deferred](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/60ace732-adc3-432c-ba75-6260549220c1)

![After the retained work finishes: the new revision applies and the deferred notice clears](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/800b47a2-e148-4768-a3e1-aed1b6298cec)

Fixes Tab completing `/think` again instead of the selected thinking level after the user selects its trailing space. This broke all three viewport cases in scheduled CI run [42769178432](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42769178432).

Users can keep a thinking level highlighted while selecting text in the argument area, then complete it with Tab and submit it. Leading commands typed before pasted text keep their existing completion behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The slash-menu owner now distinguishes a caret inside the command token from a selection extending into its arguments. The latter retains the argument picker and its selection. The existing composer regression also checks selection followed by a pending catalog refresh; no new state or timing workaround is introduced.

## Evidence

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening Activity fetched and compiled most of Chat's presentation code before Activity was ready, although that route did not execute it.

## User Impact

Activity becomes ready sooner in the measured desktop and mobile fixtures. Its empty, loaded, live-tab and media presentation stays unchanged. Startup bytes and CSS request counts do not increase.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared media resource owner also imported message normalization and Markdown. Move its unchanged projection functions and their translations to a separate module, migrate every projection caller, and keep policy/resource lifetime in the original owner. Group five small cross-route leaves in the existing deferred-support chunk; this also cuts the independent client-kind label edge into Chat presentation. Media keeps its existing deferred renderer. There is no new chunk, cache, state, renderer or dependency.

Production LOC across the affected files: **3,595 → 3,605 (+10)**. The extra lines are module imports and chunk cases. Solid refactor audit: no added signals, effects, listeners, cleanup, DOM queries, owner APIs or manual loaders.

## Evidence

The acceptance rule was recorded before timing: 20 rotated base/head/base triplets per engine and viewport, Firefox Activity at least 5% faster beyond A/A variation, no Chromium readiness/task-CPU regression, no Chat cold-boot regression at 100 ms RTT or warm-boot regression, identical visuals and no new CSS requests. No size ceiling changes.

### First-ready coverage

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mobile session switching still measured the source pane after it became visually hidden. The Region's queued width read published geometry and woke transcript consumers; mobile fade painting also read closed sheets and hidden panes.

## User Impact

Reduces wasted layout during mobile conversation switches while preserving reader position, focus, and mobile sheet appearance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bind both geometry owners to the pane's existing visual presentation fact. Hiding cancels queued work and suppresses reads/publications; revealing schedules a fresh measurement while preserving the last visible width comparison. The Region geometry implementation moves into a local leaf because the renderer is at its existing line limit. There is no new state owner, cache, dependency, CSS, or lazy-boundary change.

## Evidence

Baseline: `2dff6d2107d4e6e3252e1672340ca6decf511e22`. Candidate: `42f2b0e47762488113d4144efa15d7a5905dc39a`. Production bundles; two retained 400-message sessions; mobile 390×844. Twenty rotated base/candidate/base triplets, fresh browser per observation, with A/A control. Chromium 156.0.8078.4 on a four-CPU, 16.6 GB Linux Testbox; 1-minute host load 0.89–2.0. All 60 observations passed.

| Measurement | Base | Candidate | A/A control |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Layout count, every round trip | 4 | 2 | 4 |
| Layout CPU, median / p95 | 1.823 / 2.025 ms | 0.985 / 1.165 ms | 1.801 / 2.022 ms |
| Style CPU, median / p95 | 32.368 / 35.958 ms | 27.526 / 31.404 ms | 32.328 / 35.261 ms |
| Task CPU, median / p95 | 184.395 / 207.566 ms | 181.643 / 201.142 ms | 185.500 / 204.530 ms |
| Application readiness, median / p95 | 851.7 / 861.6 ms | 853.8 / 872.6 ms | 807.55 / 857.4 ms |

Paired median deltas: layouts −50% (A/A 0%); layout CPU −44.33% (A/A −0.42%); style CPU −16.49% (A/A −0.99%); task CPU −5.06% (A/A −0.49%). Readiness paired median −0.20% (A/A −0.23%); its paired p95 spread is +6.28% versus A/A +8.46%. The small absolute readiness movement is within the control spread.

A separate 20-triplet native trace plus read-boundary diagnostic confirms **two hidden forced layouts on every base/control round trip and zero on every candidate round trip** (100% reduction; A/A 0%). Each removed Layout span is inside the hidden Region rectangle getter. All 60 traced observations pass, with no dropped probe events. Traced timings are excluded from the performance table.

Firefox 157.0 sibling: all 60 observations passed. Application readiness median/p95 1243/1369 → 1253.5/1356 ms; A/A 1235/1430 ms. Paired median +0.55% versus A/A −0.16%; no CPU claims from Firefox. Its source diagnostic reports hidden Region publications 4→0, fade rectangle reads 4→0, and all hidden reads 46→26, with no dropped diagnostic events.

A targeted production round trip with a hidden resize preserves the same pane, history request count, reader key and exact reader offset. Closing the sheet returns focus inside the active pane. Settled reveal, reader-return, and open-sheet screenshots are byte-identical across base, candidate, and control; inspected captures use synthetic data only.

| Other validation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Two touched test files | 25/25 pass; the two new regressions fail against base |
| UI typecheck, scoped lint, format, controller guard | Pass |
| Startup JS gzip / CSS requests | 91,889 B → 91,889 B; 1 → 1 |
| Chat boot JS gzip | 1,300,472 B → 1,300,408 B (−64 B) |
| Strict performance comparison | No new violation; base and head both retain the existing 7 B total-CSS-raw excess; no ceiling changes |
| Production Knip | Base and head report the same three unlisted binaries: taskkill.exe and two btrfs uses in untouched scripts. No new finding. |
| WebKit | Both initial and closeout headless launch smokes timed out before page creation; no WebKit behavior claim. Owned processes exited. |
| Independent review | No actionable P0–P2 finding |

Commands: `pnpm tsgo:ui`; the two touched test files with `--maxWorkers=1`; `pnpm ui:build` and `pnpm ui:check-performance --base-dist <base-bundle> --json`; `pnpm deadcode:knip`; `scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts --steps session-switch --pairs 20 --fresh-browser --engines chromium --viewport mobile --bundle-dir <base> --compare-bundle-dir <head> --control-bundle-dir <base>`. Repeated the engine workload with Firefox. Local Chromium headless shell hangs in native canvas `clearRect()` on a blank document, so Chromium proof ran on Testbox [42793117058](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42793117058).

Production LOC 2,687→2,745 (+58); tests 724→806 (+82). Solid audit: no change in effect, render-effect, untrack, direct listener/query, flush, owner-API or cleanup counts (all zero in the touched production files); four existing dynamic imports remain four. The two added regressions protect cancellation/publication and fade refresh, respectively.

### Inspected before/after

| State | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retained pane reveal | ![Base retained pane](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2c9b0b34-16bc-4451-871e-bd7f8191c0b4) | ![Candidate retained pane](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51808746-5ebf-41fe-894c-7e47f41fafa9) |
| Reopened mobile sheet | ![Base mobile sheet](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c903a7a-5f8b-4038-a694-9d586ffcab4f) | ![Candidate mobile sheet](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/caa9e407-32e5-466c-9191-e751b5e2b6d8) |
